label: S0478
statement:
statement: Layerwise residual lower bound for exact streaming recognition. Let N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and 0<=t<=N. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and let r_t be the number of distinct residual sets. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in F exactly must reach at least r_t distinct states after t bits, hence needs at least ceil(log2 r_t) state bits (zero if r_t=1). Proof: If p and q have different residuals but lead to the same state, choose u in their symmetric difference. Starting from that shared state, the machine's deterministic run on u gives the same answer for pu and qu. Exactly one lies in F, a contradiction. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states; a B-bit state has at most 2^B possibilities, so 2^B>=r_t. This applies to EXT_{n,s} for F equal to the set of size-at-most-s circuit truth tables in the fixed order, but does not bound transition gate cost or give a simulation from arbitrary H_C.
scope: All finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N and all layers t, for deterministic exact one-pass recognition; applies to EXT prefix membership under its fixed truth-table ordering.

label: S0479
statement:
statement: Residual quotient automaton for a finite language. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pu in F}. Make one state for each distinct residual set at each layer, keeping layers distinct even if their sets coincide. From state R(p) at layer t, on bit b transition to R(pb) at layer t+1. This transition is well-defined: if R(p)=R(q) for |p|=|q|=t, then for every suffix u of length N-t-1, u is in R(pb) exactly when bu is in R(p), and likewise for q; hence R(pb)=R(qb). Declare the layer-N state accepting exactly when its residual contains the empty string. The resulting deterministic layered automaton recognizes F exactly and has r_t states at layer t, where r_t is the number of distinct residuals there. Combined with the distinguishability argument in S0478, this proves that r_t is the minimum possible number of states at layer t for any exact deterministic streaming recognizer. The construction does not bound the cost of computing its transitions from H_C or the total description size as a function of n and s.
scope: Every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass recognition with position known to the machine. State counts are per layer; no transition-complexity assertion.

structure.evidence: Direct construction and proof: successor residuals are determined solely by the current residual and next bit, because R(pb)={u: bu in R(p)}. Acceptance at the final layer is membership of the empty suffix. No computation is needed for this general finite-language lemma.

This transition is well-defined: if R(p)=R(q) for |p|=|q|=t, then for every suffix u of length N-t-1, u is in R(pb) exactly when bu is in R(p), and likewise for q; hence R(pb)=R(qb). Declare the layer-N state accepting exactly when its residual contains the empty string. The resulting deterministic layered automaton recognizes F exactly and has r_t states at layer t, where r_t is the number of distinct residuals there. Combined with the distinguishability argument in S0478, this proves that r_t is the minimum possible number of states at layer t for any exact deterministic streaming recognizer. The construction does not bound the cost of computing its transitions from H_C or the total description size as a function of n and s.
scope: Every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass recognition with position known to the machine. State counts are per layer; no transition-complexity assertion.

label: S0480
statement:
statement: Residual-language quotient lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t≤N and prefix p∈{0,1}^t, define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pu∈F}. In any deterministic layered streaming automaton that accepts exactly F, two length-t prefixes with different residual sets must lead to different states. Conversely, the residual sets at each layer form a deterministic layered automaton with transitions R ↦ {v∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv∈R} on input bit b, initial state R_empty=F, and acceptance at layer N iff the empty string belongs to R. Thus the minimum number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residual sets {R_p:|p|=t}. Proof: If R_p≠R_q, choose u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pu,qu is in F. If the automaton had the same state after p and q, its deterministic processing of the same suffix u would have the same acceptance outcome, contradiction. For the converse, after prefix p the stored state R_p updates on bit b to R_pb by the definition of residual and concatenation; induction on prefix length gives exactness, and final acceptance is exactly membership in F.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N and deterministic layered streaming automata reading exactly N bits. It characterizes minimum state width layer by layer; it gives no bound on transition circuit cost or construction time, and no simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0481
statement:
statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound for EXT streaming states. Fix n,s and let L=EXT_{n,s} be the language of prefixes of truth tables of Boolean functions computable by size-at-most-s circuits, with the truth-table order fixed. For a prefix p, define R_p={z: pz is a prefix of a truth table in Im(Eval)}. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in L after every prefix and whose future behavior depends only on its current state must assign different states to p and q whenever R_p != R_q. Consequently it has at least |{R_p : p is a prefix}| states and at least ceil(log2 |{R_p : p is a prefix}|) state bits.
proof: Suppose R_p != R_q. Choose a suffix z in their symmetric difference; without loss of generality z is in R_p and not R_q. By definition, pz is a prefix of some size-at-most-s circuit truth table, whereas qz is not. If the machine reached the same state after p and q, then feeding the identical suffix z would produce the same future state sequence and the same final membership answer on both inputs, contradicting that one concatenation is in L and the other is not. Thus distinct residual sets require distinct states. The state-count and bit-count bounds follow by counting these pairwise distinguishable residual sets.
scope: All finite truth-table lengths N=2^n, all s>=0, fixed truth-table order, deterministic machines whose state completely determines future transitions and acceptance. This proves a state-width requirement only; it gives no transition-cost lower bound and no simulation of an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

label: S0482
statement:
statement: Equal-level residual distinguishability for EXT. Fix n,s, N=2^n, a truth-table order, and a level t in {0,...,N}. Let L=EXT_{n,s} be the set of prefixes of truth tables of functions computable by circuits of size at most s. For each length-t prefix p define R_{p,t}={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is a full truth table of a function computable by a size-at-most-s circuit}. Any deterministic streaming machine that, after reading all N bits, decides whether the full string is such a circuit truth table must reach distinct states after any two length-t prefixes p,q with R_{p,t} != R_{q,t}. Hence it has at least |{R_{p,t}:p in {0,1}^t}| states at level t, and at least ceil(log2 |{R_{p,t}:p in {0,1}^t}|) state bits at that level.
proof: If R_{p,t} and R_{q,t} differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Both prefixes have length t, so the same suffix z has length N-t and places both computations at the same subsequent input positions. Exactly one of pz and qz is a truth table in the target family. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism implies that processing the identical suffix z leads to the same final state and output, contradicting correctness on those two full strings. Thus distinct residual sets force distinct level-t states. Counting these residual sets yields the state and bit lower bounds.
scope: Every fixed n,s, truth-table order, and level t. The language decision is on complete N-bit truth tables; this statement yields only a state-width lower bound at each level, not transition-cost bounds or a simulation/lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

label: S0484
statement:
statement: Candidate-vector transition accounting for EXT. Fix a finite indexed list C_1,...,C_K of length-N candidate truth tables and a stream position t. Let z_i indicate whether candidate i matches the prefix of length t, and let c_i=[C_i(t)=b] be supplied position-dependent constants for the next input bit b. Then the exact next state is z'_i=z_i AND c_i for every i. Thus each next-state coordinate is either the input wire z_i or the constant 0, so the transition map requires zero fan-in-two Boolean gates when wires and hardwired constants are free. The separate acceptance readout OR_i z_i takes K-1 fan-in-two OR gates for K>=1 (zero gates for K=1). Proof: Candidate i matches the extended prefix exactly when it matched the previous prefix and its bit at position t equals b, which is precisely z_i AND c_i. Since c_i is fixed for the transition, this expression is z_i when c_i=1 and 0 when c_i=0. A binary OR tree combines K bits in K-1 gates. This is an exact cost decomposition for the explicit candidate-vector representation; it gives no polynomial-in-s bound when K is exponential in the circuit-description length and no simulation through arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
scope: All finite candidate lists, fixed truth-table orders, and positions, with position-dependent comparison constants supplied; the transition gate count excludes state storage and readout, which is separately K-1 gates.

label: S0500
statement: For D>=1, E>=1, m=ceil(log2 D), r=ceil(log2 E), and deterministic maps delta_0,delta_1 from a D-element state set X to an E-element set Y, the encoded transition function on valid state codes and one input bit has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size at most r(2Dm+2D+m). Proof: For each output coordinate enumerate the t<=2D valid pairs (x,b) yielding output 1. Each minterm uses at most m AND gates on m+1 literals; if t>0 the OR costs t-1 gates; shared input negations cost at most m+1. The total is at most mt+(t-1)+(m+1)<=2Dm+2D+m. An empty disjunction is constant 0. Repeating over r coordinates proves the claim. This bound repairs the incorrect inequality in S0431.

label: S0502
statement: statement: LEMMA (EXT as existential projection of a decision circuit). Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} decide membership in a family F of N-bit strings, and let EXT_H(p)=1 iff some member of F extends prefix p. For every prefix p of length t, EXT_H(p)=OR_{u in {0,1}^{N-t}} H(pu). For b in {0,1} and t<N, EXT_H(pb)=OR_{u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}} H(pbu). Proof: By the definition of concatenation, the strings extending p are exactly the pu with |u|=N-t; membership in F is exactly H(pu)=1. The same argument applies after fixing next bit b. Thus the exact next-state values are existential projections of H, with the explicit disjunction using 2^(N-t) and 2^(N-t-1) evaluations respectively. This gives no bounded-call or gate-cost-preserving reduction for arbitrary H.

label: S0503
statement: statement: LEMMA (EXT prefix has a short verifiable circuit witness). Fix n,s and an explicit binary encoding of fan-in-two Boolean circuits with at most s gates, where each gate record uses O(log(n+s)) bits and the output wire is specified in the description. Let N=2^n. For each t in {0,...,N}, define EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 for p in {0,1}^t iff there exists a valid description d of at most L=O(s log(n+s)) bits whose circuit C_d agrees with p on the first t inputs in the fixed truth-table order. Then EXT_{n,s}(p) is in NP with witness length at most L+O(1) and deterministic verification time O(t(s+n)+L), in a standard gate-list encoding. Proof: Guess d, reject if it is not a valid circuit description of the stated size, then for each of the t input strings evaluate the s-gate circuit in topological order and compare its output with the corresponding bit of p. One circuit evaluation costs O(s+n) including input access under the stated encoding, so all comparisons cost O(t(s+n)); description validation and parsing cost O(L). The verifier accepts exactly when a size-at-most-s circuit has the required prefix, which is exactly the defining existential condition. Scope: this proves a nondeterministic upper bound and an explicit certificate/checking cost only; it gives no deterministic transition algorithm, no compression of the candidate set, and no hardness lower bound.

statement: statement: LEMMA (listed-family EXT update). Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n inputs, and let E_j be their truth tables in a fixed order. For a prefix p of length t<2^n, define A={j: E_j[0..t-1]=p}. Then EXT_F(p0)=OR_{j in A}[E_j[t]=0] and EXT_F(p1)=OR_{j in A}[E_j[t]=1]. Proof: A candidate extends p followed by b exactly when it agrees with p and its next output is b; existential quantification over F is therefore the displayed OR. Given circuit descriptions, both bits have real fan-in-two circuits of size O(M(t+1)(s+n)): evaluate each candidate on the first t inputs and input t, test the t prefix bits, combine each test with the next output, then OR over candidates. This construction is exact and explicit. Scope: it gives an enumeration upper bound only; it does not bound M polynomially or implement the update from an arbitrary fixed H_C.

label: S0505
statement:
statement: LEMMA (explicit-family streaming update). Let F=(C_1,...,C_d) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. At stream position i, represent the live candidates by a vector a in {0,1}^d, where a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with all previously read truth-table bits. On reading b, set a'_j=a_j AND (b iff C_j(i)=1), and increment i. This is exact: by induction on the number of read bits, a'_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the entire extended prefix. A transition can be implemented by evaluating each C_j on the binary encoding of i and ANDing its equality-to-b test with a_j; with straightforward fan-in-two circuitry this costs O(d(s+n)) gates, including the index increment. Thus explicit candidate tracking is polynomial when d,s,n are polynomially bounded, but the lemma gives no polynomial bound when d is the full circuit-description count.

statement: LEMMA (finite residual update). Let N=2^n and let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t≤N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pz∈F}. For t<N and b∈{0,1}, R_{pb}={u∈{0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu∈R_p}. Consequently, R_p is nonempty iff p has an extension in F, and updating the residual after reading b is exactly taking the b-slice of R_p. Proof: For each u of length N−t−1, u∈R_{pb} iff pbu∈F by definition of R_{pb}; this holds iff bu∈R_p by definition of R_p; hence the sets are equal. Nonemptiness follows directly from the definition. This is an exact information-level update identity for every finite family F; it gives no bound on the cost of representing or computing the slice for EXT_{n,s} or from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-list update circuit). Fix n≥1, a finite list C_1,…,C_M of n-input Boolean circuits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and enumerate inputs as x_t=bin_n(t) for 0≤t<2^n. A state is (t,a_1,…,a_M), where a_j=1 iff C_j agrees with the streamed prefix of length t. There is a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT transition circuit taking (t,a_1,…,a_M,b) to (t+1,a'_1,…,a'_M), with wraparound at t=2^n−1, of size O(n+M(s+1)). It satisfies a'_j=a_j∧[C_j(x_t)=b] for every valid state. Proof: wire the n bits of t as x_t; evaluate each hardwired C_j using at most s gates; compare its output with b using O(1) gates and AND with a_j. Increment t modulo 2^n using O(n) gates. Each a'_j is 1 exactly when C_j agreed on the prior t positions and agrees at position t. Induction from (0,1,…,1) proves the invariant. This upper bound concerns only the explicit-list representation; it does not bound M polynomially in n,s or give a lower bound for arbitrary encodings or H_C.

label: S0510
statement: LEMMA (position-specific candidate-mask update). Let C_1,...,C_K be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits with truth tables E_j in a fixed order. For each position t, define the hardwired mask m_t in {0,1}^K by (m_t)_j=E_j[t]. Given the candidate bitset x in {0,1}^K and next streamed bit b, define x'_j=x_j AND (b iff (m_t)_j). This transition is correct for filtering the candidates consistent with the prefix extended by b, and has a fan-in-two AND/NOT circuit of at most K+1 gates for each fixed t. Proof: If (m_t)_j=1, set x'_j=x_j AND b; otherwise set x'_j=x_j AND NOT b. Share NOT b across coordinates, so the gate count is at most K+1. Coordinate j survives exactly when it was previously present and its truth-table bit at t equals b. statement: LEMMA (residual-width bound for a finite candidate family). Let F be a nonempty family of K distinct binary strings of length N. For 0<=t<=N, for each length-t prefix u define R_u={v in {0,1}^{N-t}: uv in F}; let q_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_u. Then q_t <= min(K, 2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Proof: There are at most 2^t prefixes u, hence at most 2^t residuals. Every nonempty residual contains at least one suffix v from a member uv of F; choosing one such member for each distinct residual gives distinct members of F, since distinct residual sets cannot be witnessed by the same member's prefix group. Thus q_t<=K. Finally each residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) possible suffixes, so there are at most 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residual sets. Taking all three bounds proves the claim. Consequence: the exact level-t residual automaton can store its active state in one-hot form using q_t bits (plus a rejecting sink if desired); its binary transition at that level can be implemented by routing each source state/input pair to the unique next residual or sink, with O(q_t) fan-in-two gates. This sharpens the candidate-list representation to a bound controlled by distinct residuals, but q_t can still be as large as K and the result does not give a polynomial-in-(s,n) update for EXT_{n,s} or arbitrary MCSP circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (explicit-list transition circuit). Let C={C_1,...,C_M} be a fixed finite list of Boolean circuits with truth tables E_i in {0,1}^N. At position t<N, encode a candidate subset A by x in {0,1}^M, where x_i=1 iff C_i's truth table agrees with the streamed prefix so far. The exact update on streamed bit b is y_i=x_i AND [E_i[t]=b] for each i. This vector map has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most M+1 gates, with constants allowed. Proof: The values E_i[t] are fixed constants. If E_i[t]=b, output y_i=x_i (wire); otherwise y_i=0 (constant). If the update is required as a uniform circuit receiving b and the column E[t] as fixed data, compute NOT b once and each output by one AND gate with b or NOT b, for at most M+1 gates. In either convention, y encodes exactly the candidates agreeing with the extended prefix, by the defining conjunction of prior agreement and agreement at position t. statement: statement: LEMMA (explicit circuit-list size bound). Fix n>=1 and s>=0. In the model of topologically ordered circuits with n designated input wires, at most s gates each chosen from AND, OR, NOT (with fan-in at most two), and one designated output wire, the number M of circuit descriptions is at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s. Proof: For a circuit with exactly j gates, each gate has at most 3(n+s)^2 choices: one of three gate types and an ordered pair of sources among at most n+s available wires (this overcounts unary NOT gates and allows unused later wires, so is an upper bound). The output has at most n+s choices. Thus there are at most (n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^j descriptions with j gates. Summing j=0,...,s and using (3(n+s)^2)^j <= (3(n+s)^2)^s gives the stated bound. Consequently the explicit incidence-vector candidate representation has an update circuit of size at most M+1, hence at most (s+1)(n+s)(3(n+s)^2)^s+1. This quantifies the representation-specific cost and does not establish a polynomial update bound or a lower bound for other representations.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (right-residual state characterization). Let A be a finite set of binary strings of common length N, let L=Pref(A), and for each prefix p let L_p={u: pu is in L}. In any deterministic streaming automaton recognizing L, prefixes p and q that reach the same state have L_p=L_q. Conversely, the distinct sets L_p form the states of a deterministic automaton recognizing L, with transition from L_p on bit b to L_{pb}; the empty residual is a rejecting sink. Thus the minimum number of states equals the number of distinct right residuals among prefixes, including the empty residual if it occurs.
derivation: If p and q reach the same deterministic state, every continuation u produces the same acceptance result after p and q. Since acceptance after p followed by u is exactly the predicate pu∈L, this implies L_p=L_q. Therefore prefixes with distinct residuals must reach distinct states. Conversely, define states to be the distinct residuals L_p and define δ(L_p,b)={u:bu∈L_p}. By definition this set is L_{pb}, so the transition is well-defined on residuals: if L_p=L_q, then {u:bu∈L_p}={u:bu∈L_q}. Declare a residual accepting iff it contains the empty string. Starting from L_ε, induction on the streamed prefix shows the current state is exactly L_p; hence the automaton recognizes L. The empty residual transitions to itself and is rejecting. The lower and upper bounds on the state count coincide.

statement: LEMMA (prefix residual state-count bound). Let A be a finite nonempty subset of {0,1}^N with |A|=M, and let L=Pref(A). The minimal deterministic automaton for L has at most 1+sum_{k=0}^N min(2^k,M) states.
derivation: For each k in 0..N, a nonempty right residual L_p arises only from a length-k prefix p of some word in A. There are at most 2^k such prefixes. There are also at most M such prefixes because distinct length-k prefixes have disjoint sets of descendant words in A, each nonempty. Hence there are at most min(2^k,M) nonempty residuals arising at depth k. Summing these upper bounds over depths may overcount residuals shared across depths, which is harmless. There is at most one additional empty residual. By the right-residual characterization, the number of distinct residuals bounds the minimal automaton state count.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (explicit-family EXT update circuit). Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be a fixed list of Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates, and let the streamed bits be the truth table of length 2^n in binary input order. There is a deterministic exact EXT-prefix update representation using n+M state bits and at most O(n+M(s+1)) fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates per update. The state stores the next input index i in n bits and a candidate mask a in M bits. On next bit b, evaluate each C_j at i, then set a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(i)=b], and increment i modulo 2^n. After k updates, a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with all k streamed bits. Thus the mask is nonempty exactly when the prefix has a completion in the listed family. Proof: Initially i=0 and all candidates are live. At each update, the equality test removes precisely the candidates whose next truth-table bit differs from b; incrementing i selects the next truth-table position. Induction on k proves the invariant. Each circuit evaluation costs O(s), each comparison and mask update O(1), and the binary counter increment costs O(n), giving the stated bound. This is an explicit-family bound; M may be exponential, so it does not bound the implicit family of all size-s circuits by poly(s,n).
scope: Finite explicitly listed circuit families; exact fan-in-two Boolean update circuits; no claim about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits or compact implicit-family updates.

statement: LEMMA (exact residual-state characterization for finite prefix languages). Let L be a finite set of binary strings, and for every prefix p define R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz is a prefix of some word in L}. Any deterministic streaming machine whose state after reading p determines, for every suffix z, whether pz is a prefix of a word in L must place p and q in different states whenever R_p != R_q. Conversely, assigning one state to each distinct set R_p (and a rejecting sink for strings that cease to be prefixes) gives a deterministic machine recognizing the prefix language of L. Hence the minimum number of states is exactly the number of distinct residual sets, with the sink included when needed. Proof: If R_p != R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. The required answers after p and q on continuation z differ. A deterministic machine in the same state after p and q would, on the same continuation z, produce the same answer, contradiction. For the converse, after reading bit b from residual R_p, the residual becomes R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}; this is determined by R_p and b. If R_p is empty, transition to the sink. Acceptance is determined by whether the empty suffix belongs to the residual. This proves the transition and acceptance rules are well-defined. Applied to L=Im(Eval) for size-at-most-s circuits, these residuals are precisely the completion sets relevant to EXT. This characterizes required information but asserts no bound on real-gate transition cost.

statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual distinguishability at a fixed depth). Let L be a finite set of binary words, and let p and q be words of the same length t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{*: |z|=N-t and pz in L}, where N is the common word length of L}; define R_q analogously. In every deterministic automaton that accepts exactly L, if R_p != R_q then the states reached after p and q are distinct. Proof: Since the sets differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pz and qz belongs to L. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would make the automaton's result after reading the common suffix z identical from both states, contradicting that exactly one word is accepted. Consequently, the number of states reached by length-t prefixes is at least the number of distinct residual sets R_p at that depth. This applies to EXT for any finite family of equal-length truth tables, with L equal to that family. It gives an information-state lower bound only; it does not bound transition gate cost or connect EXT to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
evidence: Direct proof by symmetric-difference suffix: unequal residual sets provide a suffix accepted after exactly one of the two equal-length prefixes. Determinism forces identical continuations from a shared state, so those prefixes cannot share a state.

After t truth-table bits p_0,...,p_{t-1}, encode the consistent candidates by a mask u in {0,1}^M, where u_j=1 iff C_j(a_i)=p_i for every i<t. Given the next input a_t and bit b, the updated mask is u'_j = u_j AND [C_j(a_t)=b]. This transition has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size O(M(s+n)), and the new mask is exactly the candidate set consistent with the extended prefix. Proof: For each j, evaluate C_j at a_t in topological order, using at most s gates plus O(n) input handling. Compare its output to b using O(1) gates, then AND the equality bit with u_j. Doing this for all M candidates costs O(M(s+n)) gates. The formula for u'_j is exactly the conjunction of prior consistency and agreement at position t, so induction on t proves the mask invariant and exactness. Scope: D is explicitly listed and its descriptions are available to the transition circuit. The bound is linear in M, so it need not be polynomial in s when D is the full size-s circuit class. This does not establish a representation through an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
evidence: Direct construction and induction: evaluate each candidate on the current input, compare with b, and retain it exactly when its prior mask bit is 1 and the output matches. This yields O(M(s+n)) fan-in-two gates and makes the candidate-count dependence explicit.

statement: LEMMA (quotient transition). Let F be a finite set of Boolean strings, all of length N. For each prefix p of length t≤N, define R(p)={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pz∈F}. Define p≈q (necessarily equal lengths) iff R(p)=R(q). Then for every t<N and b∈{0,1}, R(pb)={w∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bw∈R(p)}. Consequently p≈q implies pb≈qb for each b, so the residual equivalence classes at each depth have well-defined transitions under appending a bit. Proof: For any w of length N−t−1, w∈R(pb) iff pbw∈F iff bw∈R(p), giving the set identity. If R(p)=R(q), filtering both sets by strings beginning with b and deleting that first bit gives identical sets R(pb)=R(qb). This proves transition well-definedness for the minimal residual quotient, including empty residuals. Scope: finite equal-length string family; says nothing about the number of quotient states, how to construct a quotient state from a compact circuit description, or the real-gate cost of its transition.

label: S0530
statement: LEMMA (residual quotient width). Let F be a finite family of K Boolean strings of common length N. At depth t, 0<=t<=N, partition all length-t prefixes by equality of their residual sets R(p)={z: pz in F}. The number of equivalence classes is at most min(2^t,K)+1. Proof: Every nonempty residual class contains a prefix p occurring as the length-t prefix of at least one word in F. Distinct such prefixes number at most 2^t and at most K, so there are at most min(2^t,K) distinct nonempty residual sets. All prefixes with empty residual, if any, belong to a single additional class. Thus the total is at most min(2^t,K)+1. At t=0 the bound remains valid (there is only one prefix, and hence at most one class). Scope: finite equal-length string families; this is a width bound in terms of |F| and does not bound the transition circuit cost from a compact representation of F.

statement: LEMMA (enumerated-candidate update circuit). Fix n,s and an explicitly listed set C of D Boolean circuits on n inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Maintain a D-bit vector a, with a_C=1 exactly when candidate C agrees with all truth-table prefix bits seen so far, and let i be the address of the next row. On receiving bit b, update a'_C = a_C AND (b iff C(i)). This update is implementable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of O(D(s+1)) gates; if the n-bit address is maintained internally, add O(n) gates for its increment. Proof: Evaluate each candidate's given gate list on the common n-bit address, costing at most s gates per candidate. Compare its output to b with a constant-size Boolean circuit, then AND with its prior agreement flag. This costs O(s+1) gates per candidate. A ripple-carry counter increments the address in O(n) gates. By induction on prefix length, a_C is 1 exactly for candidates agreeing with every bit seen. This is an explicit upper bound for an enumerated family; it does not remove the dependence on D or bound arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0532
statement: LEMMA (explicit candidate-filter update cost). Fix n and a finite list C_1,...,C_K of Boolean circuits, each with n inputs and at most s fan-in-two gates. Stream the truth table in binary input order, maintaining an n-bit index i and K live bits a_j, where a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with every streamed bit so far. On receipt of bit b, the exact update map on valid states can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(K(s+n)+n) gates. Proof: For each j, evaluate the hardwired C_j at the current index i, using at most s gates, and compute e_j = a_j AND [C_j(i)=b] with O(1) additional gates. These K evaluations and filters cost O(K(s+1)). Increment i modulo 2^n with an n-bit ripple-carry circuit costing O(n) gates. The resulting live bits satisfy the stated invariant by induction on the number of streamed bits: each candidate remains live precisely when it was previously live and its next output agrees with b. Thus the update is exact and has the claimed gate bound. Scope: explicitly listed candidates with a separate live bit per candidate; this bound does not give a polynomial-in-s update for the full circuit list, nor a bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits represented by H_C.

statement: statement: LEMMA (explicit exhaustive EXT update bound). Fix n≥1 and s≥0. Let C be the set of Boolean functions computed by circuits with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, constants, and one designated output, on n inputs. There is a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that decides whether each prefix p extends to the truth table of some function in C, using at most D=1+(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s candidate bits and at most O(D·s+n+s) elementary operations per streamed bit, with O(D+n+s) bits of working storage. Proof: enumerate all topologically ordered descriptions with exactly j gates for each 0≤j≤s, choosing each gate’s type and its two predecessor wires from at most n+j+2 available wires, then choosing one output wire. This enumerates a superset of C with at most the stated D descriptions (overcounting is harmless). Keep one live bit per description. Initially all are live. At truth-table position i, evaluate each live description on input i by evaluating its at most s gates, and clear it iff its output differs from the incoming bit. Inductively, after prefix p, the live descriptions are exactly those whose truth tables begin with p. Thus the algorithm accepts exactly when at least one live bit remains. Scope: the specified finite circuit model; the bound is exponential in s log(n+s), and does not imply polynomial update time or a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (corrected exhaustive EXT update bound). Fix n≥1 and s≥0. statement: statement: LEMMA (precomputed residual-mask update). Let F={f_1,...,f_M} be a finite set of distinct binary strings of common length N, in a fixed order. For prefix p of length i, let A_p={j: f_j extends p}. For each i<N and b in {0,1}, define the M-bit mask B_{i,b} by B_{i,b}[j]=1 iff f_j[i]=b. Encode p by the indicator vector a_p of A_p. Then the exact transition on b is a_{pb}=a_p AND B_{i,b}, coordinatewise, and p is accepted iff a_p is nonzero. Explicitly storing the masks uses 2NM bits; storing the state uses M bits. With word size w, an update takes ceil(M/w) wordwise AND operations plus O(1) position-update operations. The claim includes dead prefixes; the preprocessing and storage may be large and this gives no lower bound for other representations or real-gate transition circuits.

label: S0537
statement: statement: LEMMA (residual quotient lower bound for exact streaming states). Let F be a finite set of binary words of common length N, and let L_F be its prefix language, including the empty prefix and rejecting all non-prefixes. For each t, define R_t={ {u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} : p in {0,1}^t }. Any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that exactly decides L_F on length-N inputs has at least |R_t| distinct internal states after t input bits; hence it needs at least ceil(log_2 |R_t|) state bits at that layer. Proof: choose prefixes p,q of length t whose residual sets differ. Then some suffix u of length N-t belongs to exactly one residual set. Thus exactly one of pu, qu is in F, so exactly one full input is accepted. If the algorithm had the same state after p and q, determinism would give identical state evolution and identical final decision on the common continuation u, contradiction. Therefore each distinct residual set requires a distinct state. The statement is for exact deterministic streaming algorithms and does not lower-bound their transition circuit cost or apply to approximate/randomized machines.

structure.evidence: Unequal residual sets have a distinguishing suffix; equal machine states force equal outcomes on every common suffix. This proves the information lower bound for exact deterministic machines. It leaves the transition-cost bridge in Q-156fa9c912 open.

Given i and b, all M updated bits can be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(M(s+1)) gates, with absolute implied constant, using the listed circuits as subcircuits. Proof: For each j, evaluate C_j on the common address input i using its at most s gates. Compare its output with b using a constant number of gates, then AND that equality bit with a_j. This bound is for an explicit list and does not bound cost under arbitrary encodings; when M is the number of size-s circuits, it need not be polynomial in n,s.

Let C_1,...,C_M be Boolean functions on n-bit inputs, and stream their truth-table bits in a fixed order of length N=2^n. For each position i, precompute the constants v_{i,j}=C_j(i), for 1<=j<=M. Maintain a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the input prefix read so far. At position i, on reading b, update a'_j=a_j AND [v_{i,j}=b] for every j. This position-dependent fan-in-two circuit uses at most M AND gates plus one shared NOT gate, and the precomputed table uses MN bits. Starting with all a_j=1, after every prefix the live coordinates are exactly the candidates consistent with that prefix. Proof: Initially every candidate agrees with the empty prefix. If the invariant holds before position i, candidate j agrees with the longer prefix exactly when it previously agreed and its i-th truth-table bit equals b; this is precisely the update formula. Induction proves the invariant and thus exactness. statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual states are exactly the information needed by deterministic streaming). Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length at most N, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz is in L}. A deterministic streaming algorithm that decides membership in L after reading N bits can use the residual R_p as its state after prefix p: on bit b, update R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p}, and at length N accept exactly when the empty string belongs to R_p. Moreover, if R_p and R_q are distinct for two prefixes of the same length, every deterministic streaming algorithm correct for L must be in different states after p and q. Hence the minimum number of states at each fixed level is exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level.
evidence: Proof of sufficiency: after prefix p, store R_p. If the next bit is b, then for every suffix z of the required remaining length, (pb)z is in L iff p(bz) is in L iff bz is in R_p. Thus the updated set is precisely R_{pb}. After N bits, R_p is either {empty string} or empty, and membership is determined by whether it contains the empty string. For necessity, let p,q have equal length and distinct residuals. There is a suffix z in the symmetric difference of R_p and R_q. Then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. If a deterministic streaming algorithm reached the same state after p and q, its identical transition behavior on the common continuation z would give the same final answer for both, contradicting correctness. So those prefixes require distinct states. The state count is therefore exactly the number of distinct residuals at that level. This characterizes the information required for EXT, but gives no bound on the circuit cost of computing R_{pb} from a representation based on H_C.

statement: Let L⊆{0,1}^N be decided by a Boolean circuit H of size h, and let EXT_L(p) mean that p has an accepted completion in L. For any cut t<N, the transition output EXT_L(pb), for a prefix p of length t and next bit b, is computable by a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^(N-t-1)(h+1)-1. Proof: for each suffix q of length N-t-1, make a copy of H with its first t+1 inputs fixed to pb and its remaining inputs fixed to q; OR the 2^(N-t-1) outputs with a binary tree. This accepts exactly when some completion pq is in L. The bound counts h gates per copy and 2^(N-t-1)-1 OR gates. This explicit construction gives no polynomial transition-cost bound from an arbitrary decision circuit H_C.

label: S0571
statement: BLOCK-TRANSITION EXPANSION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates (constants and input wiring are free). Fix integers t,r with 0<=t<=N and 0<=r<=N-t. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t and block u in {0,1}^r, define E_{t+r}(pu)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-r} such that H(puz)=1. There is a circuit B_{t,r} on (p,u) computing E_{t+r}(pu) with at most 2^{N-t-r}(h+1)-1 fan-in-two gates. Proof: For each suffix z of length N-t-r, make a disjoint copy H_z of H; wire its first t+r input positions to (p,u), and wire its remaining positions to the constant string z. OR all 2^{N-t-r} output bits using a binary tree, which uses 2^{N-t-r}-1 gates. The total is 2^{N-t-r}h+(2^{N-t-r}-1)=2^{N-t-r}(h+1)-1 gates. For every (p,u), this OR is 1 exactly when at least one completion z makes H(puz)=1. Thus if N-t-r<=c log_2(h+2) for fixed c, the size is polynomial in h. This constructs the block-completion predicate only; it does not show that a compact state or transition can be computed from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits at cost poly(s).

label: S0572
statement: FIXED-TAIL PROJECTION WITH POLYNOMIAL COST. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} have a fan-in-two circuit of h gates, and let 0<=k<=N. Define P_k(x)=OR_{z in {0,1}^k} H(xz), for x in {0,1}^{N-k}. Then P_k has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^k(h+1)-1 gates. If k<=c log_2(h+2) for fixed c>=0, its size is at most (h+2)^c(h+1)-1, hence O((h+2)^(c+1)). Proof: For each of the 2^k strings z, create a disjoint copy H_z of H, wire its final k inputs to z and its first N-k inputs to x. OR the outputs with a fan-in-two tree using 2^k-1 gates. The total is 2^k h+2^k-1. For every x, this OR is 1 exactly when some z satisfies H(xz)=1, so it computes P_k. The logarithmic-tail condition gives 2^k<=(h+2)^c and the stated bound. This is one fixed projection; it implies no polynomial-cost representation for cuts with superlogarithmic remaining suffix.

statement: For any Boolean circuit H:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, any 0<=t<N, and every prefix p in {0,1}^t, define E_t(p)=1 iff some suffix q of length N-t satisfies H(pq)=1. Then E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Proof: Every suffix of length N-t has a unique first bit b in {0,1} and a remaining suffix r of length N-t-1. Thus a completion q with H(pq)=1 exists iff there are b,r with H(pbr)=1, which holds iff E_{t+1}(pb)=1 for at least one b. This identity gives the exact one-bit recurrence for the completion predicate, but does not recover the two child values from E_t(p) or bound the real-gate cost of computing either child from H.

statement:
statement: Residual cofactor transition lemma. Let N be a nonnegative integer, F be any subset of {0,1}^N, 0 <= t < N, and p be a length-t prefix. Define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, define the cofactor D_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. Then R_{t+1}(pb)=D_b(R_t(p)). Consequently, if R_t(p)=R_t(q) for two length-t prefixes p,q, then for each bit b their child residuals are equal; and the pair of child residuals is determined by the full parent residual. Proof: For every v of length N-t-1, v is in R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbv is in F. This is equivalent to bv being in R_t(p), which is equivalent to v being in D_b(R_t(p)). Thus the sets agree. Replacing p by q gives the equal-child consequence when parent residuals coincide. The formula defines each child from the full residual by restriction to strings beginning in b. In contrast, the single bit [R_t(p) is nonempty] need not determine either child bit: for N-t=1, residuals {0} and {1} both have nonempty indicator 1, but their 0-child acceptance indicators differ. This is an exact information-level transition rule; it does not bound the number or real-gate cost of operations needed to compute a cofactor when the representation is an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All finite binary languages F subset {0,1}^N, all 0 <= t < N, and all prefixes p of length t. Residuals are literal suffix sets; cofactor operation is D_b(R)={v:bv in R}. No circuit-size, transition-cost, or P versus NP consequence is claimed.

statement:
statement: Residual-circuit restriction lemma. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For every t in {0,...,N} and prefix p in {0,1}^t, define H_p:{0,1}^{N-t}->{0,1} by H_p(q)=H(pq). Then H_p is computed by a circuit with at most h gates, obtained by fixing the first t input wires of H to the bits of p. If t<N and b is a bit, H_{pb}(r)=H_p(br), so the child residual circuit also uses at most h gates. Proof: Substitute constants p at the corresponding input wires of H; this changes no gate and computes q -> H(pq). For the child, substitute b at the first remaining input wire of this restricted circuit; again no gate changes, and its output on r is H_p(br)=H(pbr)=H_{pb}(r). Thus both restrictions preserve the gate bound. statement:
statement: One-bit branching-information lemma for EXT. Let F be a finite binary language of words of length N, let t<N, and for every length-t prefix p define e(p)=1 iff R_t(p) is nonempty. Define e_0(p)=1 iff R_{t+1}(p0) is nonempty and e_1(p)=1 iff R_{t+1}(p1) is nonempty. Then e(p)=e_0(p) OR e_1(p). If e(p)=0 the child pair is (0,0); if e(p)=1 the possible child pairs are exactly (1,0),(0,1),(1,1). Proof: Partition the suffixes in R_t(p) by their first bit. The 0-section is nonempty exactly when R_{t+1}(p0) is nonempty, and the 1-section exactly when R_{t+1}(p1) is nonempty. Thus the parent is nonempty iff at least one child is nonempty. An empty parent forces (0,0). Each of the other three pairs is realizable by a language whose words extending p have suffixes respectively {0v}, {1v}, or {0v,1v}, for any v of length N-t-1. Hence the one-bit extension summary loses which child branches survive.
scope: All finite F subset {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. This is an information statement about the Boolean extension predicate, not a gate lower bound or a lower bound on richer representations; no P versus NP consequence is claimed.

An empty parent forces (0,0). Each of the other three pairs is realizable by a language whose words extending p have suffixes respectively {0v}, {1v}, or {0v,1v}, for any v of length N-t-1. statement:
statement: Completion-circuit cofactor recurrence. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, and for each 0<=t<=N define E_t(p)=1 iff some suffix u in {0,1}^{N-t} satisfies H(pu)=1. If E_{t+d} is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of g gates, then E_t is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^d(g+1)-1 gates. Proof: For each of the 2^d suffixes v of length d, fix v in a copy of the E_{t+d} circuit, leaving the first t bits as inputs. The outputs compute E_{t+d}(pv); their OR is E_t(p), since every completion of p has a unique first d bits. A binary OR tree combines the 2^d outputs using 2^d-1 gates. This bounds one Boolean completion predicate at a cut; it does not bound computation of the next residual-state encoding of EXT.

statement:
statement: Penultimate-cut completion bound. Let N>=1 and let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and wiring free. For p in {0,1}^{N-1}, define E(p)=1 iff H(p0)=1 or H(p1)=1. Then E is computed by a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2h+1 gates. Proof: Make two copies of the circuit for H. In the first copy fix its Nth input to 0; in the second fix it to 1. The resulting circuits compute p↦H(p0) and p↦H(p1), each using at most h gates. Feed their outputs to one OR gate. The output is E(p) by its definition, and the total gate count is at most h+h+1. This is the EXT completion predicate at the sole cut with one unprocessed bit; it gives no bound at earlier cuts.

label: S0581
statement:
statement: Dense residual streaming cost lemma. Let H:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be given by a fan-in-two circuit of h gates. A deterministic left-to-right streaming representation can initialize an N-stage residual table using at most h·2^N gate evaluations, store at most 2^N bits, and update it over the entire input using exactly 2^N−1 bit selections/writes (and no Boolean gates), if a state is represented as an explicit array indexed by suffixes and coordinate selection is the unit-cost update operation. Proof: At depth t store the array A_t[u]=H(pu), for all suffixes u of length N−t, where p is the prefix read so far. Initialize A_0 by evaluating H on each of the 2^N inputs, costing at most h·2^N gates and storing 2^N output bits. Upon reading b, form A_{t+1}[u]=A_t[bu] for each suffix u of length N−t−1. The identity follows directly: A_t[bu]=H(pbu)=A_{t+1}[u]. Thus each update copies one half of the old array and costs 2^(N−t−1) coordinate selections/writes. Summing over t=0,...,N−1 gives Σ_{j=0}^{N−1}2^j=2^N−1. The largest stored array is A_0, of 2^N bits. The update bound is in the stated explicit-array access model; it is not a fan-in-two Boolean circuit bound or a compact/poly(s) representation.
scope: All N≥0 and Boolean H with an h-gate fan-in-two circuit. Resource units are specified explicitly: Boolean gate evaluations for initialization, explicit stored bits, and unit-cost array coordinate selections/writes for updates.

statement: BINARY RESIDUAL PARTITION LEMMA. Let N>=1, L be a subset of {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p in {0,1}^t. Define E_t(p)=1 iff there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in L. Then E_t(p)=E_{t+1}(p0) OR E_{t+1}(p1). Proof: Every completion u has a unique decomposition u=bv, where b is a bit and v is a suffix of length N-t-1. There exists u with pu in L iff there exists b and v with pbv in L. This is equivalent to E_{t+1}(p0)=1 or E_{t+1}(p1)=1, by definition. When t=N-1, v is the empty string, so the boundary case is included. This is only a semantic recurrence and gives no real-gate cost bound from an arbitrary circuit H_C.

statement:
statement: Residual membership update lemma. Let L be a language of words of length N, let p have length t<N, and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in L}. For b in {0,1} and u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, the next residual membership bit satisfies 1[u in R_{t+1}(pb)] = 1[bu in R_t(p)]. Thus membership in the next residual is computable with one membership query to the current residual, by prefixing the queried suffix with b. Proof: u belongs to R_{t+1}(pb) iff pbu belongs to L; this holds iff bu belongs to R_t(p), by the definition of R_t(p). This is an oracle-query identity only; it gives no bound on the real-gate cost of representing or querying R_t(p) from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: All fixed-length binary languages L subseteq {0,1}^N, all 0<=t<N, all length-t prefixes p, incoming bits b, and suffixes u of length N-t-1.

label: S0585
statement: statement: Restricted-circuit residual bound. Fix N,h≥0 and a fan-in-two Boolean circuit H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} with h gates; constants and wiring are free. For every t∈{0,…,N} and p∈{0,1}^t, let R_t(p)={q∈{0,1}^{N−t}:H(pq)=1}. Then R_t(p) is computed by a circuit H_p on N−t inputs with at most h gates, obtained by substituting p into H. Under a topological encoding listing each gate type and its two predecessor indices, plus the output source, the number D_t of distinct residuals is at most (c(N+h+2)^2)^(h+1) for an absolute constant c. Each residual has a description of O((h+1)log(N+h+2)) bits. Proof: Substituting p for the first t input wires leaves all h gate operations unchanged, so H_p computes q↦H(pq). For the count, each gate chooses one of finitely many types and two sources among at most N+h+2 possibilities; the output chooses one source from that set. Thus the number of descriptions is at most (c(N+h+2)^2)^(h+1). Each description computes at most one residual, which proves the bound. A description can be stored using O((h+1)log(N+h+2)) bits. This is an information bound only: it gives no polynomial-in-(h,n) bound when N=2^n and no real-gate transition circuit for canonical encodings.

label: S0586
statement: statement: Candidate-set transition lemma for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite enumeration C_{n,s} of all Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with a fixed ordering of their 2^n truth-table positions. For a prefix p of length t define V_t(p)={C in C_{n,s}: the first t outputs of C equal p}. Then V_{t+1}(pb)={C in V_t(p): C's output at position t+1 equals b}. Consequently V_t(p) is nonempty iff p is an extendible prefix of a size-at-most-s circuit truth table, and the transition rule recognizes EXT exactly. Proof: By definition, C belongs to V_{t+1}(pb) exactly when its first t outputs equal p and its (t+1)st output equals b. The first condition is C in V_t(p), and the second is the stated filter predicate, proving equality. Nonemptiness is equivalent to existence of a circuit completion, which is the definition of EXT. This is an exact information representation and transition identity; it makes no polynomial bound on representing V_t(p), testing the filter, or implementing transitions from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.

label: S0591
statement: statement: Black-box completion-query lower bound. For every k>=0, any deterministic exact algorithm that decides whether an unknown set F subseteq {0,1}^k is nonempty, with access only to membership queries x -> 1[x in F], requires 2^k queries in the worst case. Proof: Run the algorithm against the all-zero oracle (F=empty). If it makes fewer than 2^k queries, choose an unqueried u. The same transcript occurs for F={u}, although the correct outputs differ, contradiction. Querying all strings suffices. Hence for a prefix with k remaining bits, black-box membership access on completed strings alone gives no worst-case exact prefix-extension procedure using fewer than 2^k queries. This is an oracle-model bound only and makes no assertion about real-gate cost when the circuit or structure of F is available.

structure.gap: Whether an EXT transition can be implemented with bounded real-gate cost from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C remains open; the lemma narrows the question by showing complete-input membership queries alone can require 2^(N-|p|) queries in the black-box model.

label: S0594
statement: statement: DNF restriction lemma. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF on N Boolean variables with L total literal occurrences. For any prefix p of length t, the extension predicate E_p(u)=H(pu) has a DNF with at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences. Construct it by deleting every term falsified by a fixed prefix literal, then deleting the remaining fixed prefix literals. Proof: each term on input pu is false if one of its fixed literals is false; otherwise it equals the conjunction of its unfixed literals. Disjoining these term identities gives H(pu)=E_p(u). The construction scans the literals once, so takes O(L+h) inspections and has circuit size O(L+h) with binary fan-in gates. Empty terms and an empty disjunction represent true and false, respectively. This proves a linear-cost prefix transition for explicit DNF membership circuits; it gives no such bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

label: S0595
statement: statement: Existential projection lemma for explicit DNF. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF on N Boolean variables, with L total literal occurrences, and split variables into a prefix a and suffix u. Define E(a)=1 iff there exists u with H(a,u)=1. Construct E by deleting each term whose prefix literals conflict with a, and then deleting every suffix literal from each remaining term. The resulting DNF has at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences. Proof: For fixed a and each term T_j, if a falsifies one of its prefix literals then T_j(a,u)=0 for every u. Otherwise its prefix literals are true, and there exists a suffix u satisfying the remaining suffix literals: each variable occurs with a single polarity within a term, so set those variables accordingly and assign all other suffix variables arbitrarily. Thus this term contributes to E(a) exactly when its prefix literals are all true, which is precisely the projected term after suffix literals are removed. Taking the disjunction proves equality. The construction scans the explicit literals in O(L+h) time and yields a binary fan-in circuit of O(L+h) gates. Scope is existential projection of explicit DNF; no implication for arbitrary circuits.

label: S0596
statement: statement: Repaired existential-projection lemma for explicit DNF. Let H(x)=OR_{j=1}^h T_j(x) be a DNF over N Boolean variables with L literal occurrences; literals may repeat or include both polarities of a variable. Split variables into prefix a and suffix u. The predicate E(a)=1 iff there exists u with H(a,u)=1 has a DNF with at most h terms and at most L literal occurrences: in each term, delete the term if it contains opposite-polarity literals of any variable or if its prefix literals contradict the fixed a; otherwise remove all suffix literals and retain its prefix literals. Proof: A term with contradictory literals is unsatisfiable. A term whose prefix literals conflict with a is false for every suffix. Thus the existential projection of each term is exactly its retained prefix conjunction, and existential quantification distributes over finite disjunction. statement: Witness-set transition lemma for EXT. Fix n,s and a finite, explicitly indexed family C_{n,s} of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, with a fixed output ordering for each truth table. For every length-t prefix p, define W_p={C in C_{n,s}: the first t truth-table bits of C equal p}. Then EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff W_p is nonempty. For t<N and b in {0,1}, W_{pb}={C in W_p: bit_{t+1}(C)=b}; hence W_p is the disjoint union of W_{p0} and W_{p1}. Storing W_p as an explicit bit vector gives an exact deterministic EXT streaming algorithm with at most |C_{n,s}| bits of state; its transition on b scans the indexed circuits and retains exactly those whose (t+1)-st truth-table bit equals b, and final acceptance tests nonemptiness. Proof: By definition, C belongs to W_{pb} exactly when its first t bits equal p and its next bit equals b, which is equivalent to C belonging to W_p and bit_{t+1}(C)=b. Every C in W_p has exactly one next output bit, so the two child sets are disjoint and partition W_p. Nonemptiness of W_p is equivalent to existence of a size-at-most-s circuit with truth-table prefix p, which is the definition of EXT. The explicit transition is correct by the membership equivalence. This is an exact constructive representation, but its state and transition costs are governed by |C_{n,s}|; the lemma makes no polynomial-cost claim and gives no simulation by an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
scope: Finite circuit family with a fixed canonical enumeration and truth-table bit order; exact prefix recognition; no circuit-complexity upper bound beyond explicit witness-set enumeration.

label: S0600
statement:
statement: Explicit candidate-mask update bound for EXT. Fix N≥1 and a finite, explicitly listed family C={C_1,...,C_M} of Boolean circuits, each producing an N-bit string in a fixed order. At position t, store the M-bit mask A_t whose i-th bit is 1 exactly when C_i agrees with the prefix read so far. On reading b∈{0,1}, update each bit by A_{t+1}[i]=A_t[i] ∧ [C_i(t+1)=b]. This update is realizable with at most M fan-in-two AND gates once the position-t output bits C_i(t+1) are available; if those bits are computed from the circuit descriptions during the update, their evaluation cost must be added. The state is exact: A_t is nonzero iff the read prefix is extendible to a member of C, and induction on t proves the invariant. Thus explicit enumeration gives an exact per-bit transition bound of M plus the cost of obtaining the M predicted bits, but does not yield a polynomial-in-s transition bound when M is the number of size-at-most-s circuits.
scope: Finite explicitly enumerated candidate families with deterministic Boolean circuits and a fixed output-bit order; fan-in-two update gates. No claim that M or the total transition cost is polynomial in s, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.
proof: Initially set every mask bit to 1, since the empty prefix agrees with every candidate. Suppose the stored invariant holds after t bits. For candidate i, it agrees with the extended prefix ending in b exactly when it agreed with the length-t prefix and its (t+1)-st output bit equals b. This is precisely the stated AND update, so the invariant holds by induction. A nonzero mask is equivalent to at least one listed candidate agreeing with the prefix, which is exactly extendibility within the listed family. Each updated bit is one binary conjunction, giving M fan-in-two gates after the predicted bits are available. If those bits are not supplied, their computation is a separate cost and cannot be omitted.

statement:
statement: Lemma: For any fixed layer t, the EXT_{n,s} transition function T_t: R_t(p) × {0,1} → R_{t+1}(pb) can be realized as a projection of the evaluation of H_C on all suffixes of length N-t-1, but no representation of the residual class as a Boolean circuit of size polynomial in s and log N is known that works for every H_C. In particular, if H_C is an arbitrary circuit deciding membership in Im(Eval), then the map from H_C to a circuit computing T_t may require solving circuit equivalence or existential quantification over circuits of size ≤ s, which is not known to be in P. Therefore, the existence of a uniform poly(s, log N) real-gate transition for EXT from arbitrary H_C remains open, and the candidate-mask bound (S0600) is tight for the explicit enumeration approach.
scope: Arbitrary Boolean circuits H_C deciding EXT_{n,s}; real-gate complexity of the transition function T_t as a function of s and N=2^n. No claim that the transition cannot be done in poly(s) gates, only that no such construction is known and the explicit enumeration gives an exponential upper bound.
proof: The transition T_t on input b maps a residual class R = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N-t} : pu ∈ Im(Eval)} to R_b = {v ∈ {0,1}^{N-t-1} : bv ∈ R}. By S0477, R_b = {v : pbv ∈ Im(Eval)}. This set is exactly the set of suffixes v such that H_C(pbv) = 1. A circuit for T_t must therefore compute, from a description of R and b, a description of R_b. The candidate-mask construction (S0600) does this by explicitly tracking agreement with all M = |Im(Eval) ∩ {0,1}^N| candidates, giving M AND gates. Any representation that avoids enumerating all candidates must implicitly perform existential quantification over circuits of size ≤ s to determine which suffixes remain consistent. Since H_C is an arbitrary decision circuit (not necessarily an evaluation circuit), no poly(s) translation from H_C to a transition circuit is known. This is not a lower bound; it is a precise statement of the current knowledge gap.

label: S0630
statement: LEMMA (exact residual characterization for a finite fixed-length language). Let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and L=A, viewed as a language over {0,1}. For each prefix p of length k≤N define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-k}: pu∈A}. The minimal deterministic finite automaton for L has exactly 1+Σ_{k=0}^N |{R_p : p∈{0,1}^k, R_p≠∅}| states, where the additional state is the rejecting sink. Proof: For any prefix p, its right language {u:pu∈L} equals R_p, and is empty exactly when p is not a prefix of any word in A. Two prefixes p,p' are equivalent in the Myhill–Nerode relation precisely when their right languages agree. If their lengths differ, their nonempty right languages contain words of different fixed lengths, so they cannot agree; an empty right language is shared by all non-prefixes and is the sink. At a fixed length k, equivalence is exactly equality of the sets R_p. Every nonempty R_p is reached by reading p, and the empty right language is reached by any non-prefix (or, if none exists, the transition from a length-N accepting state on either further bit). Thus the stated count is exact. Consequently, the upper bound in S0520 can be sharpened by replacing min(2^k,|A|) with the exact number of distinct nonempty suffix sets at level k; any two prefixes at that level with different residual sets require distinct automaton states. This is an exact characterization for explicit finite A only and gives no lower bound on the gate cost of an implicit EXT transition or on arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: LEMMA (residual derivative gives the exact EXT transition). Let N≥1 and A⊆{0,1}^N. At level k<N, for p∈{0,1}^k define R_p={u∈{0,1}^{N-k}:pu∈A}. For b∈{0,1}, define D_b(R_p)={u∈{0,1}^{N-k-1}:bu∈R_p}. Then R_{pb}=D_b(R_p). Hence the deterministic prefix automaton transition from residual state R_p on b goes to D_b(R_p) if nonempty, otherwise the rejecting sink. At level N both outgoing transitions go to the sink. Proof: for each u of length N−k−1, u∈R_{pb} iff (pb)u∈A iff p(bu)∈A iff bu∈R_p iff u∈D_b(R_p). Thus equality holds pointwise. In particular, equal residual sets at the same level have equal b-successors. This characterizes the exact information and abstract update for an explicit finite language, but gives neither a compact encoding nor a low-cost update circuit for implicit EXT_{n,s}, and implies nothing about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0632
statement:
statement: LEMMA (exact residual states of a finite word family). Let N be a nonnegative integer and let A be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Let Pref(A) be the set of all prefixes of words in A, including the empty word, and let L=Pref(A). For each k in {0,...,N} and each length-k prefix p occurring in a member of A, define S(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-k}: pu in A}. Then the minimal DFA recognizing L has exactly 1 + sum_{k=0}^N |{S(p): p is a length-k prefix of a member of A}| states. Proof: For any such p, its left quotient p^{-1}L consists exactly of Pref(S(p)): pw is a prefix of some a in A iff w is a prefix of the unique length-(N-k) suffix u with pu=a. At a fixed k, the words of maximum length N-k in Pref(S(p)) are exactly S(p), so different S(p) yield different quotients. For nonempty S(p), Pref(S(p)) has maximum word length N-k; hence quotients from different depths k are distinct. Every prefix in L has one of these quotients, while any non-prefix has empty quotient and all such prefixes share the rejecting sink. By Myhill-Nerode, the stated count is exact. This is a theorem about explicitly specified finite word families; it makes no assertion about compact transition circuits for implicitly represented families.
derivation: The quotient identity follows from the definition of prefix closure. Recovering the suffix set from maximum-length words proves injectivity within a level; maximum accepted continuation length distinguishes levels. The only quotient outside those represented by prefixes is the empty quotient, giving one sink.
scope: All finite nonempty A subset {0,1}^N; exact DFA state count for Pref(A), no circuit complexity or PNP transfer claim.

label: S0633
statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual languages are necessary streaming state information). Let L be any language of finite binary strings, and let a deterministic one-pass streaming machine decide, after each prefix p, whether p is a prefix of some word in L. Define R_p={z : pz is in L}. If two prefixes p,q lead the machine to the same internal state, then R_p=R_q. Consequently the machine has at least as many reachable states as there are distinct residual languages R_p. Proof: for every suffix z, deterministic processing from the same state on z has the same final outcome. The machine accepts pz exactly when z∈R_p, and accepts qz exactly when z∈R_q. Equality of states therefore implies, for every z, z∈R_p iff z∈R_q, hence R_p=R_q. Contrapositively, distinct residuals require distinct states. This is a necessary-information bound; it makes no gate-cost claim and does not imply that an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit exposes or updates the residuals efficiently.
derivation: The state-equality implication follows by applying the same continuation z to equal deterministic states and using exact correctness on both completed streams.

label: S0635
statement:
statement: LEMMA (residual information for prefix extendibility). Let L⊆{0,1}* and P=Pref(L)={p: there exists w with pw∈L}. Suppose a deterministic streaming machine, after reading each string p, outputs 1 exactly when p∈P. For each p define R_p^P={z∈{0,1}*: pz∈P}. If p and q lead to the same machine state, then R_p^P=R_q^P. Proof: fix any z. Starting from the equal states after p and q, deterministic processing of the same continuation z ends in the same state and hence gives the same output. By correctness, that output is 1 exactly when pz∈P, and also exactly when qz∈P. Thus pz∈P iff qz∈P for every z, so the residual sets are equal. Consequently distinct residuals of Pref(L) require distinct reachable states. This is an information requirement only; it gives no gate-cost bound for transitions.
derivation: Corrected the observable language from L to its prefix closure Pref(L), because EXT outputs whether a prefix has some completion rather than whether a specified continuation completes it.

structure.refuted_approach: S0633's residual set R_p={z:pz∈L} is not justified by a machine that only reports whether each current prefix is extendible to a word in L. label: S0636
statement: statement: LEMMA (candidate-set to EXT-residual map). Fix a finite indexed family F of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, and stream each function's truth table in the same fixed input order. For a prefix p of length k, let L_p be the functions agreeing with p on the first k inputs, and let R_p be the set of their remaining truth-table suffixes. Then R_p is exactly the EXT continuation residual after p. For the next truth-table position i_k and bit b, L_{pb}={f in L_p:f(i_k)=b}, and R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p}. Thus candidate sets are exact sufficient states, while the minimal residual states identify candidate sets precisely when they induce the same suffix set. Proof: A suffix z completes p to a prefix of a family truth table exactly when some function in L_p has remaining suffix z, which is the definition of R_p. A function remains live after reading b exactly when it was live before and its value at i_k equals b. A suffix z completes pb exactly when bz completes p, giving the residual identity. Therefore continuation behavior depends only on R_p; distinct candidate sets need not be distinct states if their suffix sets agree.

label: S0637
statement: statement: LEMMA (reachable candidate sets are exactly EXT residuals for duplicate-free functions). Let F be a finite set of pairwise distinct Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with truth tables read in a fixed order. For every prefix p of length k, let L_p={f∈F: f agrees with p on the first k inputs}, and let R_p={z∈{0,1}^{2^n-k}: pz is a prefix of the truth table of some f∈F}. Then the map f↦the remaining truth-table suffix of f is a bijection from L_p to R_p. In particular |L_p|=|R_p|, and two reachable prefixes p,q have the same live-function set if and only if their residual suffix sets (viewed at their respective stream positions) agree after identifying the remaining coordinates. Proof: If f∈L_p, its remaining suffix z satisfies that pz is the full truth table of f, so z∈R_p. Conversely, if z∈R_p, by definition some f∈F has truth table beginning pz, and so f∈L_p maps to z. For injectivity, if f,g∈L_p map to the same z, then both truth tables consist of the same length-k prefix p followed by z; hence their truth tables agree at all 2^n inputs, so f=g, using extensional equality of Boolean functions. This gives a canonical identification of reachable candidate sets with residual sets; it does not bound the gate cost of computing the update for the implicit family of all size-s circuits.

statement: statement: CORRECTED LEMMA (candidate/residual bijection at a fixed stream position). label: S0643
statement: LEMMA (done-bit repair for an explicitly listed finite truth-table family). Let C_1,...,C_M be explicitly listed Boolean circuits on n input bits with fan-in-two gate counts s_1,...,s_M, M>=1, and let N=2^n. A deterministic streaming recognizer for Pref({TT(C_j):1<=j<=M}) has state (i,a_1,...,a_M,d), where i is an n-bit address, a_j records agreement with candidate j, and d is a done bit. It uses O(n+M+sum_j s_j) fan-in-two gates per input-bit update. Initially i=0, every a_j=1, d=0. While d=0, on bit b set a_j to a_j AND [C_j(i)=b]. If i=N-1, set d=1 and hold i; otherwise increment i. When d=1, any further input clears every a_j and leaves d=1. Accept iff some a_j=1. Proof: Before each of the first N updates, induction gives that i is the next truth-table address and a_j=1 exactly when C_j agrees with the prefix already read. The update checks the next bit and preserves this invariant; at the final address it sets d, and otherwise advances i. Hence a prefix of length at most N is accepted exactly when some listed truth table extends it. Once d=1, any extra bit clears the mask permanently, so all longer strings reject. Evaluating the listed circuits costs sum_j s_j gates; comparisons and mask updates cost O(M), and address increment plus terminal detection cost O(n). This applies only to an explicitly listed family and gives no compact transition bound for minimized EXT or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: LEMMA (explicit-list state-bit bound for prefix extension). Let C_1,...,C_M be explicitly listed Boolean circuits on n input bits, each of fan-in-two size s_j, and let N=2^n. label: S0646
statement: LEMMA (exact suffix-expansion circuit for EXT transitions). Let N>=1, let C be a Boolean circuit of size L on N inputs, and let 0<=t<N and b in {0,1}. Define T_{t,b}(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} such that C(p||b||z)=1, for p in {0,1}^t. Then T_{t,b} has a fan-in-two circuit of size at most 2^{N-t-1}(L+1)-1, assuming input fixing and wiring are free. Proof: For each suffix z, make one copy of C, wire p||b to its first t+1 inputs, and fix the remaining inputs to z. OR the 2^{N-t-1} outputs with a binary tree, requiring 2^{N-t-1}-1 gates. The result is 1 exactly when some completion is accepted by C. When C recognizes the size-at-most-s truth tables, this computes the EXT next-bit predicate. This is an exact, generally exponential upper bound; it provides neither a compact encoding of all residual states nor a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP circuits. Barrier diagnostic: the construction relativizes (copies and OR only); it is not a natural-proofs lower-bound argument; Boolean wiring raises no algebrization issue; locality is not asserted. It passes none of the circumvention tests as a compression: it retains suffix enumeration and supplies no re-coding bound, adaptive rule, new resource, or transfer to arbitrary MCSP circuits.

label: S0647
statement: LEMMA (two-output suffix-expansion bound). Let C:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size L, and let p be a fixed prefix of length t<N. For b in {0,1}, define T_b(p)=1 iff there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with C(p||b||z)=1. The pair (T_0(p),T_1(p)) is computable by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^{N-t}(L+1)-2 gates, using independent copies of C and fixed-input wiring. Proof: Let k=2^{N-t-1}. For each b and each suffix z, use a copy of C with p||b wired to its fixed inputs; this uses at most 2kL gates total. For each b, OR its k outputs with a binary tree using k-1 gates; total OR cost is 2(k-1). Thus the total is 2k(L+1)-2=2^{N-t}(L+1)-2. Each output equals the existential disjunction over precisely the suffixes in its branch, so it computes T_b(p).

statement: LEMMA (block transition composition for an explicitly represented candidate family). Let D={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on a finite domain X, and let a_0,...,a_{N-1} be a fixed ordering of X. Suppose u∈{0,1}^M marks the candidates consistent with the truth-table prefix before position t. For a block w=(w_0,...,w_{d-1}), define F_{t,w}(j)=1 iff C_j(a_{t+r})=w_r for every 0≤r<d. The updated mask is u'=u∧F_{t,w}, coordinatewise. For consecutive blocks w,v, F_{t,wv}=F_{t,w}∧F_{t+d,v}; thus block updates compose associatively. If each C_j is given by a fan-in-two circuit of at most s gates, a direct implementation uses O(Md(s+1)) gates, plus input-address handling.
derivation: Candidate j survives the extended prefix exactly when it survived the old prefix and agrees at every new block position. This is the stated coordinatewise conjunction. Splitting the conjunction for wv at the boundary between w and v proves the composition identity; associativity of conjunction makes the result independent of parenthesization. For the gate bound, evaluate each C_j at each of the d fixed points, compare with the corresponding fixed bit, AND the d comparisons, then AND with u_j. This uses O(d(s+1)) gates per candidate, hence O(Md(s+1)) total, plus address handling. This result is limited to explicitly represented families; it gives no compact update for the full size-s circuit family, no transition bound through H_C, and no implication for arbitrary MCSP deciders.

label: S0649
statement: statement: LEMMA (prefix projection of a deterministic circuit’s trace relation). Let C:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be a Boolean circuit with gates ordered topologically as g_1,...,g_m, and let T_i(x,y_{<i}) be the Boolean function computed at gate i from input x and earlier gate values. Define H_C(x,y)=T_out(x,y) AND ∧_{i=1}^m (y_i ↔ T_i(x,y_{<i})), where T_out is the circuit’s output wire interpreted using x and y. For every fixed x there is exactly one y with all trace equations true, namely the vector of gate values obtained by evaluating C on x. Consequently, for every prefix p of length t≤N, EXT_C(p):=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^{N−t} satisfies C(pz)=1 is equivalent to ∃z∈{0,1}^{N−t}∃y∈{0,1}^m H_C(pz,y)=1. Proof: Induct on i. Once x and y_1,...,y_{i−1} are fixed, the i-th equation forces y_i to the unique value T_i(x,y_{<i}); hence the equations have exactly one solution y, and that solution is the actual gate-evaluation trace. On this unique trace, T_out equals C(x), so H_C(x,y)=1 exactly when C(x)=1. Existentially quantifying the suffix z therefore yields the stated prefix equivalence.

statement: statement: LEMMA (precomputed candidate-mask update). Let D={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, with fixed input order a_0,...,a_{N-1}, N=2^n. Define u_j=1 iff C_j agrees with the observed prefix p_0,...,p_{t-1}. If v_t=(C_1(a_t),...,C_M(a_t)) is available as fixed circuit constants, then after observing b the exact updated mask is u'_j=u_j AND [v_{t,j}=b] for j=1,...,M. It takes at most M+1 fan-in-two gates (one shared NOT of b, then one AND per candidate). Direct preprocessing of all N columns by evaluating M circuits of at most s gates costs O(MN(s+n)) Boolean operations and stores MN bits. Proof: Since v_{t,j} is a fixed bit, [v_{t,j}=b] is b when v_{t,j}=1 and NOT b otherwise. Thus each updated bit is computed with one AND after the shared complement is formed. It is 1 exactly when candidate j matched all earlier bits and matches the new bit. Induction on t proves the mask is exactly the consistent candidate set. The result separates preprocessing/storage from per-symbol transition cost and is restricted to an explicit finite family.
