label: S0974
statement:
statement: statement: EXPLICIT PREFIX-TRIE TRANSITION BOUND. Let N>=0 and L be any subset of {0,1}^N with M=|L|. The prefix trie has at most 1+NM nodes and NM directed edges. It recognizes L with a deterministic finite automaton using at most 2+NM states, counting one rejecting sink. Proof: Each word contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, so their union has at most NM nodes; adjoining the empty root gives at most 1+NM trie nodes. Every nonroot trie node has exactly one incoming edge, so there are at most NM edges. Add one rejecting sink; from each trie node on bit b follow the b-edge if present and otherwise enter the sink, and let exactly the length-N word nodes be accepting. This deterministic automaton accepts exactly L. Its states can be encoded using ceil(log2(2+NM)) bits. This is a finite-state transition-table construction, not a Boolean circuit size bound for implementing the transition function.
derivation: Count at most N nonempty prefixes per word and take their union; each nonroot trie node corresponds to exactly one edge; add a sink and define transitions by trie edges or sink, with accepting nodes precisely L.
scope: All finite N>=0 and L subset {0,1}^N; gives state count and an explicit transition table only, without circuit complexity guarantees.

label: S0975
statement:
statement: EXACT PREFIX RECURRENCE FOR A FIXED CIRCUIT. Let C:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be a Boolean circuit, and let H_C(x,y) be its local tableau verifier, with y containing one output bit per gate. For each prefix p of length t≤N, define E_C(p)=1 iff there are z∈{0,1}^{N−t} and y such that H_C(pz,y)=1. Then E_C(p)=E_C(p0)∨E_C(p1) for t<N, and E_C(p)=C(p) for t=N. Also, for every p, E_C(p)=1 iff some completion x of p satisfies C(x)=1. Proof: The gate equations in H_C uniquely force y to be the evaluation of C on its input, by induction in topological gate order. Thus H_C(x,y)=1 for some y exactly when C(x)=1. For t<N, every completion of p has a unique first suffix bit b∈{0,1} and a remaining suffix z′; hence a satisfying completion of p exists exactly when a satisfying completion of p0 or p1 exists. At t=N the only completion is p itself, giving E_C(p)=C(p). This establishes exact information and its recurrence; it makes no bound on the ordinary-circuit cost of computing E_C from a representation of H_C.
derivation: Use uniqueness of the local gate-evaluation tableau to replace existential quantification over y by C(x)=1. Partition all completions of a nonterminal prefix according to their next bit; at a full-length prefix there is only that input.
scope: All finite N and all fixed Boolean circuits C; fan-in is unrestricted for the recurrence, provided H_C correctly encodes C. This is a semantic identity, not a transition-cost or MCSP lower-bound claim.

structure.lemma: The local tableau verifier for a fixed circuit gives exact existential prefix semantics and a binary recurrence, but does not by itself bound ordinary-circuit transition cost.

label: S0976
statement:
statement: FINITE-FAMILY PREFIX FILTER TRANSITION. Let N,K be positive integers and let C_1,...,C_K be explicitly listed Boolean functions on {0,1}^N (equivalently, K fixed truth tables). Define Q(p)={i in [K] : C_i[1..t]=p} for each prefix p of length t. On reading b at position t+1, update q_i to q_i AND [C_i[t+1]=b]. The update is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most K AND gates, with the comparison bits fixed by the family and position. For every prefix p, the maintained set is exactly Q(p), so Q(p) is nonempty iff p is extendible by a member of the listed family. Proof: Initially Q(empty)=[K]. If the invariant holds at length t, then an index remains after the update exactly when its function matched p and its next truth-table bit equals b, which is equivalent to matching p concatenated with b. Induction proves the invariant at every length. Each coordinate update uses one AND gate with a fixed comparison bit, hence at most K gates per transition. This statement gives no polynomial bound in s when K is the full family of size-s circuit descriptions.
scope: All finite N,K and any explicitly listed family of K Boolean truth tables; transition circuit uses the candidate-membership vector as its state and position-dependent fixed comparison bits.

structure.evidence: A finite exhaustive check was requested for N=2 and K<=3; its result is pending. The proof is the direct induction on prefix length given in the statement.
structure.gap: The full size-s circuit family has exponentially many descriptions, so this K-gate state update does not resolve whether EXT transitions have poly(s) real-gate cost or whether arbitrary MCSP decision circuits can implement them.

statement: statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-COFACTOR PROJECTION BOUND. Let H(x,w) be a Boolean function with w in {0,1}^r. Suppose the distinct functions among H_w(x)=H(x,w) are d functions, each computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most h gates. Then G(x)=exists w H(x,w) has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most d(h+1)-1 gates. Proof: Choose one witness assignment for each distinct cofactor function. Compute those d functions with separate circuits, then OR their outputs in a binary tree using d-1 additional gates. The resulting function is exactly G because duplicate cofactors do not change a disjunction. This bound gives no claim that d is small or efficiently computable.

label: S0978
statement: statement: PREFIX RESTRICTION MONOTONICITY FOR WITNESS COFACTOR COUNTS. Let H(x,w) be any Boolean function and, for each prefix p, define F_{p,w}(z)=H(pz,w). Let d_p be the number of distinct functions F_{p,w} over all witnesses w. For every next bit b, d_{pb} <= d_p. Proof: restriction R_b sends each parent function f(z) to f(bz'), and every child function is its parent's image under this map. Hence the child set is an image of the parent set, whose cardinality cannot increase. This is semantic; it asserts no efficient way to compute the classes or representatives.

label: S0979
statement: statement: BOUNDED-REMAINING-SUFFIX COFACTOR ENUMERATION. Let H:{0,1}^{t+q}×W→{0,1}, where W is finite, and let h be the gate size of a circuit for H. Given prefix p of length t, one can construct the exact projected cofactor G_p(z)=∨_{w∈W}H(pz,w) by enumerating all w and all z∈{0,1}^q, storing each truth table, deduplicating identical tables, and OR-ing one representative per distinct table. The construction uses O(|W|2^q(h+q+1)) time and at most d(h+1)-1 output gates, where d is the number of distinct cofactor tables. Proof: direct evaluation fills each table; equality of finite bit strings decides functional equality on the q-bit domain; deduplication preserves the disjunction; a binary OR tree combines the d retained functions. This is useful when |W|2^q is polynomial in the parameters, and gives no bound when q or |W| is large.

structure.gap: For EXT_{n,s}, the witness domain and remaining suffix are not known to satisfy |W|2^q=poly(s); find an EXT-specific representation that avoids this enumeration or establish a useful lower bound on the required update resources.

label: S0980
statement: statement: FINITE-DOMAIN PROJECTION CIRCUIT CONSTRUCTION (repaired explicit construction). Let H(x,w) be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, x=(u,z) with |z|=q, and W be an explicitly listed finite witness set of size M. For fixed u, G_u(z)=OR_{w in W} H(u,z,w) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most M(h+1)-1 gates: make one copy of H per w, substitute u,w by constants, and combine outputs with M-1 OR gates. Writing the construction takes O(M(h+q+|u|)) time under explicit circuit encoding. No truth-table synthesis is used; the bound is useful when M and h are polynomial in the target parameters.

statement: statement: RESIDUAL-LANGUAGE CHARACTERIZATION OF EXACT EXT STATES. Fix n,s and let T be the set of truth tables of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s. For every prefix p of length t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{2^n-t}: pz is in T}. In any deterministic exact streaming algorithm deciding whether each received prefix extends to a member of T, prefixes p,q that reach the same internal state must satisfy R_p=R_q. Conversely, the state R_p, updated on bit b by R_{pb}={z: bz is in R_p}, is sufficient to decide extendibility by testing whether R_p is nonempty. Proof: if R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference; after the identical continuation z, exactly one of pz,qz is extendible, so a deterministic machine in the same state could not answer both correctly. The update formula follows directly by decomposing a completing suffix after its first bit. This characterizes required information, but gives no compact encoding or efficient update bound.

label: S0983
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-STATE CHARACTERIZATION FOR FIXED-LENGTH LANGUAGES. Let N be a nonnegative integer and L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. Any deterministic exact recognizer that reads bits left to right and decides membership in L must be in different states after any two length-t prefixes p,q with R_p != R_q. Conversely, a recognizer whose states at depth t are the distinct residual sets R_p, and whose transition on b maps R_p to {z: bz in R_p}, decides L exactly. Thus the minimum number of reachable states at depth t is exactly the number of distinct residuals at that depth.
derivation: Necessity: if R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. If the machine had the same state after p and q, its deterministic continuation on z would have the same result, although exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L, contradiction. Sufficiency: after reading p, store R_p. On reading b, the residual becomes R_pb={z: pbz in L}={z: bz in R_p}, so the transition rule preserves the invariant that the state is the residual of the prefix read. At depth N the residual contains only the empty string when the full word is in L; accept in exactly that case. The two inequalities give the exact minimum state count.
scope: All finite fixed-length binary languages and every depth 0<=t<=N. The statement concerns abstract deterministic states; it gives no circuit-size bound for encoding residuals or implementing transitions, in particular no bounded-cost transformation from arbitrary MCSP decision circuits H_C.

label: S0984
statement:
statement: FIXED-DEPTH EXT RESIDUAL COUNT. Let F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N and 0 <= t <= N. For p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. Then the number of distinct sets R_p is at most |F|+1.
derivation: Let P+ be the length-t prefixes p with R_p nonempty. For each p in P+, choose f_p in F whose length-t prefix is p. Distinct prefixes yield distinct chosen words, so p -> f_p is injective and |P+| <= |F|. Every nonempty residual is realized by a prefix in P+, hence there are at most |F| distinct nonempty residuals. All empty residuals equal the empty set, adding at most one more. Thus the total is at most |F|+1. Distinct residual sets need not be disjoint; the proof uses only the injection from viable prefixes to F.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and all 0 <= t <= N; a state-count bound for the exact prefix automaton.

label: S0985
statement:
statement: RESIDUALS ARE EXACTLY THE FUTURE DISTINGUISHERS. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. Any deterministic left-to-right streaming recognizer correct for F must be in different internal states after prefixes p and q whenever R_p != R_q. If R_p=R_q, then p and q have the same acceptance outcome for every common suffix.
derivation: If R_p=R_q, then for every suffix z, pz is in F iff z is in R_p iff z is in R_q iff qz is in F. If R_p!=R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pz and qz is in F. If a deterministic recognizer were in the same state after p and q, processing the same suffix z from that state would produce the same final output on both inputs, contradicting correctness. Thus different residuals require different states, and equal residuals have identical future acceptance behavior. This identifies the exact future-membership information at depth t, without bounding the cost of computing transitions or total state count.
scope: All N>=0, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and fixed depths 0<=t<=N; deterministic left-to-right streaming recognizers with a common transition rule and correct final membership output.

label: S0986
statement:
statement: EXT STATE-BIT BOUND FROM CIRCUIT DESCRIPTIONS. Fix n,s>=0. Let F_{n,s} be the set of truth tables on {0,1}^n computed by Boolean circuits with at most s fan-in-at-most-two gates, where each gate is one of the 16 Boolean functions of two inputs, inputs may be chosen from the n variables, constants 0 and 1, or earlier gate outputs, and one output wire is selected. For every prefix depth t in [0,2^n], the number of distinct EXT residuals R_p={z in {0,1}^{2^n-t}: pz in F_{n,s}} is at most |F_{n,s}|+1, and hence can be represented by at most ceil(log2(|F_{n,s}|+1)) bits. In particular, this is O((s+1)log(n+s+2)) bits.
derivation: Put A=16(n+s+2)^2. A circuit with exactly k gates, for 0<=k<=s, has at most A^k possible ordered descriptions: for each gate there are 16 choices of Boolean function and at most (n+s+2)^2 choices of ordered input wires, an upper bound that allows unavailable future wires and therefore only overcounts. Its output wire has at most n+s+2 choices. Thus the number D of descriptions of circuits of size at most s is at most (n+s+2) sum_{k=0}^s A^k <= (s+1)(n+s+2)A^s. Every truth table in F_{n,s} has at least one such description, so |F_{n,s}|<=D. At depth t, each prefix with nonempty residual has an extension in F_{n,s}; choosing one extension for each such prefix is injective because distinct prefixes cannot be prefixes of the same word. Hence there are at most |F_{n,s}| distinct nonempty residuals, and all empty residuals coincide, giving at most |F_{n,s}|+1 residuals total. The required fixed-width encoding takes ceil(log2(|F_{n,s}|+1)) bits. Finally, log2(D+1)=O((s+1)log(n+s+2)) from the displayed bound and A=16(n+s+2)^2. This proves the claimed state-bit bound. It supplies no circuit for computing a residual transition from H_C and no transition gate-cost bound.
scope: All n,s>=0, this explicit fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit description model, and each fixed prefix depth. A bound on the number of semantic automaton states only; no claim about transition complexity or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S0987
statement:
statement: POLYNOMIAL-CARDINALITY CIRCUIT-UNION PROJECTION LEMMA. Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be a nonempty finite family of Boolean circuits on common input x, each with at most h fan-in-two gates; allow constants and input wiring for free. Define U(x)=1 iff C_i(x)=1 for some i. Then U has a fan-in-two circuit with at most M(h+1)-1 gates. For every fixed input prefix p, the cofactor U_p has a circuit with at most the same number of gates, and fixing one more input bit to obtain U_{pb} does not increase this bound. Consequently, if M and h are polynomially bounded in a parameter, then U and all its prefix cofactors have polynomial-size circuits. Proof: Copy each C_i separately and combine their outputs using a binary OR tree. The copies use at most Mh gates, and the OR tree uses M-1 gates, for a total Mh+M-1=M(h+1)-1. Substituting fixed prefix bits in a circuit only replaces input wires by constants, so cannot increase the number of gates; this applies again to the next bit. Polynomially bounded M and h make the displayed product polynomial. This lemma applies to an explicitly enumerable finite family; it gives no polynomial-size bound when M is exponential, as in the unrestricted family of size-s circuits.
derivation: For each member circuit take a disjoint copy; join the M outputs by a binary OR tree; hardwire prefix bits in the resulting circuit. The gate count is Mh+(M-1), and cofactors cannot have larger gate count.
scope: All integers M>=1,h>=0 and all finite families of Boolean circuits over a fan-in-two basis containing OR, with constants and input wiring free. Does not bound unrestricted EXT when its candidate family is exponential.

label: S0988
statement:
statement: EXT RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION. Let F be a finite family of Boolean functions on N-bit inputs, with truth tables in a fixed order, and let p be a prefix of length t that occurs as the first t bits of at least one member of F. Define R(p)={u in {0,1}^{2^N-t}: pu is the truth table of some f in F}. For V(p)={f in F: the truth table of f begins with p}, R(p) is exactly the union, over f in V(p), of the suffixes of f's truth table after position t. Consequently two occurring prefixes p,q (possibly of different lengths) have identical residual completion languages if and only if these unions of suffixes are equal. In particular, equality of candidate sets implies equality of residual languages, but equality of candidate sets is not necessary. Proof: A suffix u belongs to R(p) iff pu is the truth table of some f in F. This is equivalent to f belonging to V(p) and u being exactly the suffix of f after the prefix p. Taking the union over V(p) gives the first equality. Applying that equality to p and q proves the stated iff. The candidate-set map therefore gives a sufficient, possibly nonminimal, representation of the residual language.
derivation: Unpack membership in the residual completion language: an extension pu is a member truth table exactly when a family member has prefix p and suffix u. This is exactly the union of suffixes over V(p). Equality of residuals is therefore equivalent to equality of those unions; the map from candidate sets to unions can identify different sets.
scope: Every finite family of Boolean functions with a fixed truth-table order and every occurring prefix. This is an information characterization only; it makes no gate-complexity or transition-cost claim.

statement: statement: FINITE ENUMERATION TRANSITION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let F={w_1,...,w_M} be an explicitly listed set of distinct binary strings of common length L, and let D_t be the distinct length-t prefixes of strings in F. Encode each live prefix by an injective index in {0,...,|D_t|-1}, and reserve one additional index for dead. For each fixed t<L, the exact next-prefix transition (state i, input bit b) to the index of the length-(t+1) prefix if it exists in D_{t+1}, else dead, is computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates, with constants and wiring free. Proof: There are at most M live indices and one dead index. For each live i and b, the explicit list F determines a unique target index j or dead. A binary equality comparator between the state bits and fixed index i uses O(log(M+1)) gates; AND with the input literal selects the corresponding row. OR the selected indicators for each output bit, using O(M log(M+1)) gates in total, and similarly form dead's code. The dead row maps to dead and costs O(log(M+1)) gates. Since |D_t|<=M, the total is O((M+1)log(M+1)). This proves a transition circuit conditional on the family being explicitly listed; it does not bound the cost of generating that list, and for all size-<=s circuits M may be exponential in s log(n+s).

structure.evidence: A direct transition-table implementation uses at most M live indices plus a dead state and O(log(M+1)) bits. For each state and input bit the list specifies one target; selecting these rows and ORing target-code bits costs O(M log(M+1)) fan-in-two gates. This is a constructive upper bound for explicitly listed F only.

label: S0990
statement: statement: RESIDUAL-INDEXED TRANSITION CIRCUIT BOUND. Let F be a finite set of distinct binary strings of common length L. For 0<=t<L, let R_t be the set of distinct nonempty residual suffix languages after length-t prefixes, and let r_t=|R_t|. Index these states and reserve a dead state. The exact one-bit transition from a state R in R_t and bit b to {u: bu in R}, or to dead if this set is empty, has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O((r_t+1) log(r_t+2)) gates, with constants and wiring free. The transition table can be constructed from an explicit listing of F. Proof: For each R and b, its child {u:bu in R} depends only on R, not on the prefix representing it. It is therefore a unique member of R_{t+1} or empty. Decode each state code with an equality comparator, select the target code according to b, and OR the selected target bits for each output bit. There are 2r_t live rows, O(log(r_t+2)) code bits, and O(log(r_t+2)) gates per row/output selection, so the total is O((r_t+1) log(r_t+2)); add a dead row mapping to dead. This bounds circuit size only; table generation may depend on |F| and no polynomial bound follows for an implicit circuit family.

structure.evidence: Each target is the left quotient {u:bu in R}, determined solely by the residual language R. A direct decoded transition table therefore has 2r_t live rows and O(log(r_t+2)) bits per code.

statement: statement: PREFIX-MATCHING RELATION FROM A UNIVERSAL EVALUATOR. Let D be a finite set of descriptions, let P(d) be a Boolean predicate selecting the valid size-at-most-s candidates, and let U(d,x) be a Boolean circuit of u gates that outputs the truth-table bit of the circuit described by d on input x whenever P(d)=1. For any ordered list x_0,...,x_{k-1} of distinct inputs and bit string a in {0,1}^k, there is a Boolean circuit V_a(d) of at most k(u+1)+v+O(k) fan-in-two gates, where v is the size of P, such that V_a(d)=1 exactly when P(d)=1 and U(d,x_i)=a_i for every i<k. Consequently, existence of a size-at-most-s circuit matching the selected k truth-table positions is exactly the existential statement ∃d V_a(d)=1. Proof: Make k copies of U with x_i hardwired, negate each output whose desired bit a_i is 0, and AND all k literals with P(d). Hardwiring x_i adds no gates; each output negation costs at most one gate, and a fan-in-two conjunction of k+1 terms costs at most k gates. Thus the stated bound holds. The conclusion is an existential circuit encoding, not a procedure for eliminating d or producing an ordinary small circuit for the projected predicate on a.

Hardwiring x_i adds no gates; each output negation costs at most one gate, and a fan-in-two conjunction of k+1 terms costs at most k gates. Thus the stated bound holds. The conclusion is an existential circuit encoding, not a procedure for eliminating d or producing an ordinary small circuit for the projected predicate on a.

statement:
statement: DISTINCT-WITNESS-COFACTOR CIRCUIT BOUND. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For each w∈{0,1}^r define H_w(x)=H(x,w), and let q be the number of distinct Boolean functions among the H_w. Then G(x)=∃w H(x,w) has a fan-in-two circuit with at most qh+q−1 gates. For every fixed prefix p of the visible input x, the cofactor G_p has a circuit with at most qh+q−1 gates. Proof: Choose one witness representative for each distinct function H_w. For each of the q representatives, copy the circuit for H and hardwire that witness, using at most qh gates total. The OR of the q outputs is exactly ∨_w H_w(x), since every witness function occurs among the representatives; a binary OR tree uses q−1 gates. Hardwiring a visible prefix in this circuit cannot increase its gate count. This is an existence bound only: it gives no efficient method to find representatives and no bound on q for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement: statement: RESIDUAL-SET CHARACTERIZATION OF EXACT ONE-PASS STATES. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz in L}. In any deterministic one-pass machine recognizing L exactly, prefixes p,q with R_p != R_q reach different states. Thus the machine has at least as many states as there are distinct residual sets. Conversely, the machine whose states are the distinct residual sets (with level/remaining-length implicit) and whose transition on b maps R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p} recognizes L exactly. Proof: if R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference; exactly one of pz,qz lies in L, so equal machine states would imply equal outcomes after the common continuation z, contradiction. For the converse, maintain the current residual set; its update is exactly the displayed restriction, and at length N accept iff the empty continuation belongs to it. This is a semantic state characterization only and provides no real-gate bound for updating the representation.

statement:
statement: BOUNDED-WITNESS PROJECTION CIRCUIT. Let H(x,w) be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates, where x has N bits and w has r bits. Define G(x)=OR_{w in {0,1}^r} H(x,w). Then G has a fan-in-two circuit of at most 2^r(h+1)-1 gates. For any fixed prefix p of x, the cofactor G_p has a circuit of no greater size, and the child cofactor G_{pb} is obtained by fixing the next visible input bit without increasing size. Consequently, if r <= c log_2(h+1) for a fixed constant c, G has polynomial size at most (h+1)^{c+1}. Proof: For every witness w, copy H and hardwire w, using h gates. Combine the 2^r outputs by a binary OR tree using 2^r-1 gates. The sum is 2^r h+2^r-1. Fixing visible input bits only substitutes constants into this circuit, so cannot increase gate count. Finally 2^r <= (h+1)^c under the hypothesis, yielding the stated polynomial bound. This applies to a fixed verifier with logarithmically many witness bits relative to its gate count; for H_C, tableau witnesses have g bits and the bound remains exponential in g, so it does not solve the arbitrary-MCSP transition-cost bridge.
derivation: Expand existential quantification over all 2^r assignments to w by a disjunction of 2^r independently hardwired copies of H; cofactoring preserves gate count. Under r<=c log2(h+1), the explicit bound is polynomial.
scope: All finite Boolean circuits with constants and wiring free; fan-in-two gates. The polynomial conclusion requires the stated witness-width condition and does not apply to arbitrary H_C tableaux.

label: S0996
statement:
statement: DESCRIPTION-ONLY EXISTENTIAL WITNESS FOR EXT. Fix a canonical encoding d of fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits with at most s gates on n inputs, with encoding length L=O(s log(n+s)); invalid encodings are rejected. For each valid d and input x, let y list one output bit per gate, and let H(d,x,y) assert all gate equations and that the output is 1. Then for every x, exists d exists y H(d,x,y) iff exists valid d such that C_d(x)=1. Consequently, for every prefix p, exists z exists d exists y H(d,pz,y) iff exists z exists valid d such that C_d(pz)=1. Proof: Fix valid d and x. Induct through the gates in topological order: each local equation uniquely forces the next gate-output bit, so exactly one tableau y satisfies all gate equations, namely the evaluation of C_d(x). The output condition accepts this tableau iff C_d(x)=1. Taking the existential quantifiers over d and z preserves the equivalence. Thus the tableau contributes no independent witness choice; the remaining existential choice is the circuit description. This does not provide a polynomial-size ordinary Boolean circuit for projecting over all descriptions d or for updating EXT residuals.
derivation: For each fixed valid description d and input x, gate equations uniquely determine the tableau by topological induction. Therefore existentially quantifying y is exactly evaluation of C_d(x); then quantify over d and, for prefix predicates, over suffix z.
scope: Finite fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuits under the stated canonical encoding, with gate outputs represented explicitly; applies to every input and fixed prefix. No gate bound for projection over descriptions is claimed.
obstacle: The remaining existential projection over all circuit descriptions and suffixes has no polynomial ordinary-gate implementation bound established here.
attack: Use this witness reduction to isolate the circuit-description projection; seek either a compact representation/update for that projection or a lower bound for this specific residual representation.
target_relevance: Shrinks the EXT tableau-witness formulation by showing that gate tableau bits are functionally determined, while identifying the unresolved cost as projection over candidate circuit descriptions.

label: S0997
statement:
statement: PREFIX-FEASIBILITY OR RECURRENCE FOR A FIXED VERIFIER. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be any Boolean relation, and define E(p)=1 iff there exist a suffix z of length N−|p| and witness w∈{0,1}^r such that H(pz,w)=1. For every prefix p with |p|<N, E(p)=E(p0)∨E(p1). At length N, E(p)=1 iff some w satisfies H(p,w)=1. Proof: Every suffix z of positive length has a unique first bit b∈{0,1} and a remaining suffix z′. Thus a pair (z,w) witnessing E(p) yields a witness for E(pb), where b is that first bit. Conversely, a witness (z′,w) for E(pb) gives the suffix bz′ witnessing E(p). Taking the disjunction over the two possible first bits proves the recurrence. When |p|=N there is no suffix variable, leaving exactly the stated witness condition. This is an exact semantic recurrence; it supplies neither a small ordinary circuit for E nor a bound on the cost of computing either child from a representation of H.
derivation: Partition the existential suffix assignments by their first bit. Each assignment belongs to exactly one part; the witness variable is unchanged in either part. The full-length boundary case has an empty suffix, so only the witness remains.
scope: All finite N,r, Boolean relations H and prefixes p. Gate complexity of the projected predicate and transition cost are not asserted.

label: S0998
statement:
statement: TRUTH-TABLE RESIDUAL ENCODING AND HALVING UPDATE. Let G:{0,1}^N→{0,1} be any Boolean predicate and, for a prefix p of length t, let R_p:{0,1}^{N-t}→{0,1} be R_p(z)=G(pz). Store R_p by its truth vector in lexicographic suffix order, using exactly 2^{N-t} bits. For t<N, the vectors for R_{p0} and R_{p1} are respectively the first and second halves of the vector for R_p; thus either one-child update is obtained by selecting a half, with zero Boolean gates and O(2^{N-t}) bit reads/copies in an explicit bit-array representation. At t=N, the vector has one bit and equals G(p). Proof: list suffixes z of length N-t in lexicographic order. The suffixes of R_{p0} are exactly the strings 0z in the first half of the parent’s ordered suffix list, and those of R_{p1} are exactly the strings 1z in the second half. Evaluating R_p on each listed suffix gives G(pz), which is precisely the child vector entries in order. At full length the only suffix is the empty string, so the sole entry is G(p). This representation is exact and has exponential worst-case storage; it gives no polynomial transition or construction bound from a succinct circuit for G or from H_C.
derivation: Explicitly encode each residual function by all of its suffix values; lexicographic suffix order partitions by first suffix bit into two equal contiguous blocks, which are the child residual truth vectors.
scope: All N≥0, all Boolean predicates G, and all prefixes p of length 0..N. Update cost is stated as bit-array access/copy cost, not Boolean gate complexity.

label: S0999
statement:
statement: LIVE-PREFIX COUNT BOUND FOR A FINITE LANGUAGE. Let N be a nonnegative integer and L be a subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N, let T_t={p in {0,1}^t : there exists z in {0,1}^{N-t} with pz in L}. Then |T_t|<=min(2^t,|L|), and the total number of live-prefix nodes in the trie of L is at most sum_{t=0}^N min(2^t,|L|). Proof: The ambient set {0,1}^t has size 2^t. For each p in T_t choose one extension w_p in L. If p and q are distinct length-t strings, no length-N string can extend both, so w_p != w_q. Thus p -> w_p is an injection T_t -> L, proving |T_t|<=|L| as well. Summing the level bounds proves the total bound. For L equal to the set of truth tables of circuits in any fixed finite description class, this yields an upper bound by replacing |L| with the number of circuit descriptions. It gives no bound on ordinary Boolean-gate cost for updating a succinct representation.
derivation: At each depth t, count prefixes both by the full binary level and by an injection that sends each live prefix to one distinct accepted string extending it; sum over depths.
scope: All finite N and all L subset {0,1}^N, including L empty. Counts trie nodes only; no circuit transition complexity is asserted.

structure.evidence: The proof is an injection/counting argument. The prior finite recurrence experiment cm-d1d0c95223694b26 is not used as a premise.

label: S1000
statement:
statement: EXT CONTINUATION-EQUIVALENCE LEMMA. Let L be any language of finite binary strings and let A be a deterministic streaming automaton that reads strings left to right and decides L at end of input. For each prefix p, define its residual language R_p={z in {0,1}*: pz in L}. If A reaches the same state after prefixes p and q, then R_p=R_q. Conversely, if R_p=R_q for all prefixes p,q that reach one given state partition, the quotient whose states are the distinct residual languages R_p, with transition delta(R_p,b)=R_{pb}, is well-defined and recognizes L. Proof: If A(p)=A(q) as states, determinism implies that for each suffix z, processing z from that state yields the same final decision; hence pz is in L iff qz is in L, so R_p=R_q. For the converse, if R_p=R_q then for each bit b and suffix z, pbz in L iff p(bz) in L iff q(bz) in L iff qbz in L; thus R_{pb}=R_{qb}, so delta is independent of the representative. The initial state is R_empty. After reading p the quotient state is R_p by induction on |p|, and at end it accepts exactly when the empty string belongs to R_p, equivalently p in L. Therefore every correct deterministic streaming implementation of EXT must distinguish any pair of prefixes p,q for which there exists a suffix z with EXT(pz) != EXT(qz); these residual languages are the exact semantic information in its state. This makes no assertion about the number of residuals or the Boolean circuit/gate complexity of computing delta.
derivation: Use determinism to show equal reached states give equal outcomes on every common continuation. For the quotient construction, verify that appending one bit preserves residual equality, then induct over the input and use epsilon membership as the accepting condition.
scope: All languages L subseteq {0,1}* and deterministic streaming automata; applies to EXT_{n,s} on its fixed-length truth-table prefixes by restricting suffixes to the remaining length. It characterizes semantic state only; it gives no real-gate transition bound and no lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

statement:
statement: COMPATIBLE-CIRCUIT SET UPDATE LEMMA. Let F be any finite indexed family of Boolean circuits C_i:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, i in I, and let L_F={x in {0,1}^N: C_i(x)=1 for some i in I}. For each prefix p of length t define I_p={i in I: C_i(pz)=1 for some z in {0,1}^{N-t}}. Then for every bit b, I_{pb}={i in I_p: there exists z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} with C_i(pb z')=1}; in particular I_{pb} is computable from I_p by filtering each surviving index according to whether its circuit has an accepting completion under the extended prefix. Moreover p has an accepting completion in L_F iff I_p is nonempty. Proof: If i∈I_{pb}, then pbz' is an accepting completion for C_i, hence p(bz') witnesses i∈I_p; also its first suffix bit is b, so i passes the stated filter. Conversely, if i∈I_p and C_i has an accepting completion with next bit b, write that completion uniquely as bz'; then i∈I_{pb}. The final equivalence follows directly from the existential definitions and finiteness of I. This yields an exact streaming representation using a subset of I as its semantic state, with at most 2^{|I|} raw states; it does not give a bounded fan-in circuit cost for the filtering predicate from H_C, nor a bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Expand the existential quantifier over the suffix into its first bit and remaining suffix. Both inclusions follow by concatenation/decomposition of that suffix. Nonemptiness is equivalent to the existential choice of a family index and accepting completion.

statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE BITSET UPDATE LEMMA. Let C={c_1,...,c_M} be an explicitly listed family of strings in {0,1}^N. statement:
statement: EXACT PREFIX-COFACTOR IDENTITY FOR EXISTENTIAL WITNESS RELATIONS. Let D,Y,Z be finite sets, let H:D×{0,1}^N×Y→{0,1}, and define E(p)=1 iff there exist d∈D, y∈Y, and z∈{0,1}^{N-|p|} such that H(d,pz,y)=1, for every prefix p of length at most N. If |p|<N and b∈{0,1}, then E(pb)=1 iff there exist d∈D, y∈Y, and z'∈{0,1}^{N-|p|-1} such that H(d,pbz',y)=1. Proof: By definition, E(pb)=1 exactly when there exist d,y and a suffix w of length N-|p|-1 with H(d,(pb)w,y)=1. Concatenation is associative, so (pb)w=p(bw), where bw has length N-|p|. Thus this condition is exactly the defining condition E(p)=1 witnessed by the suffix bw whose first bit is b. Conversely, any suffix z of length N-|p| witnessing E(p)=1 and beginning with b has the form bz', and then H(d,pbz',y)=1 witnesses the right-hand side. This is an exact identity for the semantic prefix projection. It gives no Boolean-circuit size bound for computing E or its transitions.
derivation: Expand both sides using the existential definition of E; split a suffix of length N−|p| into its first bit b and the remaining suffix, and use associativity of concatenation. The reverse implication uses the same decomposition in reverse.
scope: All finite D,Y, all N≥1, all H:D×{0,1}^N×Y→{0,1}, and all prefixes p with |p|<N. No circuit-complexity claim is made.

label: S1004
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-LANGUAGE DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND FOR EXACT STREAMING. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and L_F={p in {0,1}^{<=N}: p is a prefix of some x in F}. For each prefix p with |p|<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz in F}. In any deterministic streaming machine that reads the N bits left-to-right and at each position retains a state such that its final acceptance decides membership in F, if two same-length prefixes p,q have R_p != R_q, then the machine must be in different states after p and q. Consequently, at depth t it needs at least |{R_p: p in {0,1}^t}| states (and at least the maximum of these quantities over t). Proof: Since R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to F. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism implies that processing the common continuation z leads to the same final state and acceptance in both cases, contradicting exact decision. Thus distinct residual sets force distinct states. Counting the equivalence classes gives the stated lower bound.
derivation: For same-length prefixes with different residual sets, choose a suffix in their symmetric difference. Determinism makes equal states remain equal under that shared suffix, contradicting exact acceptance. Counting residual classes gives the lower bound.
scope: Every finite N and every F subset of {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass left-to-right exact streaming. The bound concerns state count only; it says nothing about transition circuit cost or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1005
statement:
statement: GENERIC CIRCUIT IMPLEMENTATION OF FINITE-STATE TRANSITIONS. Let Q be a state set of size m>=2, encode its states injectively in k=ceil(log2 m) bits, and let delta:Q x {0,1}->Q be any deterministic transition function. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit on the k state bits and one input bit that agrees with delta on every valid encoded state, with O(k^2 m) gates. Proof: For each output bit j, take the disjunction over all pairs (q,b) whose next state has bit j equal to 1, of the conjunction testing that the state input equals the code of q and that the input bit equals b. Each test uses O(k) fan-in-two gates, there are at most 2m terms, and the disjunction uses O(m) gates. Thus each output bit costs O(km), and all k output bits cost O(k^2m). Values on invalid state codes may be arbitrary. This is an upper bound for a fixed transition table, not a lower bound and not a polynomial-in-log(m) bound.
derivation: Explicit DNF for each output bit: enumerate the at most 2m valid state/input pairs yielding 1, test each pair with O(k) fan-in-two gates, OR the terms, and repeat for k outputs.
scope: Every finite deterministic state transition system with m>=2 states, binary input alphabet, injective k-bit state encoding. Does not address how EXT's transition table is computed, nor arbitrary algorithms' representations.

label: S1006
statement:
statement: WIRING-ONLY TRANSITION FOR CHARACTERISTIC-VECTOR RESIDUALS. Let N≥1 and F⊆{0,1}^N. At level t, for each prefix p∈{0,1}^t encode its residual R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pz∈F} by the characteristic vector v_p indexed by {0,1}^{N−t}. For b∈{0,1}, the vector v_pb is obtained from v_p by selecting coordinates bz, for z∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}, and deleting the initial b from each coordinate label. Thus the transition from v_p on input b to v_pb is a coordinate-selection wiring map with zero Boolean gates. The encoding uses 2^{N−t} bits at level t; consequently this is an exact but generally noncompact representation and gives no compact-state transition-cost bound for EXT.
derivation: For every suffix z of length N−t−1, the coordinate of v_pb indexed by z equals 1 iff pbz∈F. The coordinate of v_p indexed by bz equals 1 iff p(bz)∈F. Since pbz=p(bz), these bits agree. Hence all child coordinates are obtained by selecting the indicated parent coordinates; selection and relabeling require only wires. The vector length is the number 2^{N−t} of suffixes at the parent level.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N, N≥1, all levels t<N and all prefixes p of length t. Exactness is unconditional. The transition is gate-free only in the explicit characteristic-vector representation, whose width is exponential in remaining suffix length; no bound for the compact EXT state representation is asserted.

label: S1007
statement:
statement: COUNTING-PRESERVING TABLEAU ENCODING FOR A FIXED CIRCUIT. Let C be a fixed acyclic Boolean circuit with N inputs and g fan-in-at-most-two gates in topological order. Introduce one Boolean variable y_i for each gate output. Let H_C(x,y) be the conjunction of the local gate equations and the condition that C's output is 1. Then H_C has O(g) fan-in-two Boolean gates (with constants and wiring free), and # {(x,y) in {0,1}^{N+g}: H_C(x,y)=1} = # {x in {0,1}^N: C(x)=1}.
derivation: For each input x, induct through the gates in topological order. Once the input bits and earlier gate outputs are fixed, the local equation for gate i uniquely forces y_i to the value of that gate. Thus exactly one y satisfies all local gate equations: C's evaluation tableau on x. This tableau satisfies the output condition iff C(x)=1. Consequently, each accepting x contributes exactly one satisfying pair (x,y), and each rejecting x contributes none, proving the counting identity. A gate's local equation involves at most three bits and has a constant-size Boolean implementation; combining the g equations and the output condition with a binary AND tree uses O(g) gates.
scope: All finite N and g, for one fixed acyclic fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit. This does not bound existential elimination of y or quantification over candidate circuit descriptions.

statement: statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY RESIDUAL FILTERING LEMMA. Let N>=1 and let F=(f_1,...,f_K) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on {0,1}^N, each given by its full truth table. For a prefix p in {0,1}^t define I(p)={i: f_i begins with p}. For t<N and b in {0,1}, I(pb)={i in I(p): f_i(t+1)=b}, where f_i(t+1) denotes the truth-table bit at the next position. Thus the K-bit indicator of I(pb) is obtained from that of I(p) by K AND gates when the K next-bit tests are supplied as inputs. Proof: For each i, membership in I(pb) is equivalent to agreement with p and agreement with the next bit b. The first condition is i in I(p); the second is the supplied test f_i(t+1)=b. Conjoining these per index gives the identity and the stated circuit. The lemma concerns explicit truth tables with supplied tests; it does not give a circuit generating those tests from p and does not apply to the implicit family of all size-s circuits.

statement: statement: BOUNDED-WITNESS PROJECTION CONSTRUCTION. Let H:{0,1}^u x {0,1}^r -> {0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates, with constants and wiring free. Define G(x)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(x,w)=1. Then G has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^r(h+1)-1 gates. For each fixed prefix p of x, the cofactor G_p has a circuit with no more gates, and either child cofactor G_{pb} can be obtained by hardwiring b with no added gates. Proof: For each w, copy the h-gate circuit H and hardwire its witness inputs to w. OR the 2^r outputs using a binary tree of 2^r-1 OR gates. This constructs G with 2^r h + 2^r-1 gates. Hardwiring visible input bits preserves the function and cannot add gates; applying it to the child bit proves the cofactor assertion. This is a constructive cost bound for bounded witness length r, with an explicit exponential dependence on r.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL AUTOMATON CHARACTERIZATION. Let L be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. In any deterministic exact streaming recognizer whose state after reading p determines acceptance for every continuation z, prefixes with distinct residuals R_p must reach distinct states. Conversely, the residuals at all depths form an exact recognizer: on bit b, R_p transitions to D_b(R_p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R_p}, and this equals R_{pb}; at depth N, accept iff the empty string belongs to R_p. Proof: If R_p and R_q differ, choose z in their symmetric difference. A deterministic recognizer in the same state after p and q would give the same acceptance on continuation z, contradicting the definition of residual. For the converse, if R_p=R_q, then for each b and z, bz belongs to R_p iff z belongs to D_b(R_p), so D_b(R_p)=D_b(R_q); hence transitions are well-defined on residual classes. The identity D_b(R_p)=R_{pb} follows directly from p(bz)=(pb)z. Induction on the number of remaining bits shows that the residual state accepts exactly the continuations completing a word of L. The terminal rule is precisely membership of the empty continuation. For L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), this characterizes the exact information an EXT prefix state must preserve, but does not bound the Boolean gate cost of computing a transition from H_C or imply anything about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Distinct residuals are separated by a continuation in their symmetric difference, so exact deterministic recognition requires distinct states. Equality of residual sets is a right congruence under the left-derivative operation D_b; direct concatenation gives D_b(R_p)=R_{pb}. The terminal empty-string test and induction establish exact recognition.
scope: All finite N and all L subset {0,1}^N; deterministic exact one-pass recognition of fixed-length words. Applied to EXT with L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), it identifies required residual information only; no transition circuit or general MCSP lower bound is claimed.

statement: statement: FULL PREFIX REGISTER UPDATE LEMMA. Fix N>=1 and a time layer t in {0,...,N-1}. Encode a length-t prefix p as an N-bit vector q with q_i=p_i for 0<=i<t and q_i=0 for t<=i<N; the layer t is part of the recognizer's control (so this is a layered transition, not one time-homogeneous map). On input b, the next encoded prefix is q'_i=q_i for i<t, q'_t=b, and q'_i=0 for i>t. Each output bit is computed by a fan-in-two {AND,OR,NOT} circuit of at most one gate (indeed q'_i=q_i for i<t, q'_t=b, and q'_i=0 for i>t, so constants/wires suffice); hence total transition circuit cost is O(N), with zero nontrivial gates if wires and constants are free. The encoding is exact: induction on t gives q=(p,0^{N-t}) after every legal prefix. Given any fixed Boolean relation H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, the represented continuation predicate R_q(z)=1 iff exists w H(qz,w) is therefore updated exactly to R_{pb} by this transition. Proof: the coordinate equations copy the old prefix, append b at the unique next coordinate, and zero all unused coordinates; the induction establishes the invariant, and substitution into the definition gives R_{q'}(z)=exists w H(pb z,w). This result only bounds updates for the redundant full-prefix representation; it gives no bound for transitions on the succinct residual-state encoding of EXT, nor for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1014
statement:
statement: REPAIRED PADDED-PREFIX UPDATE LEMMA. Let N>=1, let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, and at layer t in {0,...,N} encode p in {0,1}^t by q=(p,0^{N-t}) in {0,1}^N. Define comp_t(q,z) in {0,1}^N for z in {0,1}^{N-t} by comp_t(q,z)_i=q_i for i<t and comp_t(q,z)_i=z_{i-t} for t<=i<N. Define F_t(q,z)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(comp_t(q,z),w)=1. For t<N and b in {0,1}, define q' by q'_i=q_i for i<t, q'_t=b, and q'_i=0 for i>t. Then q'=(pb,0^{N-t-1}) and for every z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, F_{t+1}(q',z')=F_t(q,bz'). The update on legal layer-t encodings has coordinate outputs that are wires/constants except coordinate t, which is b; its circuit uses zero nontrivial gates when wires and constants are free, or O(N) gates if output copies/constants are charged. Proof: Since q=(p,0^{N-t}), coordinatewise definition gives comp_t(q,bz')=pbz'=comp_{t+1}(q',z'). Existential quantification over the same w therefore gives equality of the F values. The coordinate formula for q' establishes the invariant at layer t+1. This is only a redundant full-prefix encoding; it makes no claim about bounded-cost updates on a succinct residual-state encoding or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: For legal q=(p,0^{N-t}), the first t coordinates of comp_t(q,bz') are p, and the remaining coordinates are bz'. Thus comp_t(q,bz')=pbz'. The updated legal register q' stores pb followed by zeros, so comp_{t+1}(q',z')=pbz' as well. H receives identical input vectors and the same witness domain {0,1}^r, hence the existential predicates are equal. The update coordinate equations give the stated gate cost.
scope: All finite N>=1, layers t<N, Boolean relations H with arbitrary fixed witness length r; deterministic layered updates on the padded-prefix register. No succinct-state or arbitrary-MCSP lower-bound implication.

label: S1015
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-COUNT TWO-SIDED BOUND. Let N>=0, L be a subset of {0,1}^N, and for t in {0,...,N} define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for each p in {0,1}^t. Let d_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_p. Then d_t <= min(2^t, |L|). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so d_t<=2^t. For each distinct nonempty residual R choose one prefix p_R realizing it. Distinct residuals have distinct chosen prefixes, since one fixed prefix determines exactly one set R_p. Choose any z_R in R. The words p_R z_R are distinct because their length-t prefixes p_R are distinct, and each belongs to L. This injects the d_t residuals into L, giving d_t<=|L|. Thus d_t<=min(2^t,|L|). This does not imply d_t<=2^{N-t}: residuals are subsets of the suffix universe, not suffixes.
derivation: Count the 2^t prefixes. Then choose one realizing prefix for each distinct nonempty residual; these prefixes must be distinct. Choosing one accepted suffix for each residual maps each residual to a distinct word in L, proving d_t<=|L|. Combining the bounds gives the result.
scope: All finite binary languages L subseteq {0,1}^N and all cut depths t. This bounds nonempty residual-state count but not transition circuit cost or the size of the bound for circuit-truth-table languages.

label: S1016
statement:
statement: LAYERED RESIDUAL RECOGNIZER LEMMA. Let N>=0 and L be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each t=0,...,N and p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}; let D_t={R_p:p in {0,1}^t}, including the empty residual if it occurs. There is an exact layered deterministic recognizer for L whose states at layer t are D_t and whose transition on b in {0,1} is delta_t(R,b)={z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz' in R} for t<N. Its terminal state R at layer N accepts iff the empty word belongs to R. At each layer |D_t|<=min(2^t,|L|)+1, so the total number of layer-state pairs is at most (N+1)(|L|+1). Proof: For each reachable state R=R_p, delta_t(R_p,b)={z': bz' in R_p}={z': pbz' in L}=R_{pb}; thus the transition is well-defined on residual sets, independent of which prefix represents the state, and induction on t shows the state after p is exactly R_p. At t=N the suffix universe consists only of the empty word, so membership of that word in R_p is equivalent to p in L. For the count, the nonempty residuals number at most min(2^t,|L|) by S1015's injection argument; there is at most one additional empty residual. Summing the per-layer bounds gives at most (N+1)(|L|+1) layer-state pairs. This is a state-count and semantic-transition result; it does not bound the Boolean circuit cost of implementing delta_t on a succinct encoding.
derivation: For any p,b, membership z' in delta_t(R_p,b) is equivalent in sequence to bz' in R_p, pbz' in L, and z' in R_{pb}; hence delta_t(R_p,b)=R_{pb}. This proves well-defined transitions and the recognizer invariant by induction. Terminal acceptance follows from the definition at suffix length zero. The per-layer bound follows from at most min(2^t,|L|) nonempty residuals plus at most one empty residual; summing N+1 layers yields the stated total.
scope: All finite fixed-length binary languages L and N>=0. Counts layered state pairs; no ordinary-gate transition-cost or MCSP implication is asserted.

label: S1017
statement:
statement: BINARY DFA TRANSITION CIRCUIT UPPER BOUND. Let A=(Q,{0,1},δ,q0,F) be any deterministic finite automaton with q≥1 states, and encode states by distinct k-bit strings where k=ceil(log2 q) (with k=0 if q=1). For each input symbol b∈{0,1}, the map δ_b on valid state codes, extended arbitrarily to unused k-bit codes, is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(qk+q) gates; hence one transition circuit taking (state,b) and outputting the next state uses O(q log(q+1)) gates. Proof: For each valid state code a and output coordinate j, form its equality indicator e_a(state)=∧_{i=1}^k (state_i if a_i=1 else ¬state_i), using O(k) gates per code. For each output coordinate j, form y_j=∨_{a∈Q: δ(a,b)_j=1} e_a(state), requiring O(q) gates after the indicators. Compute both b-specific outputs and select by b with one mux per output coordinate, O(k) additional gates. Total O(qk+q); q=1 is constant. The circuit agrees with δ on every valid code; unused codes may be assigned arbitrary behavior. This gives a general construction but for EXT, q may be as large as the number of distinct prefix residuals, which is not shown polynomial in n,s, so it does not close the arbitrary-MCSP transition-cost gap.
derivation: One-hot equality tests for all q valid k-bit codes cost O(qk). For each symbol and coordinate, OR the indicators of states whose transition output has that coordinate set; this costs O(qk) total over k coordinates and two symbols. The transition symbol selects between the two output words with O(k) gates. Overall O(qk+q), and valid-state correctness follows because exactly one equality indicator is true.
scope: All finite DFAs over a binary alphabet, ordinary fan-in-two Boolean circuits, binary state encoding; no assertion on the size of the EXT residual automaton.

label: S1018
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL SUFFICIENCY AND CHILD UPDATE LEMMA. Let N,r be nonnegative integers and H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1}. For each prefix p∈{0,1}^t, 0≤t≤N, define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}: ∃w∈{0,1}^r H(pz,w)=1}. Then for every p of length t<N and b∈{0,1}, R_{pb}={z∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bz∈R_p}. Consequently R_p alone is sufficient to determine the next residual set after reading b: the update is the left quotient b^{-1}R_p. Proof: Fix p,b,z. By definition, z∈R_{pb} iff ∃w H(pb z,w)=1. Since bz is a length-(N−t) string, the definition of R_p says exactly that bz∈R_p iff ∃w H(p(bz),w)=1. These predicates are identical for every z, so the sets are equal. The right side depends only on R_p and b, hence equal residual sets have equal child residuals for each common next bit. This proves exact semantic state sufficiency for the projection automaton. It does not bound the cost of representing R_p or computing its quotient from a circuit description H in an ordinary fan-in-two circuit model.
derivation: Pointwise membership equivalence: z∈R_{pb} iff ∃w H(pb z,w) iff bz∈R_p. Extensional equality follows; the quotient is a function of R_p and b.
scope: All finite N,r, all Boolean relations H, all prefixes shorter than N; semantic residual states only, with no circuit-cost assertion.

label: S1019
statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-AGREEMENT FILTERING LEMMA. Let N be a positive integer and let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be any fixed finite list of Boolean functions f_j:{0,1}^N->{0,1}. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, define A_p={j in [M]: f_j(pz)=p_i for every i in [t], where z is the suffix completing pz to length N}; equivalently, j is live iff f_j agrees with p on the t queried inputs. After observing the next input string x_t (the t-th point in a fixed ordering x_1,...,x_{2^N} of {0,1}^N) and its target bit b_t, update each flag a_j to a'_j=a_j AND [f_j(x_t)=b_t]. Then the updated flags encode exactly A_{p'} for the extended observation prefix p'=(p,b_t). A synchronous fan-in-two Boolean circuit implements this update using at most 2M gates when the comparison bits [f_j(x_t)=b_t] are fixed constants for this time step. Proof: Initially all flags are 1, so A_empty=[M]. Suppose inductively that a_j=1 exactly for candidates agreeing with all earlier observed pairs (x_i,b_i), i<t. The update sets a'_j=1 exactly when that condition holds and f_j(x_t)=b_t, which is precisely agreement on all pairs through t. Each coordinate is one AND with a fixed bit (or a wire/constant); even charging one equality-to-constant AND and one combining AND gives at most 2M fan-in-two gates. This establishes the invariant by induction. Scope: fixed finite candidate list and fixed time-step comparison constants. The bound is O(M), with no assertion that M is polynomial in n,s, that comparisons can be generated cheaply, or that the state represents arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Induct on the number t of observations. Base: no observations leaves every candidate live. Step: retain candidate j exactly when it was previously live and its fixed prediction on x_t equals the observed b_t. This is exactly the defining condition for agreement on the extended prefix. Coordinatewise AND with a fixed comparison bit gives a fan-in-two implementation using at most 2M gates.

label: S1020
statement:
statement: REPAIRED CANDIDATE-AGREEMENT FILTERING LEMMA. Let X be a finite set, let F=(f_1,...,f_M) be a fixed finite list of functions f_j:X->{0,1}, and let H_t=((x_1,b_1),...,(x_t,b_t)) be any finite history in X×{0,1}. Define a_j(0)=1 and a_j(t+1)=a_j(t) AND [f_j(x_{t+1})=b_{t+1}]. Then for every j and t, a_j(t)=1 iff f_j(x_i)=b_i for every i≤t. Consequently the vector (a_1(t),...,a_M(t)) exactly represents the set of candidates consistent with H_t. If each comparison bit [f_j(x_{t+1})=b_{t+1}] is supplied as a constant, the update is implemented by at most M fan-in-two AND gates. Proof: Induct on t. At t=0, the history is empty and every candidate is consistent, matching a_j(0)=1. Suppose the equivalence holds at t. By definition, a_j(t+1)=1 iff a_j(t)=1 and f_j(x_{t+1})=b_{t+1}. Applying the induction hypothesis, this is equivalent to agreement on all pairs through t+1. One AND gate computes each coordinate from its prior flag and supplied comparison bit, for M gates total.
derivation: Induction on history length; each update conjoins precisely the newest agreement predicate.
scope: All finite X, all M≥0, arbitrary histories including inconsistent histories; the comparison predicates are assumed supplied. This repairs the mixed prefix/history wording in S1019 but does not bound comparison generation or arbitrary MCSP transition cost.

statement: FIXED-WIDTH PREFIX SHIFT-REGISTER LEMMA. Let N>=1 and H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1} be any Boolean relation. A layered machine with state (a,u) in {0,1}^N x {0,1}^{N+1}, initialized (0^N,e_0), after t bits p=b_1...b_t stores a=0^{N-t}p and u=e_t. On input b its transition is a'=a_2...a_N b and u'=shift(u), so every next-state output is a current bit, input bit, or constant: zero fan-in-two Boolean gates when wires/constants are free. At layer t, decode p as the last t bits of a and represent R(z)=1 iff exists w in {0,1}^r H(pz,w). This is exactly the existential prefix residual, and the transition on b represents the child residual. Proof: induction on t; the initial state stores the empty prefix. Shifting and appending b transforms 0^{N-t}p into 0^{N-t-1}pb and shifts e_t to e_{t+1}. The residual identity follows by substitution into its definition. This gives zero-gate transitions only for an explicit O(N)-bit encoding. For EXT, N=2^m, so it implies neither a poly(m,s)-bit state bound nor a transition bound for compact residual encodings or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

structure.evidence: Induction verifies the prefix invariant at each layer; each next-state bit is a wire, input, or constant, hence zero gates under the stated circuit convention. Existential projection is exact by the residual definition. State uses N+(N+1) bits, exponential in m when N=2^m.

label: S1022
statement:
statement: LAYERED DFA TRANSITION-CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let q>=2 and let a layered deterministic automaton over alphabet {0,1} have at most q states in each layer, with a specified initial state and a specified accepting subset at the final layer. There is an encoding of each layer's states by r=ceil(log2 q) bits such that each layer transition and the final acceptance test are computed by fan-in-two Boolean circuits using O(q log q) gates per layer. Proof: Pad each layer to q states and define transitions arbitrarily from padded states. For each state i, compute the equality selector e_i on the r state bits; each selector uses O(r) gates, so all q selectors use O(qr) gates. For each input symbol b and each next-state output bit k, OR the selectors e_i for which the transition from i on b has output bit k. The total number of selector appearances over the r output bits is at most qr for each b, so these ORs cost O(qr) gates per b. The symbol b can be included as a literal in each selector or the two symbol cases can be combined with O(qr) gates. The final acceptance bit is the OR of e_i over accepting states and costs O(qr). As r=ceil(log2 q), all stated bounds are O(q log q).
derivation: Explicit one-hot equality decoders from the binary state encoding feed ORs for each next-state bit; gate count is O(qr) for decoder construction and O(qr) for all output-bit ORs, with r=ceil(log2 q).
scope: All finite layered deterministic automata with binary alphabet and at most q states per layer, under fan-in-two Boolean circuits; this is an implementation upper bound only and makes no claim that the EXT residual automaton has polynomially many states in its parameters.

label: S1023
statement:
statement: FINITE-LANGUAGE LAYERED TRANSITION CIRCUIT. For every integer N>=0 and every fixed finite language L subseteq {0,1}^N, put M=|L|. There is a layered deterministic automaton recognizing L with at most M+1 states at every depth t in {0,...,N}, and its transitions and final acceptance test have fan-in-two Boolean circuit implementations of total size O(N(M+1) log(M+1)), with the convention log(M+1) is replaced by 1 when M=0. Proof: At depth t, a state is a residual R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for some p in {0,1}^t; include the empty residual if it occurs. There are at most M distinct nonempty residuals: for each prefix p with nonempty R_p choose z_p in R_p. The words pz_p are distinct for distinct prefixes p, so there are at most M such prefixes and hence at most M distinct nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual, giving at most M+1 states. The transition on b in {0,1} maps R_p to R_{pb}={z: bz in R_p}; this is well-defined on residuals because equal sets have equal cofactors, and the empty residual maps to itself. At each layer encode its q<=M+1 states by distinct r-bit strings, r=ceil(log2(M+1)) when M+1>=2 and r=1 otherwise. For a fixed input bit b and output bit j, form the OR over all source states u whose b-successor has jth code bit 1 of the equality selector [state_code=u]; an equality selector is an AND of r literals. Fan-in-two trees implement each equality selector and OR using O(qr+q) gates for that input symbol, hence O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates per layer under the stated convention. At depth N, the residual is either {epsilon} or empty, and a state equality test outputs acceptance exactly in the former case, using O((M+1)log(M+1)) gates. Summing over N layers proves the bound. For L=empty the sole state is empty and a constant-zero output suffices. This is a finite-language construction; applied to L=Im(Eval_{n,s}) its bound remains exponential unless M is independently controlled, and it gives no representation theorem for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Residuals form the canonical layered DFA; each nonempty residual has a distinct witnessing word in L, so each layer has at most |L|+1 states. A transition table on q encoded states is implemented by equality selectors and OR trees in O(q log q) fan-in-two gates per symbol. Summing across N layers yields the claimed bound.
scope: All N>=0 and all fixed finite L subseteq {0,1}^N; gate bound is parameterized by |L| and is not claimed polynomial in a succinct description of L.

statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-MASK UPDATE LEMMA. Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits, each with N input bits and a fixed truth-table ordering 0,...,N-1. For a prefix p in {0,1}^t define q_i(p)=1 iff C_i's truth table agrees with p on positions 0,...,t-1. On receiving b at position t<N, the next mask is q'_i=q_i(p) AND [C_i(t)=b] for i=1,...,M. Given the M bits a_i=C_i(t), all next-mask bits are computable by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most M+1 gates: share NOT b once, then use one AND gate per i, selecting b when a_i=1 and NOT b when a_i=0. The mask is exact: q_i(p)=1 iff C_i agrees with p; hence q'_i=1 iff C_i agrees with pb. Consequently, after t updates, q_i=1 exactly for listed circuits whose truth tables extend p, so q is nonzero iff p is extendible within F. The update uses M state bits and O(M) Boolean gates; it does not give a poly(log M) bound in general. The cost of producing constants a_i from circuit descriptions is excluded. This does not solve the arbitrary MCSP-decider transition problem.
derivation: Induct on t. Initially all q_i=1 for the empty prefix. For each listed circuit i, let a_i=C_i(t). Agreement at the new coordinate requires b=a_i as well as q_i=1. Thus q'_i=q_i AND b when a_i=1, and q'_i=q_i AND NOT b when a_i=0. Compute NOT b once and use one AND gate for each i. Therefore q'_i=1 exactly when C_i agrees with all t+1 coordinates. Induction proves the invariant and the nonzero-mask characterization.
scope: Every finite explicitly listed circuit family F and every prefix length t<N. Fan-in-two Boolean circuits over AND/OR/NOT; the vector a_i=C_i(t) is supplied to the update, and its production cost is excluded.

structure.gap: This candidate-mask lemma bounds updates only for an explicit list of M circuits and supplied next-coordinate evaluations. It leaves open Q-156fa9c912's central gap: whether a representation derived uniformly from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C can compute these candidate updates with poly(s,n) workspace and worst-case update time, including the cost of producing the constants.

label: S1025
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL COFACTOR UPDATE LEMMA. Let N>=1, L be any subset of {0,1}^N, and for a prefix p of length t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. For b in {0,1} and t<N, R_{pb}={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu in R_p}. Thus the exact residual after reading b is the b-cofactor of the previous residual. Moreover, prefixes p,q of the same length have R_p=R_q if and only if for every suffix z of length N-t, pz∈L iff qz∈L. Proof: For every u, u∈R_{pb} iff pbu∈L iff bu∈R_p, proving the identity pointwise. Equality of residual sets is by extensionality exactly equality of these membership predicates for every suffix. Consequently R_p is a sufficient state for deciding all future completions, and no coarser state that merges unequal residuals can preserve every future answer: if R_p≠R_q choose u in their symmetric difference, which distinguishes the continuation. The lemma gives exact information and the canonical distinguishability criterion, but asserts no efficient encoding or transition circuit for R_p.
derivation: Expand the definition of R_p and concatenate the next bit b with the remaining suffix u. The cofactor identity follows pointwise. Extensional equality gives the iff characterization. If two residuals differ, their symmetric difference contains a suffix whose completion answer differs, so any state representation preserving all completion answers must keep them distinct.
scope: All finite binary languages L subset {0,1}^N, every prefix depth t<N. This is an information-theoretic statement only; no size or cost bound is claimed.

structure.gap: This closes only the exact residual-information subclaim: the residual is necessary and sufficient as a semantic state, and its transition is cofactoring. It leaves open the assigned bridge: represent and compute these cofactors from arbitrary MCSP decision-circuit H_C with poly(s,n) workspace and worst-case update time, charging all operations and output generation.

label: S1026
statement:
statement: EXPLICIT-FAMILY TRACKER WITH OUTPUT-GENERATION COST. Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates and N input bits, with a fixed truth-table ordering indexed by 0,...,2^N-1. A streaming tracker processes a proposed truth table y in that order. Its state consists of M candidate bits q_i and an N-bit coordinate counter. Initially all q_i=1 and the counter is 0. On each incoming bit b at coordinate t, evaluate every C_i(t), set q_i'=q_i AND [C_i(t)=b], and increment the counter. The update can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(Ms+N) gates. After t updates, q_i=1 iff C_i agrees with the first t bits of y; hence some q_i=1 iff the prefix extends to the truth table of a member of F.
derivation: Evaluating all M listed circuits on the current N-bit coordinate uses O(Ms) gates. Each equality-to-b test and candidate-bit conjunction uses O(1) gates per circuit, hence O(M) gates. A binary increment of the N-bit counter uses O(N) gates. Thus one update uses O(Ms+N) gates. Initially the invariant holds vacuously. At coordinate t, the update preserves q_i precisely when its next truth-table bit matches b; induction proves the invariant after every prefix. Therefore nonzero mask is equivalent to extendibility within F.
scope: Explicit finite listed families; gate count excludes storage-cell implementation and assumes the candidate circuits are given. No polynomial-in-s bound follows when M is large; this does not establish a transition bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1028
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL SPLIT AND RECONSTRUCTION LEMMA. Let N be a nonnegative integer, L subseteq {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, and p in {0,1}^t. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, and for b in {0,1}, R_{pb}={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: pbu in L}. Then R_p = ({0} x R_{p0}) disjoint-union ({1} x R_{p1}). In particular, the ordered pair (R_{p0},R_{p1}) uniquely determines R_p, and for any p,q of length t, R_p=R_q implies R_{pb}=R_{qb} for each b. Proof: For any z in {0,1}^{N-t}, write its first coordinate uniquely as b and its remaining suffix as u, so z=bu. By definition, z in R_p iff pbu in L iff u in R_{pb}. Thus z lies in {b}xR_{pb}, establishing both inclusions in the displayed union. The union is disjoint because its members have distinct first coordinates. This identity reconstructs the parent set from its two child sets. If R_p=R_q, then for each b and u, u in R_{pb} iff bu in R_p iff bu in R_q iff u in R_{qb}, hence the child residuals are equal.
derivation: Split every suffix z according to its first bit; membership in the resulting child suffix set is exactly membership in the corresponding child residual. Disjointness follows from the distinct leading bit. Equality of parent residuals therefore implies equality of each bit-slice.
scope: All finite binary languages and all nonterminal prefix depths. This is a semantic transition/decomposition lemma; it gives no bound on the circuit cost of computing a represented child residual.

statement:
statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE PREFIX FILTER CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let N,k>=0 and W=(w_1,...,w_k) be an explicit list in {0,1}^N. At layer t encode prefix p by v_i=1 iff p=w_i[0:t]. On bit b, set v_i'=v_i AND [w_i[t]=b]. With W hardwired, this uses at most k fan-in-two AND gates per layer, Nk total across N layers, and masks are constructible in O(Nk) time and bits. At t=N, OR_i v_i accepts exactly the listed words. This gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound for W=Im(Eval_{n,s}) unless that image is explicitly listed at polynomial cost.
derivation: Induct on t. At t=0 every word matches the empty prefix. If v_i indicates agreement through positions <t, then AND with [w_i[t]=b] indicates agreement through positions <t+1, exactly the prefix pb. At t=N some coordinate is 1 iff p is listed. Each update is one AND with a fixed bit; there are k coordinates per layer. Constructing all masks by scanning W takes O(Nk) time and bits.

statement:
statement: PREFIX-REGISTER CIRCUIT UPDATE / ENDPOINT-SEPARATION LEMMA. Let N>=1 and L be any subset of {0,1}^N. At layer t, 0<=t<=N, represent the observed prefix p in an N-bit register P, with P_i=p_i for i<t and P_i=0 for i>=t; the layer index t is supplied by the layered machine. Given next input bit b, copy P_0,...,P_{t-1}, write b into coordinate t, and zero coordinates t+1,...,N-1. This update has O(N) fan-in-two circuit cost (in fact it is only wires and constants, if those are free). After N inputs, acceptance is exactly the predicate P in L. label: S1033
statement:
statement: SURVIVING-DESCRIPTION RESIDUAL CHARACTERIZATION. Let D be any finite set of descriptions, each describing a word Eval(d) in {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t, let A_p={d in D: Eval(d) begins with p}, and let R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in {Eval(d):d in D}}. Then R_p={suffix_{N-t}(Eval(d)):d in A_p}. Consequently, two prefixes p,q of the same length have identical residual languages iff the sets of suffix words produced by their surviving descriptions are equal; the surviving-description sets themselves need not be equal. Proof: If z in R_p, then pz=Eval(d) for some d, so d belongs to A_p and its remaining suffix is z. Conversely, if d belongs to A_p, Eval(d)=pz for its unique remaining suffix z, so pz is in the image and z belongs to R_p. Equality of residual languages is therefore exactly equality of these projected suffix-image sets, and does not imply equality of A_p and A_q.
derivation: Both inclusions follow directly from the definitions: a suffix in the residual is witnessed by a description whose word has prefix p; every surviving description's word factors uniquely as p followed by its suffix. Thus residual equivalence quotients surviving descriptions by equality of their suffix-image sets.
scope: All finite description families and each fixed prefix length t. This is a semantic characterization; it gives no efficient representation, update algorithm, or bound for transitions of arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1034
statement:
statement: TOTAL PREFIX-RESIDUAL COUNT LEMMA. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N. For each depth t in {0,...,N}, and each prefix p in {0,1}^t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. Let d_t be the number of distinct nonempty sets R_p at depth t. Then sum_{t=0}^N d_t <= (N+1)|L|. If the empty residual is counted at each depth, the total number of distinct residual states over all depths is at most (N+1)(|L|+1). Proof: For each depth t, let P_t={p in {0,1}^t:R_p is nonempty}. For each p in P_t choose one word w_p in L extending p. Distinct prefixes at the same depth yield distinct chosen words, so |P_t|<=|L|. Since every distinct nonempty residual at depth t is realized by at least one p in P_t, d_t<=|P_t|<=|L|. Summing over the N+1 depths gives the first bound. At each depth there is at most one empty residual, so adding at most N+1 gives the second bound.
derivation: At each fixed depth, choose one extending word for each nonempty prefix. The chosen words are distinct because their length-t prefixes differ. Thus the number of nonempty prefixes, and hence distinct nonempty residuals, is at most |L|. Sum over depths; add at most one empty residual per depth.
scope: Every finite N>=0 and every L subset of {0,1}^N. This counts states in the depth-layered prefix residual representation and asserts no bound on transition computation cost.

statement:
statement: TAGGED CHILD-DECOMPOSITION OF PREFIX RESIDUALS. Let N>=0, let L⊆{0,1}^N, and for every prefix p of length t≤N define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}: pz∈L}. For t<N, R_p = {0z:z∈R_{p0}} ∪ {1z:z∈R_{p1}}, and these two sets are disjoint. Consequently, |R_p|=|R_{p0}|+|R_{p1}|. Proof: If z∈R_p, then pz∈L. Its first bit a∈{0,1} is unique; write z=aw. Then p a w∈L, so w∈R_{pa}, and z belongs to the corresponding tagged child set. Conversely, if w∈R_{pa}, then p a w∈L, hence aw∈R_p. The tagged sets are disjoint because their first bits differ. Their cardinalities therefore add. This is a recursion for the semantic residual sets and does not bound the gate cost of computing them.

scope: Every finite N, every L⊆{0,1}^N, and every prefix p with |p|<N. No circuit complexity or PNP separation conclusion.
