label: S1036
statement:
statement: EXPLICIT RESIDUAL-AUTOMATON CIRCUIT SYNTHESIS. Let L be a finite language of words of length N, with at most K distinct residuals at each depth, including the empty residual. Its canonical layered deterministic automaton has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit implementing each one-bit update using O(K log(K+1)) gates, uniformly for every layer, with O(log(K+1)) state bits. Proof: At a fixed depth enumerate its r≤K residual states and assign distinct q=ceil(log2 r) bit codes (take q=1 if r=1). For each input b∈{0,1}, each state code u, and each output-code bit j, form the minterm [state=u] AND [input=b], costing O(q) fan-in-two gates per (u,b), with constants allowed. The next residual after reading b is uniquely determined; for each output bit j, OR together the minterms whose transition target has jth bit 1, using at most 2r−1 further gates (an empty set is constant 0). Thus all q next-state bits cost O(rq+r q)=O(r log(r+1)); a separate accepting/output bit can be computed by OR of the accepting-state minterms at cost O(rq+r). Invalid codes may transition to a fixed sink. The argument applies independently at each layer and gives the same O(K log(K+1)) worst-case gate bound. Correctness follows because exactly one state/input minterm is true for each valid encoded pair, and its target code is selected in each output bit. Applied to L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), this converts a residual-state bound K into a real-gate transition bound O(K log(K+1)); it does not establish K=poly(n,s), nor a small circuit for the existential projection from H_C.
derivation: Enumerate residual states at each layer, decode state and symbol by minterms, and encode each deterministic successor output bit as an OR of exactly the minterms leading to 1 in that bit. A unique true minterm proves the transition outputs equal the designated successor code.
scope: Finite fixed-length binary languages; per-layer residual count at most K; nonuniform layer-specific circuits; fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates with constants; state update only.

label: S1037
statement:
statement: CIRCUIT-COUNT BOUND ON EXT RESIDUAL WIDTH. Fix n,s≥0 and a Boolean basis of fan-in at most two with B fixed gate types. Let N=2^n and L_{n,s} be the N-bit truth tables computed by circuits on n inputs with at most s gates. At every depth t, the number K_t of distinct prefix residuals R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N-t}:pz∈L_{n,s}}, including the empty residual, is at most min(2^t, 1+(s+1)(n+s+1)(B(n+s+1)^2)^s). Proof: Topologically order any j≤s gates. For each gate there are at most B choices of type and (n+s+1)^2 choices of predecessor wires; the output wire has at most n+s+1 choices. Thus the number of descriptions, summed over j=0,…,s, is at most (s+1)(n+s+1)(B(n+s+1)^2)^s, with the zero-gate case covered by this overcount. Hence |L_{n,s}| is at most that quantity. There are at most 2^t prefixes. For each prefix with a nonempty residual, choose one completion yielding a truth table in L_{n,s}. Distinct prefixes yield distinct truth tables, so the number of such prefixes—and therefore distinct nonempty residuals—is at most |L_{n,s}|. At most one empty residual exists. Combining these bounds proves the claim. This gives a 2^{O(s log(n+s+2))} upper bound, not polynomial width for growing s, and implies no transition lower bound.
derivation: Count topologically ordered circuit descriptions to bound the number of realized truth tables. At a fixed prefix depth, choose one completion for each prefix with nonempty residual; distinct prefixes yield distinct full truth tables, so the number of nonempty residuals is bounded by the number of truth tables. Add at most one empty residual.
scope: All finite n,s and prefix depths t=0,…,2^n; fixed finite Boolean basis of fan-in at most two; nonuniform circuits. Bounds residual count only.

statement:
statement: EXT LEFT-DERIVATIVE LEMMA. Fix n,s and let L_{n,s} be the set of truth tables of Boolean circuits on n inputs of size at most s, in a fixed truth-table bit order, with N=2^n. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L_{n,s}}. For every t<N, every p of length t, and b in {0,1}, R_{pb}={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R_p}. Proof: For any such z, z belongs to R_{pb} iff pbz belongs to L_{n,s}, iff bz belongs to R_p by the definition of R_p. Hence equality holds pointwise. The identity gives the exact semantic next residual but gives no bound on the circuit or time cost of computing an encoding of that residual; in particular it does not show that a fixed-circuit verifier H_C suffices for the existential union over all size-s circuits.
derivation: Pointwise equivalence from the definition of prefix residuals: z∈R_pb iff pbz∈L iff bz∈R_p.
scope: All finite n,s, standard finite Boolean circuit descriptions and fixed truth-table bit order; semantic residuals only, with no transition implementation bound.

statement:
statement: EXPLICIT RESIDUAL-VECTOR COFACTOR UPDATE LEMMA. Let N be a nonnegative integer, let L be any subset of {0,1}^N, let 0 <= t < N, and let p in {0,1}^t. Define the Boolean residual vector v_p indexed by z in {0,1}^{N-t} by v_p(z)=1 iff pz is in L. For b in {0,1}, define v_{pb} on {0,1}^{N-t-1} analogously. Then for every u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, v_{pb}(u)=v_p(bu). Thus the exact transition on this explicit truth-vector representation is restriction to the coordinates whose first suffix bit equals b, followed by deletion of that first coordinate; in general it is not same-coordinate copying.
derivation: For each u, v_{pb}(u)=1 iff pbu is in L by definition of the child vector. Also v_p(bu)=1 iff p(bu) is in L by definition of the parent vector. Since p(bu)=pbu, the two Boolean values are equal. The statement about coordinate restriction is a direct restatement of this pointwise equality.
scope: All finite binary languages L and all valid prefix lengths. This specifies the transition only for the explicit residual truth-vector representation; it gives no polynomial-size encoding or Boolean-gate bound for arbitrary state representations.

statement:
statement: ZERO-GATE COFACTOR WIRING LEMMA. Let L be a subset of {0,1}^N, and at a prefix p of length t store the explicit residual vector v_p with one coordinate v_p(z)=1 iff pz is in L for each z in {0,1}^{N-t}. For t<N and b in {0,1}, the child vector v_{pb} is obtained by selecting, for each u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, the parent coordinate indexed by bu. Thus a transition circuit with unrestricted free wires and coordinate relabeling computes the child vector using zero Boolean gates. Its state width is 2^(N-t) before the update and 2^(N-t-1) after it; hence this representation has an exponential-width cost when N-t grows linearly with N, despite its zero-gate transition.
derivation: For each output coordinate u, the cofactor identity gives v_{pb}(u)=v_p(bu). Therefore connect the child output wire indexed by u directly to the parent input wire indexed by bu. No Boolean operation is needed. The coordinate counts follow from the sizes of the suffix sets. This proves only the cost for the stated explicit encoding under the stated free-wiring convention.
scope: All finite binary languages and valid prefix lengths. Gate count is zero only when wiring/relabeling and fanout are free; state width is counted separately. This gives no bound for compact encodings or arbitrary streaming machines.

label: S1042
statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-MASK COFACTOR UPDATE LEMMA. Let C_1,...,C_M be a fixed finite family of Boolean functions on a fixed ordered input domain, and let T_i be the truth table of C_i in that order. For a prefix p of length t, define A_p(i)=1 iff T_i begins with p. Let y_p(i) be the (t+1)-st bit of T_i. For b in {0,1}, define A_{pb}(i)=1 iff T_i begins with pb. Then for every i, A_{pb}(i)=A_p(i) AND [y_p(i)=b]. Consequently, given the full vector y_p, the child viability mask is computable from A_p using at most M AND gates, with the equality-to-b bits treated as available inputs. This statement gives no bound for computing y_p from a compact representation or an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
derivation: Fix i. By definition, T_i begins with pb exactly when its first t bits equal p and its next bit equals b. The first condition is A_p(i)=1; the second is [y_p(i)=b]. Their conjunction is therefore exactly A_{pb}(i). Applying this identity independently to all M coordinates uses one AND gate per coordinate if y_p(i)=b is supplied as an input bit (or obtained by a NOT of y_p(i) for b=0, with at most M additional NOT gates if complements are not free).
scope: All finite fixed candidate families and all valid prefix lengths. The circuit-cost bound is conditional on receiving the next-output vector as input. It does not compute that vector, exploit a compact encoding, or imply a bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1043
statement:
statement: EXPLICIT CANDIDATE-FAMILY TRANSITION COST LEMMA. Let D be a finite input domain with a fixed ordering x_1,...,x_N, and let C_1,...,C_M be Boolean circuits, each of fan-in two and size at most s, computing functions on D. For each t<N and prefix p in {0,1}^t, let A_p(i)=1 iff the truth table of C_i begins with p. Let x_{t+1} be the next domain input. Given the circuits C_1,...,C_M and the mask A_p, one can compute A_{pb} for either b in {0,1} by a fan-in-two circuit with at most Ms+M AND gates, and at most M additional NOT gates if complemented outputs are not free. In particular the transition has O(Ms) gates. This bound is for an explicit candidate family and mask; it does not imply a polynomial-in-s,n bound when M is large and does not apply to an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit.
derivation: Evaluate each C_i on the fixed input x_{t+1}, using at most s gates per candidate, for at most Ms gates total. Call the resulting bit y_i. By the candidate-mask cofactor identity, A_{pb}(i)=A_p(i) AND [y_i=b]. For b=1 the equality bit is y_i; for b=0 it is NOT y_i, costing at most one NOT per candidate when needed. One AND per coordinate completes the update. This proves the stated bound and correctness coordinatewise.
scope: All finite ordered domains, all fixed finite candidate families of fan-in-two circuits of size at most s, and all t<N. The candidate circuits are supplied as part of the representation; no compact description of the family or arbitrary-decider transition is established.

label: S1044
statement:
statement: DESCRIPTION-ENUMERATION TRANSITION BOUND. Fix n input bits and a fan-in-two basis {AND, OR, NOT} with constants. Let D_s be the set of syntactic circuit descriptions with at most s gates, in a fixed topological encoding in which each gate chooses its type from a fixed finite set and each predecessor chooses among n input wires, two constants, and at most s earlier gate outputs. Then |D_s| <= (s+1) K^s (n+s+2)^(2s) for an absolute constant K depending only on the encoding. For the explicit candidate mask indexed by D_s, one next-bit transition can be computed by evaluating each described circuit on the next truth-table input and applying the coordinatewise cofactor update, using O(s |D_s|) fan-in-two gates. Hence this representation has an explicit transition bound exp(O(s log(n+s))) but this does not yield a polynomial-in-s,n transition bound or a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP deciders.
derivation: For exactly j gates, there are at most K choices for each gate type and at most (n+j+2)^2 choices for its two predecessor wires; this overcounts gates of smaller arity and invalid wire patterns, so is an upper bound. Summing over j=0,...,s gives |D_s| <= (s+1)K^s(n+s+2)^(2s). For each description, evaluate its at most s gates on the fixed next truth-table input, then apply A_{pb}(i)=A_p(i) AND [y_i=b], costing O(s) gates per description. Summing gives O(s|D_s|). Taking logarithms of the cardinality bound gives log |D_s|=O(s log(n+s)), hence the stated exponential expression. The construction is syntactic and explicit; it makes no claim that this is optimal or that every MCSP decision circuit uses this representation.
scope: All n>=0 and integer s>=0 under the stated finite circuit encoding; explicit mask over syntactic descriptions only. No arbitrary-decider transition lower bound follows.

label: S1045
statement:
statement: ONE-HOT PREFIX REGISTER UPDATE LEMMA. Fix N>=1. A state consists of x in {0,1}^N and e in {0,1}^N, where after t<N input bits p have been read, x is p followed by N-t zeros and e_j=1 exactly for j=t. On input b, define x'_j=x_j OR (e_j AND b) for every j, and define e'_0=0 and e'_j=e_{j-1} for 1<=j<N. Then for every t<N, x' is p followed by b followed by N-t-1 zeros, and e' marks t+1 when t+1<N; at t=N-1 the data register becomes the full string pb and the marker becomes the all-zero terminal marker. The data update is implemented by at most 2N fan-in-two AND/OR gates; the marker update is wiring. Proof: Since e has its only 1 at coordinate t, for j!=t, x'_j=x_j; at j=t, x'_t=x_t OR b=b because the invariant gives x_t=0. Thus precisely coordinate t is written and all prior coordinates are preserved. The shift equation moves the unique 1 from t to t+1 if that coordinate exists, and yields the zero vector at the final boundary. This is an explicit O(N)-gate transition circuit for the stated one-hot encoding; it asserts no bound for arbitrary EXT or MCSP decision-circuit state encodings.
derivation: Coordinatewise use the one-hot invariant: only the current zero suffix coordinate is selected; the marker shift handles the terminal boundary.
scope: Every N>=1, every prefix length 0<=t<N and every next bit b; fan-in-two AND/OR circuit model.

label: S1046
statement:
statement: MINIMAL PREFIX-RESIDUAL STATE COUNT. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N and let a deterministic streaming recognizer read exactly N bits, with fixed initial state, deterministic transitions, and final acceptance determined by its state after N bits. For each t and p in {0,1}^t define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. At depth t every recognizer for L has at least |{R_p:p in {0,1}^t}| distinct reachable states. There exists a layered deterministic recognizer with exactly that many states at every depth, whose state after p is R_p and whose transition on b maps R_p to R_{pb}. Proof: If R_p differs from R_q, choose z in their symmetric difference. If the states after p and q were equal, determinism would give the same final acceptance after processing z, although exactly one of pz and qz belongs to L, contradiction. Conversely, use residual sets as states and define the b-transition R_p to R_{pb}. This is well-defined: for every suffix z of length N-t-1, z is in R_{pb} iff bz is in R_p; hence R_p=R_q implies R_{pb}=R_{qb}. At depth N accept precisely residuals containing the empty string. Induction shows the state after p is R_p, so the recognizer accepts exactly L. This is an exact state-count result only; it gives no Boolean gate bound for implementing transitions.
derivation: A suffix in the symmetric difference distinguishes prefixes, forcing separate states. Residual transitions are well-defined because child membership is parent membership after prepending b; induction proves the constructed recognizer is exact.
scope: All finite binary languages L subset {0,1}^N and N>=0; deterministic layered streaming recognizers with transitions allowed to depend on depth. Exact state counts per depth; no circuit transition cost asserted.

label: S1047
statement:
statement: LINEAR ONE-HOT RESIDUAL TRANSITION LEMMA. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N. At depths t and t+1, let A_t and A_{t+1} be the sets of distinct residuals R_p={z:pz in L} over prefixes p of the respective lengths, including the empty residual if it occurs, and put K_t=|A_t|, K_{t+1}=|A_{t+1}|. The deterministic transition R_p --b--> R_{pb} of the layered residual automaton can be implemented by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(K_t+K_{t+1}) gates under one-hot state encodings. Proof: For each source residual R in A_t, choose a representative prefix p with R_p=R. The child residual R_{pb} depends only on R and b: for every suffix z of length N-t-1, z in R_{pb} iff bz in R_p, so equal parent residuals have equal b-children. Thus the transition is a well-defined function δ:A_t×{0,1}→A_{t+1}. For each source R and bit b, form the edge signal e_{R,b}=q_R AND literal_b, where q_R is the one-hot source-state bit and literal_b is b or NOT b. These are 2K_t signals and require O(K_t) gates, including at most one shared NOT for the input literal. For each destination S, define its output bit as the OR of all edge signals e_{R,b} with δ(R,b)=S; if there are none, use constant 0. Across all destinations, the total number of incoming edge occurrences is exactly 2K_t, so binary OR trees require at most 2K_t gates in total. Supplying the K_{t+1} output wires and constants costs at most O(K_{t+1}) in the standard circuit description. On a valid one-hot source encoding, exactly one edge signal is active and its destination bit is the unique active output. Hence the circuit implements δ and has O(K_t+K_{t+1}) gates. This is a layered-automaton compilation bound; it does not bound K_t in terms of H_C or imply anything about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Equal residuals have equal children because child membership is parent membership after prefixing b. The transition graph has exactly two outgoing labelled arcs per source; create each arc as a one-hot-state/input conjunction and OR incoming arcs at each destination. Total arcs and OR terms are 2K_t, giving the stated linear gate bound.
scope: Every finite binary language L subset {0,1}^N and every 0<=t<N; fan-in-two Boolean circuits on valid one-hot state encodings. No assertion about succinct state encoding, residual-count bounds from H_C, or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1048
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY STATE LOWER BOUND. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N, let 0<=t<=N, and define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for p in {0,1}^t. Any deterministic one-pass automaton that reads its input left-to-right and decides membership in L must have at least K_t distinct internal states reachable after t input bits, where K_t is the number of distinct sets R_p. Proof: Suppose prefixes p,q of length t reach the same internal state but R_p != R_q. Then their symmetric difference is nonempty, so choose z in it. The automaton starts from the same state after p and q and receives the same remaining suffix z, hence produces the same accept/reject result on pz and qz. But exactly one of pz,qz lies in L by the choice of z, contradiction. Thus distinct residuals require distinct reached states, yielding at least K_t states. With fixed-width binary state encodings, at least ceil(log2 K_t) bits are required when K_t>=1. This is a storage lower bound only; it gives no lower bound on update computation or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Distinct residuals have a distinguishing suffix by set inequality. Determinism makes equal states indistinguishable under every common continuation, contradicting language membership on the distinguishing suffix.
scope: Finite binary languages of fixed length N; deterministic left-to-right recognizers with a well-defined state after each prefix. No update-time or unrestricted-circuit consequence.

label: S1049
statement:
statement: BINARY-ENCODING RESIDUAL TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N and 0<=t<N. Let A_t and A_{t+1} be the sets of distinct residuals R_p={z:pz in L} at depths t and t+1, including the empty residual if present, and put K_t=|A_t|>=1 and K_{t+1}=|A_{t+1}|>=1. Assign each layer's states distinct binary codes of widths w_t=ceil(log2 K_t) and w_{t+1}=ceil(log2 K_{t+1}), with width zero for a singleton. On valid source codes, the transition (state,b)->child state is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(K_t log(K_t+1)+K_t log(K_{t+1}+1)) gates. Proof: Equal parent residuals have equal b-children, since z is in R_{pb} exactly when bz is in R_p; hence the layered transition is well-defined. For each source code i, compute its equality indicator e_i using O(w_t+1) gates, for total O(K_t(w_t+1)). For each destination output bit j, OR the terms e_i AND literal_b for source indices i whose b-child has code bit j equal to 1. There are at most 2K_t terms per output bit and w_{t+1} output bits, so this takes O(K_t(w_{t+1}+1)) gates. On a valid source code exactly one e_i is 1, and the output bits equal the code of that state's child. Singleton layers use constants. Combining the counts proves the bound. No correctness is claimed on invalid source codes, and no arbitrary-representation lower bound follows.
derivation: Equal residuals have equal children because child membership is parent membership after prefixing b. Decode the binary source code into equality indicators; each destination bit is the OR of the source-and-input terms selecting a child code with that bit set. Exactly one source indicator is active on valid codes, yielding the transition. Count the decoder and output logic as O(K_t(w_t+1)+K_t(w_{t+1}+1)).
scope: Every finite binary language L subset {0,1}^N and layer 0<=t<N; fan-in-two circuits on valid source codes under fixed enumerative binary encodings; upper bound only.

On valid source codes, the transition (state,b)->child state is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(K_t log(K_t+1)+K_t log(K_{t+1}+1)) gates. Proof: Equal parent residuals have equal b-children, since z is in R_{pb} exactly when bz is in R_p; hence the layered transition is well-defined. For each source code i, compute its equality indicator e_i using O(w_t+1) gates, for total O(K_t(w_t+1)). For each destination output bit j, OR the terms e_i AND literal_b for source indices i whose b-child has code bit j equal to 1. There are at most 2K_t terms per output bit and w_{t+1} output bits, so this takes O(K_t(w_{t+1}+1)) gates. On a valid source code exactly one e_i is 1, and the output bits equal the code of that state's child. Singleton layers use constants. Combining the counts proves the bound. No correctness is claimed on invalid source codes, and no arbitrary-representation lower bound follows.

Decode the binary source code into equality indicators; each destination bit is the OR of the source-and-input terms selecting a child code with that bit set. Exactly one source indicator is active on valid codes, yielding the transition. Count the decoder and output logic as O(K_t(w_t+1)+K_t(w_{t+1}+1)).
scope: Every finite binary language L subset {0,1}^N and layer 0<=t<N; fan-in-two circuits on valid source codes under fixed enumerative binary encodings; upper bound only.

label: S1050
statement: statement: LEFT-QUOTIENT RESIDUAL TRANSITION LEMMA. Let N be a nonnegative integer, L be any subset of {0,1}^N, t<N, p in {0,1}^t, and b in {0,1}. Define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. Then R_{pb}={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R_p}. Proof: For each z of length N-t-1, z is in R_{pb} iff pbz is in L, by definition. This is equivalent to bz being in R_p, since bz has length N-t and p(bz)=pbz. Thus the two sets are equal. Consequently the exact semantic child residual is the left quotient of the parent residual by b. This identity alone gives no bound on the circuit or operation cost of computing a canonical encoding of that quotient.

label: S1051
statement: statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY STATE LOWER BOUND. Let L be a subset of {0,1}^N and let a deterministic streaming machine read one bit per step and decide membership in L after N bits. At a fixed depth t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} for each p in {0,1}^t. If the machine has q possible states at depth t and is correct on every length-N input, then q is at least the number K_t of distinct sets R_p; hence its state encoding requires at least ceil(log2 K_t) bits. Proof: Suppose p and p' lead to the same state. Determinism implies that for every suffix z, continuing from that same state on z gives the same final decision. Correctness therefore gives [pz in L]=[p'z in L] for every z of length N-t, so R_p=R_p'. Thus prefixes with distinct residuals must lead to distinct states, proving q>=K_t. This is an information lower bound for exact deterministic streaming representations; it makes no claim about update time or arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1052
statement: statement: STREAMING-TO-CIRCUIT UNROLLING LEMMA. Let N,w,g,d be nonnegative integers. Suppose a deterministic one-pass machine on length-N binary inputs has a fixed w-bit initial state, transition circuits T_i:{0,1}^w×{0,1}->{0,1}^w with at most g fan-in-two gates each, and a final decision circuit D with d gates. With wiring, constants, and fan-out free, the language recognized by the machine has a fan-in-two circuit of at most Ng+d gates. Proof: Compose N copies of T_1,...,T_N in temporal order, wiring each state output to the next state input and x_i to the i-th transition. At stage zero the wires encode the fixed initial state. Inductively, if stage i-1 encodes the machine state after i-1 input bits, T_i computes its state after i bits. Applying D to the last state therefore gives exactly the machine's decision. The composed circuit has at most the sum of the N transition sizes plus d, hence Ng+d gates. This is conditional: it neither constructs bounded-size transitions for EXT nor yields a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

label: S1053
statement:
statement: LITERAL-PREFIX CONSTANT-UPDATE TRADEOFF. Fix N and any language L subseteq {0,1}^N, including Im(Eval_{n,s}). A deterministic one-pass machine can recognize whether the current prefix p has an extension in L while using N bits of state and at most O(1) fan-in-two Boolean gates per update (with time-position-dependent transition circuits and wire copies free): store p padded to N bits; at position t, write incoming b into coordinate t+1 and leave all other coordinates unchanged; the output predicate is the fixed function [exists z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L]. This proves an exact O(1)-gate transition upper bound only with N-bit workspace and a possibly nonuniform output predicate; it gives no poly(s,log N)-space representation or transition bound for EXT.
proof: At position t the invariant is that the first t state coordinates equal the observed prefix p and all remaining coordinates are zero. The next transition copies the existing coordinates, writes b at coordinate t+1, and leaves later coordinates zero, so the invariant holds at t+1. At each position the machine's output can be defined as 1 exactly when some z of length N-t extends the stored prefix to a word in L; this is precisely the EXT residual predicate. The update uses only copying wires and the incoming bit (or one constant-size gate per updated coordinate under a gate-count convention that charges coordinate selection). The state has N bits. Thus the construction trades workspace for update simplicity and does not imply a small real-gate transition for the compressed automaton.

structure.evidence: Constructive explicit representation and induction on prefix length; applies to every finite L of fixed length N. The output predicate may be arbitrarily costly and is not claimed to be a circuit of bounded size.

statement:
statement: ONE-HOT TRANSITION UPPER BOUND. For any q-state deterministic binary transition map, its successor on valid one-hot inputs is computable by a fan-in-two circuit of O(q^2) gates. For each destination j and bit c, OR the x_i with δ(i,c)=j; output y_j=(¬b∧A[j,0])∨(b∧A[j,1]). Each destination costs O(q), hence O(q^2) total. A valid one-hot input activates exactly the correct destination. This is only an upper bound for one-hot encoding.
derivation: The one-hot input selects one source i. The input-bit gate selects the corresponding transition, so exactly y[δ(i,b)] is 1. Each destination uses two OR trees and constant additional gates, totaling O(q^2).
scope: Finite total deterministic binary transition maps; valid one-hot encodings; fan-in-two circuits.

label: S1055
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-TRIE ONE-HOT UPDATE BOUND. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N, and let T_L be the prefix trie whose states are all prefixes p of words in L, plus a dead state; from state p on bit b, move to pb if pb is a prefix of a word of L, and otherwise move to dead, which loops. The accepting states are the length-N prefixes in L. If K=|L|, then T_L has at most 1+NK+1 states, and its binary transition function on valid one-hot state encodings has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O((NK+2)^2) gates. Proof: Each word contributes at most N nonempty prefixes, so the number of trie states is at most NK; adding dead gives q<=NK+1 (for L empty, q=1). For each input bit b and target state v, form the OR of all one-hot source bits u whose b-transition is v; each such transition contributes to exactly one target per b, so the total number of source-target incidences over both symbols is 2q. A fan-in-two OR tree per target costs at most the number of its incoming sources minus one when nonempty; AND each target indicator with the input symbol as needed to combine the two symbol cases, using O(q^2) gates as a uniform safe bound. On valid one-hot inputs exactly one source bit is 1, hence exactly the destination bit is 1 and all others are 0. This constructs an exact deterministic update representation for the trie, with explicit state count and update cost; it does not improve to polynomial in n,s for L=Im(Eval_{n,s}) unless |L| and the resulting circuit size meet such a bound.
derivation: Build trie states from prefixes of words in L and add a looping dead state. Bound the number of trie states by charging each prefix to one of at most K words, with at most N prefixes per word. Encode states one-hot. For each target and input symbol, OR the source indicators mapped to that target; gate the contributions by the symbol and combine, giving at most O(q^2) fan-in-two gates. Valid one-hot inputs select precisely the unique transition destination.
scope: All finite N and languages L⊆{0,1}^N; circuit correctness is asserted only on valid one-hot state encodings. This is an explicit upper bound, not a lower bound or an arbitrary-representation simulation.

label: S1056
statement:
statement: CORRECTED FINITE-LANGUAGE TRIE SIZE AND UPDATE BOUND. Let N≥0 and L⊆{0,1}^N have K elements. If K>0, form the prefix trie with one state for each prefix of a word in L, including the empty prefix, and add one dead state; if K=0, use only a dead state. The number q of states is at most K(N+1)+1 when K>0, and q=1 when K=0. Its binary deterministic transition function on valid q-bit one-hot state encodings is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with O(q) gates. Proof: For each of the K words there are N+1 prefixes, so the union of their prefix sets has size at most K(N+1); adding dead gives the stated bound. For b∈{0,1} and each target state v, let P_{b,v} be the source states whose b-transition is v. The output bit for v is (b AND OR_{u∈P_{1,v}} z_u) OR ((NOT b) AND OR_{u∈P_{0,v}} z_u). Across all v and both symbols, the total number of source incidences is 2q. The OR trees therefore use O(q) gates in total; the symbol conjunctions and final ORs use O(q) additional gates. On a valid one-hot input z, exactly one source coordinate is 1, so these formulas set exactly the unique destination coordinate to 1, as required. For the empty language, the dead state loops and the same construction applies.
derivation: Count at most N+1 prefixes per word, including root, then add dead. For each target, express its next-state indicator as the OR of its symbol-conditioned predecessor indicators. Since each source has one destination for each of two symbols, there are 2q incidences total, yielding O(q) fan-in-two gates overall. One-hot correctness follows from exactly one active source.
scope: Every finite N≥0 and every L⊆{0,1}^N; transition-circuit correctness only on valid one-hot encodings. The bound is for the trie representation and makes no claim about arbitrary MCSP deciders.

statement:
statement: RESIDUAL AUTOMATON STATE COUNT. Let N≥0 and let L⊆{0,1}^N have K>0 words. For each prefix p of length t define R_p={z∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pz∈L}. The deterministic residual automaton with one state for each distinct nonempty R_p, plus one empty state, has at most 1+Σ_{t=0}^N min(2^t,K) states. Proof: At depth t there are 2^t prefixes. For every prefix with nonempty residual choose z_p∈R_p. The words pz_p are distinct for distinct prefixes of the same length, so at most K prefixes at that depth have nonempty residual. Thus there are at most min(2^t,K) distinct nonempty residuals at depth t. Nonempty residuals from different depths cannot be equal, since their elements have different fixed lengths N−t. Summing over depths bounds all nonempty states; the empty residual contributes at most one additional state. The transition on bit b maps R_p to R_{pb}, with empty residual mapped to itself, so this is a well-defined deterministic residual automaton.
derivation: At each depth t, the number of prefixes is 2^t and the number with nonempty residual is at most K by the injection p↦pz_p into L. Equal residuals are merged. Residuals at different depths have different word lengths and hence are distinct when nonempty. Sum these bounds and add the empty state.
scope: All finite N≥0 and nonempty L⊆{0,1}^N. This bounds states of the canonical residual automaton only; it gives no update-circuit lower bound or polynomial-in-(n,s) bound for arbitrary MCSP deciders.

statement:
statement: FIXED-CIRCUIT RESIDUAL UPDATE SCOPE LEMMA. Let C:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be a Boolean circuit, and let L_C={x:C(x)=1}. For each prefix p of length t define R_{C,p}(z)=1 iff pz is in L_C. For t<N and b in {0,1}, the child residual is exactly R_{C,pb}(z')=R_{C,p}(bz'). Thus a representation retaining C and p can specify the child residual by appending b to p, with no semantic loss. For a finite circuit family F, define L_F=union_{C in F} L_C and R_{F,p}(z)=1 iff exists C in F with C(pz)=1. Then R_{F,pb}(z')=R_{F,p}(bz') also holds, but this identity alone does not identify or construct a finite encoding of the child residual from a representation of R_{F,p}. Proof: In both equations, substitute the definition of the residual: R_{C,pb}(z')=1 iff pbz' in L_C iff C(pbz')=1 iff R_{C,p}(bz')=1. For F, R_{F,pb}(z')=1 iff exists C in F with C(pbz')=1 iff exists C in F with C(p(bz'))=1 iff R_{F,p}(bz')=1. These are pointwise equalities for every suffix z'. They establish semantic residual updating by restriction. They assert no gate bound for computing a canonical residual-state identifier; for F=all circuits of size at most s, obtaining such an identifier remains open.
derivation: Direct substitution into the definitions, for each suffix z', first for one C and then for existential union over finite F.
scope: All finite N, all Boolean circuits C, all finite circuit families F, all prefix lengths t<N and bits b.

statement: statement: RESIDUAL AUTOMATON TRANSITION SYNTHESIS LEMMA. Let L be a nonempty finite subset of {0,1}^N. For each t and prefix p in {0,1}^t let R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}, and let R_t be the number of distinct such residual sets at level t. Put R=max_t R_t and K=ceil(log2 R). There is a deterministic level-specific encoding of all residuals using K bits and, for each t<N, a total fan-in-two Boolean transition circuit T_t on K+1 input bits and K output bits such that T_t(code_t(R_p),b)=code_{t+1}(R_{pb}). Each T_t has O(K 2^K) gates. Proof: At each level injectively assign the distinct residuals codes from {0,1}^K; since L is nonempty, R>=1. For a valid code u representing R_p and b in {0,1}, define T_t(u,b) to be the assigned code of R_{pb}; the residual identity R_{pb}={z:bz in R_p} guarantees this is well-defined from the represented residual, even if multiple prefixes share it. Define T_t arbitrarily, for example as the all-zero word, on invalid codes. Each output bit is now a Boolean function of K+1 bits. Express it as an OR of at most 2^(K+1) minterms, each a conjunction of K+1 literals. Binary trees for each conjunction and the disjunction use O(K 2^K) fan-in-two gates total over K output bits. Thus the bound holds with an absolute constant. Empty L is handled separately by one residual state and a constant transition. This is an upper bound for the canonical level-specific residual representation only; it gives no lower bound for arbitrary encodings, no uniform-in-t circuit bound, and no decoder-inclusive cost bound.

label: S1061
statement:
statement: FINITE RESIDUAL AUTOMATON CIRCUITIZATION LEMMA. Let A be a complete deterministic layered automaton with q states over the binary alphabet. It has an injective state encoding using k=ceil(log2 q) bits and a fan-in-two {AND,OR,NOT} circuit computing its next state from the current code and input bit, with O(qk) gates. Its acceptance predicate has a circuit with O(q) gates. Thus, if an exact prefix language L subseteq {0,1}^N is recognized by its canonical layered residual automaton, a transition circuit exists with O(kQ) gates, where Q is the total number of residual states across all depths, including the empty residual. This bound is in Q and implies no polynomial bound in N or in the description size of L.

Proof: Assign distinct k-bit codes to the q states. For each state code a and input symbol b, form the indicator [state=a AND input=b] by comparing the k code bits and the symbol, using O(k) gates. For each of the k output coordinates, OR the indicators whose successor code has that coordinate equal to 1. There are 2q indicators, each used in at most k output ORs, so the total cost is O(qk). Define arbitrary outputs on unused codes. The acceptance predicate is the OR of the indicators for accepting codes and costs O(q). For residual states (t,R_p), define the transition on b as (t+1,R_{pb}); it is well-defined because R_{pb}(z)=R_p(bz), so equal residuals at depth t have equal children. Add a rejecting sink for transitions after depth N and apply the circuit construction.
derivation: Use equality decoders for each state-symbol pair; each next-state bit is the OR of decoders whose successor has that bit set. The residual-child identity makes the canonical transitions well-defined.
scope: All finite complete deterministic layered binary automata; fan-in-two Boolean gate cost. The bound is in total state count Q, not an asymptotic MCSP transition-cost bound.

label: S1062
statement:
statement: WITNESS-ENUMERATION CIRCUIT FOR PREFIX RESIDUALS. Let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r -> {0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of h gates. For each prefix p in {0,1}^t, define F_p(z)=1 iff there exists y in {0,1}^r with H(pz,y)=1, where z has length N-t. Then F_p has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of at most 2^r(h+1) gates. The construction is uniform given H and p by making one copy of H for each y, substituting p and y as constants, and OR-ing the 2^r outputs. This is an upper bound, not a lower bound; at r=O(s) it may be exponential in s and does not give a cheap transition for EXT.
derivation: For each y in {0,1}^r, let H_y(z)=H(pz,y). Substitution of constants into H does not increase its h gate count. A binary OR tree over the 2^r outputs uses 2^r-1 gates. The total is 2^r h + 2^r-1 <= 2^r(h+1). For each z, this OR is 1 exactly when some witness y makes H(pz,y)=1. For r=0, the construction is one copy with no OR gates.

label: S1063
statement:
statement: LITERAL PREFIX-REGISTER UPDATE. Let H:{0,1}^N x {0,1}^r->{0,1}, and for each prefix p of length t define R_p(z)=1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^r with H(pz,w)=1. After reading b in {0,1}, store pb and retain H. For every z' in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, the represented residual equals R_{pb}(z')=1 iff exists w H(pb z',w)=1. Proof: by the definition of R at prefix pb, both predicates are the same existential statement over the same witness domain, pointwise for every z'. The register update appends b and retains the previous prefix and H description. In a model charging register operations separately, it uses zero Boolean gates; the representation uses t+1 prefix bits at depth t+1, in addition to the retained H description. Thus this proves exact semantic updating for a literal-prefix representation, but makes no compact-state, canonical-residual, or real-gate transition-cost claim for EXT.
derivation: Expand the definition of R at prefix pb. The update changes the stored prefix from p to pb and leaves H and the witness domain unchanged. Therefore the post-update predicate is exactly the existential projection defining R_{pb}. Count stored prefix bits explicitly; do not identify this representation with a canonical residual encoding.
scope: All finite N,r,t with 0<=t<N; arbitrary Boolean relation H. Cost statement assumes register append/storage is not charged as Boolean gates; prefix storage is t+1 bits.

statement:
statement: FULL-TRUTH-TABLE COFACTOR UPDATE. Let f:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, let p be a prefix of length t<N, and encode its residual R_p by the ordered table T_p=(f(pz):z in lexicographic order on {0,1}^{N-t}). For b in {0,1}, the child residual table T_{pb} is exactly the contiguous block of T_p with indices b*2^(N-t-1) through (b+1)*2^(N-t-1)-1. Proof: every suffix z' of length N-t-1 has index b*2^(N-t-1)+index(z) in the parent table when its next bit is b; hence the corresponding entry is f(pb z'), which is the child-table entry. Thus child construction is a block selection requiring no Boolean evaluation gates if table access/copy is a primitive; it stores 2^(N-t-1) bits and gives no polynomial-size or ordinary-circuit transition bound.
derivation: Order suffixes lexicographically. Split the parent table by the first suffix bit into its 0-block and 1-block. By the definition of residual evaluation, each block entry is exactly the corresponding child residual value.
scope: All finite Boolean functions f, all N>=1 and 0<=t<N; table representation and block-copy update only.

label: S1065
statement:
statement: FINITE-LANGUAGE CANDIDATE-MASK UPDATE LEMMA. Let N>=0 and L be any finite subset of {0,1}^N with k=|L|. After reading prefix p in {0,1}^t, store the k indicator bits a_w=[w has prefix p], in a fixed ordering of L. On reading b when t<N, update each coordinate by a'_w=a_w AND [w_{t+1}=b]. Then a'_w=1 exactly for w in L with prefix pb. The represented residual {z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: pbz in L} is exactly the suffix projection of the updated live candidates. The initial state uses k bits; each update has at most k two-input AND gates, with position-dependent comparison constants hardwired. Proof: Induct on t. At t=0 every word has the empty prefix, so all coordinates are 1. If a_w indicates that w has prefix p, then a'_w=1 iff w has prefix p and its next bit is b, equivalent to w having prefix pb. This proves the invariant at t+1. A suffix z extends pb to an element of L iff some indexed candidate is live after update and has suffix z, so projection is exact. If k=0 the state is empty and update is vacuous. At t=N no update is required; acceptance is whether any live coordinate remains. This bounds only the explicit candidate-mask encoding and gives no polynomial-in-description-length transition bound when k is large.
derivation: Induction on prefix length: initialize every candidate live; each update conjoins prior liveness with agreement at the newly read coordinate, exactly characterizing extension by the longer prefix. Surviving candidates' suffixes are precisely the residual language.
scope: All finite N>=0 and L subset {0,1}^N, including empty L; explicit one-bit-per-word representation only.

label: S1066
statement:
statement: ENUMERATED-CIRCUIT EXT TRACKER BOUND. Fix n>=1 and s>=0. Let D_{n,s} be descriptions of Boolean circuits on n inputs with at most s topologically ordered gates, each an AND, OR, or NOT gate whose predecessors are input wires or earlier gate outputs; choose the output from all input and gate wires. Let L be the N=2^n-bit truth tables computed by these descriptions. There is an exact prefix tracker for L using at most |D_{n,s}| state bits and at most |D_{n,s}| two-input AND gates per update. Also |D_{n,s}| <= (s+1) 3^s (n+s)^(2s+1). Proof: For exactly j gates, gate types have at most 3^j choices. Each gate has at most (n+s)^2 predecessor-tuple choices, overcounting NOT gates, and the output has at most n+s choices. Thus there are at most 3^j(n+s)^(2j+1) descriptions. Summing for j=0,...,s gives at most (s+1)3^s(n+s)^(2s+1). Now keep one live bit per description, initially 1. At position t, update its bit by AND with the description's predicted truth-table bit at t if the observed bit is 1, or with the complement of that prediction if the observed bit is 0. Equivalently the update is either identity or AND with 0, so at most one AND gate per description when the position-dependent prediction is hardwired. Inductively, after prefix p the live descriptions are exactly those whose truth tables extend p. Hence a live description exists exactly when p is an EXT prefix. This bound does not include the cost of generating the predicted bits and is not a polynomial-in-(n,s) bound.
derivation: Overcount circuit descriptions by gate count, gate-type choices, predecessor choices, and output choice. Apply the candidate-mask invariant: each update retains exactly the descriptions matching the newly read truth-table bit.
scope: All n>=1 and s>=0 in this ordered fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT description model. Position-dependent predicted bits are treated as hardwired constants; no uniform cost to generate them is claimed.

label: S1067
statement: statement: RESIDUAL DERIVATIVE TRANSITION LEMMA. For every N>=0, every language L subseteq {0,1}^N, every t with 0<=t<N, every prefix p in {0,1}^t, and b in {0,1}, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L} and D_b(R)={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R}. Then R_{pb}=D_b(R_p). Consequently, the transition on exact residual sets is well-defined: if R_p=R_q for prefixes p,q of the same depth t, then R_{pb}=R_{qb} for each b. Proof: For each z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, z in R_{pb} iff pbz in L iff bz in R_p iff z in D_b(R_p). Thus the sets are equal. If R_p=R_q, applying the same set map D_b gives equal child residuals. This establishes an abstract transition rule only; it gives no bound on the real-gate cost of computing the derivative from an arbitrary H_C.

label: S1068
statement: statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND FOR PREFIX RECOGNIZERS. Let L be any fixed-length language over {0,1}^N, and let A be a deterministic one-pass streaming recognizer that reads all N bits and then accepts or rejects from its final state. For prefixes p,q of the same length t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in L}. If R_p≠R_q, then A must be in different states after reading p and q. Consequently A has at least |{R_p:p in {0,1}^t}| states after t bits and needs at least ceil(log2 |{R_p:p in {0,1}^t}|) state bits at that depth. Proof: choose z in the symmetric difference of R_p and R_q. Then exactly one of pz,qz belongs to L. If A had the same state after p and q, determinism forces identical subsequent state evolution on the common suffix z, hence the same final decision on pz and qz, a contradiction. This is a lower bound on exact recognizer state count only; it does not bound the cost of computing transitions or imply a lower bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.

structure.evidence: Complete distinguishing-suffix proof is included in the statement. No unreviewed proof step is used as a premise.

label: S1069
statement:
statement: CANDIDATE-FILTER TRANSITION LEMMA. Let D be a finite set of descriptions, each describing a Boolean function f_d:{0,1}^N->{0,1}. At a fixed input position i, represent the descriptions consistent with the already-read prefix by a bit vector q in {0,1}^D, where q_d=1 exactly for consistent descriptions. On reading input bit b, define q'_d=q_d AND [f_d(x_i)=b]. This next-state map is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most |D| AND gates when the fixed labels f_d(x_i) are constants; its output is nonzero exactly when some description in D is consistent with the extended prefix. Proof: For each d, the next prefix is consistent with d iff the old prefix is consistent with d and its predicted bit at position i equals b. This is precisely q_d AND [f_d(x_i)=b]. Since the prediction is a fixed Boolean constant, the output coordinate is either q_d or 0 (and can be implemented with at most one AND gate); hence the gate bound. Taking the disjunction of output coordinates, or simply using nonzeroness of q', gives the extendibility equivalence. This lemma concerns the explicit candidate-vector representation and fixed per-candidate predictions; it gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound when |D| is exponential, and does not derive such a representation from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
derivation: For each description d, consistency after reading b is equivalent to consistency before reading b together with f_d(x_i)=b. Thus q'_d=q_d∧[f_d(x_i)=b]. The bracketed value is a fixed constant, so each coordinate is computed with at most one AND gate. There is a surviving description iff at least one output coordinate is 1.
scope: Finite D, fixed position i and fixed functions f_d; fan-in-two Boolean gates with fixed prediction labels available as constants. No claim about constructing labels from H_C or compressing D.

structure.gap: The explicit candidate-vector update costs O(|D|), which may be exponential in s log(n+s) for size-s circuit descriptions. The central open issue remains whether an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C yields a compact state representation with a proved bounded-cost transition.

This next-state map is computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most |D| AND gates when the fixed labels f_d(x_i) are constants; its output is nonzero exactly when some description in D is consistent with the extended prefix. Proof: For each d, the next prefix is consistent with d iff the old prefix is consistent with d and its predicted bit at position i equals b. This is precisely q_d AND [f_d(x_i)=b]. Since the prediction is a fixed Boolean constant, the output coordinate is either q_d or 0 (and can be implemented with at most one AND gate); hence the gate bound. Taking the disjunction of output coordinates, or simply using nonzeroness of q', gives the extendibility equivalence. This lemma concerns the explicit candidate-vector representation and fixed per-candidate predictions; it gives no polynomial-in-s transition bound when |D| is exponential, and does not derive such a representation from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

The bracketed value is a fixed constant, so each coordinate is computed with at most one AND gate. There is a surviving description iff at least one output coordinate is 1.
scope: Finite D, fixed position i and fixed functions f_d; fan-in-two Boolean gates with fixed prediction labels available as constants. No claim about constructing labels from H_C or compressing D.

statement:
statement: BOUNDED-SUFFIX PROJECTION LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. Fix a prefix p∈{0,1}^{N-k}. Define E_H(p)=1 iff there exist u∈{0,1}^k and y∈{0,1}^r with H(pu,y)=1. There is a fan-in-two circuit on no input variables computing E_H(p), of size at most 2^k(h+1)+2^k, by making one copy of H for each u, substituting p,u, existentially OR-ing over all y is NOT performed by this construction; thus this statement as written is false unless y is absent or its domain is also explicitly enumerated. Corrected lemma: for H:{0,1}^N→{0,1} (r=0), E_H(p)=OR_{u∈{0,1}^k}H(pu) has a circuit of size at most 2^k h+(2^k−1). For H(x,y) with r witness bits, the same bound holds only when r is a fixed constant and the 2^r witness assignments are enumerated, giving size at most 2^{k+r}h+(2^{k+r}−1).
derivation: For each complete assignment u (and, in the witness version, each y), substitute the constants p,u (and y) into a separate copy of H. OR all resulting output bits using a binary tree; a binary tree with M leaves uses M−1 fan-in-two OR gates. The resulting output is 1 exactly when one enumerated completion satisfies H. This construction also identifies the earlier gap: copying H and enumerating only u leaves the existential y uneliminated, so it does not construct E_H for arbitrary r.
scope: Exact circuit construction for Boolean circuits with h fan-in-two gates. Cost is exponential in the number of enumerated suffix plus witness bits; no claim for arbitrary long suffix or unbounded witness length.

statement:
statement: VARIABLE-PREFIX PROJECTION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let H:{0,1}^N×{0,1}^r→{0,1} be computed by a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with h gates. For 0≤k≤N, define E:{0,1}^{N-k}→{0,1} by E(z)=1 iff there exist u∈{0,1}^k and y∈{0,1}^r such that H(zu,y)=1. Then E has a fan-in-two circuit with at most 2^(k+r)h + 2^(k+r)−1 gates (allowing constants at inputs). Proof: Let M=2^(k+r). For each pair (u,y), make a copy of H and substitute the constants u,y into the corresponding input positions, leaving z as the variable inputs. Each copy has at most h gates. OR the M outputs using a fan-in-two tree with M−1 gates (zero OR gates when M=1). For each z, this output is 1 exactly when some pair (u,y) satisfies H(zu,y)=1, which is the definition of E(z).
derivation: The construction enumerates all assignments to the eliminated suffix and witness bits, substitutes each assignment while retaining the prefix variables, and ORs the resulting circuit outputs. Constant substitution does not increase gate count; a binary OR tree on M outputs uses M−1 gates.
scope: All N,r,k with 0≤k≤N and all fan-in-two Boolean circuits H with h gates. The bound is exponential in k+r; it gives no polynomial bound when those parameters grow.

label: S1072
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL DISTINGUISHABILITY LOWER BOUND. Let L be any language of fixed-length strings {0,1}^N recognized by a deterministic left-to-right streaming machine whose state after prefix p determines acceptance of every completion z of the appropriate remaining length. At depth t, if two prefixes p,q in {0,1}^t have different residual sets R_p={z:pz in L} and R_q={z:qz in L}, then the machine must be in different states after p and q. Consequently its number of states at depth t is at least the number of distinct residuals {R_p:p in {0,1}^t}; if states are encoded by S bits, S >= ceil(log2 K_t), where K_t is that residual count. Proof: Since R_p != R_q, their symmetric difference is nonempty; choose z in it. Exactly one of pz,qz lies in L. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism implies that feeding the same suffix z produces the same final state and acceptance bit, contradiction. Thus states are pairwise distinct for different residuals, giving the count and bit bound. Applied to EXT_{n,s}, this gives a necessary information bound for every exact prefix-streaming algorithm, independently of its transition implementation. It does not imply a superpolynomial state lower bound or a transition-gate lower bound.
derivation: For each pair of unequal residuals choose a distinguishing suffix; deterministic evolution from equal states under the same suffix must be identical, contradicting different language membership. Inject distinct residual classes into states; S-bit encodings provide at most 2^S states.
scope: All finite fixed-length languages and deterministic streaming recognizers with state-sufficient acceptance; in particular every depth of EXT_{n,s}.

label: S1073
statement:
statement: ENUMERATED-CIRCUIT PREFIX UPDATE LEMMA. Fix n,s>=0 and a finite fan-in-two Boolean basis B of constant size with constants allowed. Let D_{n,s} be all syntactic circuit descriptions with n input wires and at most s gates, each gate selecting a basis operation and at most two earlier wires. Order the 2^n inputs once and for all as x_1,...,x_{2^n}. There is an exact streaming recognizer for EXT_{n,s}: its state after t bits is the set A_t of descriptions C in D_{n,s} whose first t output bits equal the observed prefix. On seeing bit b at position t+1, update A_{t+1}={C in A_t:C(x_{t+1})=b}. The update is correct and can be implemented in O(|D_{n,s}|s) Boolean gate operations per step using a stored description list and evaluating each circuit on one input; initialization costs O(|D_{n,s}|) candidate setup plus evaluation overhead. Since each gate has at most |B|(n+s+O(1))^2 choices, |D_{n,s}| <= (s+1)(|B|(n+s+O(1))^2)^s, so per-step update is O((s+1)s(|B|(n+s+O(1))^2)^s). This is an exhaustive upper bound, not polynomial in n,s in general, and it makes no claim about arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: For each description C maintain whether its truth-table prefix agrees with the stream. At step t+1, a surviving C remains exactly when its output on the next fixed input x_{t+1} is b. Induction on t proves that the maintained set is precisely A_t: A_0 contains all descriptions; the update intersects A_t with the descriptions producing b at coordinate t+1, which is exactly the definition of A_{t+1}. One circuit evaluation on a fixed input takes O(s) basis-gate operations, so scanning the full list costs O(|D_{n,s}|s). A description with j<=s gates is specified by at most |B|(n+j+O(1))^2 choices per gate; summing over j=0,...,s gives the displayed upper bound after enlarging the constant in O(1). Duplicate descriptions/functions do not affect correctness because existence of a matching description is equivalent to membership of at least one candidate. The maintained list accepts a prefix iff it has a survivor, exactly the definition of EXT.

label: S1074
statement:
statement: TOTAL PREFIX-AUTOMATON STATE BOUND. Let L be a finite subset of {0,1}^N with q=|L|, and define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-|p|}: pz in L} for every prefix p of length at most N. The deterministic prefix automaton whose states are distinct residuals R_p has at most sum_{t=0}^N (min(2^t,q)+1) states, hence at most (N+1)(q+1) states and ceil(log2((N+1)(q+1))) bits suffice to encode its states. Proof: At depth t there are 2^t prefixes. For each prefix with nonempty residual choose one completion z_p in R_p. The words pz_p are distinct for distinct prefixes, so there are at most q such prefixes. Thus at most min(2^t,q) distinct nonempty residuals occur at depth t, plus at most one empty residual. Summing over depths gives the first bound. Each summand is at most q+1, giving the second bound. Indexing the finite state set gives the bit bound. A semantic successor is determined by R_{pb}={u:bu in R_p}; this does not bound Boolean-circuit cost to compute the indexed successor.
derivation: At each depth t, inject prefixes with nonempty residuals into L by selecting one completion per prefix. Bound distinct nonempty residuals by both the number of such prefixes and 2^t; add the unique possible empty residual. Sum the per-depth bounds and encode the resulting finite state set by an index.
scope: All finite N and L subset {0,1}^N. State count and information-bit bound only; no transition-circuit complexity statement.

label: S1075
statement:
statement: ONE-HOT RESIDUAL SUCCESSOR CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each 0<=t<N, let A_t be the set of distinct residuals R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}:pz in L} over prefixes p of length t, including the empty residual, and let d_t=|A_t|. For each fixed b in {0,1}, there is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with d_t input indicator bits (one-hot state encoding) and d_{t+1} output indicator bits that maps the indicator of R_p to the indicator of R_{pb}; on the valid one-hot inputs its size is at most d_t+d_{t+1}+O(1). Proof: For every R in A_t, define its b-successor σ_b(R)={z:bz∈R}. This is well-defined as a residual in A_{t+1}: if R=R_p then σ_b(R)=R_{pb}; if R_p=R_q, membership of every bz agrees, hence R_{pb}=R_{qb}. For each target S∈A_{t+1}, let P_S={R∈A_t:σ_b(R)=S}. Set output bit y_S=OR_{R∈P_S}x_R. These predecessor sets partition A_t, so each valid one-hot input x_R produces exactly the unique successor indicator. Implement each nonempty OR with |P_S|-1 binary OR gates; the total is d_t - r gates, where r is the number of nonempty predecessor groups, hence at most d_t. Add only constant overhead for the empty/singleton OR conventions. This gives the stated bound. No bound on d_t for EXT_{n,s}, no encoding/decoding cost for arbitrary MCSP circuits, and no consequence for arbitrary decision circuits is asserted.
derivation: Define σ_b on residual equivalence classes by suffix restriction. Equality of residual sets guarantees well-definedness. Route each one-hot source bit to its unique target class; each target output is the OR of its predecessor indicators. The predecessor sets partition the source states, so total OR gates are at most d_t (plus constant wiring/convention overhead).
scope: All finite L⊆{0,1}^N and each level t<N and bit b; transition is required only on valid one-hot encodings.

structure.lemma: One-hot successor transitions for any finite binary language have a linear gate bound in the number of residual states on adjacent levels. This does not imply the needed EXT_{n,s} uniform polynomial bound; it isolates the remaining quantity.

label: S1076
statement:
statement: PADDED TRUTH-TABLE RESIDUAL UPDATE LEMMA. Let N≥1 and L⊆{0,1}^N. After reading a prefix p of length t≤N, define a state B_p indexed by q∈{0,1}^N by B_p(q)=1 iff p followed by the first N−t bits of q belongs to L. For t<N and next bit b, the exact next state satisfies B_{pb}(q)=B_p(b q_1…q_{N−t−1}) for every q. Thus, given t and b, the next 2^N-bit state is obtained from the current state by selecting and duplicating wires, with no Boolean gates in the usual circuit model with unrestricted fanout. The representation uses 2^N state bits (plus a depth counter if t is not externally known). Proof: By definition, B_{pb}(q)=1 exactly when pb q_1…q_{N−t−1} belongs to L. Applying the definition of B_p to the N-bit index b q_1…q_{N−t−1} followed by t arbitrary padding bits gives the same membership test; the padding is irrelevant because B_p uses only the first N−t index bits. Hence the stated identity holds for every q. The next state’s coordinates can therefore be connected directly to the indicated current-state coordinates. This proves exactness and zero-gate transition cost for this explicit exponential-size representation; it gives no compact representation or bound for arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Coordinatewise, both sides test membership of the same length-N string pb q_1…q_{N−t−1} in L; the remaining index bits are ignored by the residual encoding. Implement each output coordinate as a wire from its specified input coordinate.
scope: Finite binary languages L⊆{0,1}^N, all prefix lengths t<N, both next-bit values. State width 2^N; unrestricted wire fanout. No claim about compact state, construction cost for L=Im(Eval), or arbitrary MCSP circuits.

statement:
statement: PADDED TRUTH-TABLE RESIDUAL UPDATE LEMMA (corrected indexing). Let N>=1, L subseteq {0,1}^N, 0<=t<N, p in {0,1}^t, and b in {0,1}. For every q in {0,1}^N define B_p(q)=1 iff p concatenated with the first N-t bits of q lies in L. Define u to be the N-bit string whose first N-t bits are b followed by the first N-t-1 bits of q, and whose final t bits are zero. Then B_{pb}(q)=B_p(u). Consequently each coordinate of B_{pb} is a wire selected from the 2^N coordinates of B_p (with unrestricted fanout), so the transition uses no Boolean gates; the state has 2^N bits. Proof: The first N-(t+1) bits of q are exactly the suffix following pb in the definition of B_{pb}(q). The first N-t bits of u are b followed by those same bits. Hence both B_{pb}(q) and B_p(u) test membership in L of the identical N-bit string pb q_1...q_{N-t-1}. Since u is a fixed function of (q,t,b), every output coordinate is copied from one input coordinate. This is an exact update for the explicit exponential-width representation only; it asserts no compactness or MCSP transition bound.

statement: statement: BINARY-ENCODED LAYERED AUTOMATON TRANSITION LEMMA. Let Q_t and Q_{t+1} be finite state sets with sizes q_t,q_{t+1} >= 1, and let delta:Q_t->{Q_{t+1}} be any function. Fix injective encodings e_t:Q_t->{0,1}^{a_t} and e_{t+1}:Q_{t+1}->{0,1}^{a_{t+1}}, where a_t=ceil(log2 q_t) and a_{t+1}=ceil(log2 q_{t+1}); when a layer has one state, use a zero-bit encoding and a constant output. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit on a_t input bits that, on every valid encoded state e_t(q), outputs e_{t+1}(delta(q)), with O(q_t(a_t+a_{t+1})) gates. Proof: For each q in Q_t, form the equality indicator I_q that the input equals e_t(q), using at most a_t literals and a binary AND tree, costing O(a_t) gates. For output coordinate j, form the OR of I_q over all q for which coordinate j of e_{t+1}(delta(q)) is 1; an empty OR is constant 0. This costs O(q_t) gates per coordinate, hence O(q_t a_{t+1}) overall, in addition to O(q_t a_t) for the indicators. On a valid input e_t(q), injectivity makes I_q=1 for precisely that q, so each output coordinate equals the corresponding bit of e_{t+1}(delta(q)). The circuit's behavior on invalid encodings is unconstrained. This bound is finite-state and generally exponential in the state bit length; it supplies no polynomial transition bound for EXT_{n,s} and no bounded-operation representation through H_C.

label: S1079
statement:
statement: SPARSE-OUTPUT TRANSITION CIRCUIT LEMMA. Let δ:Q→Q′ be any map between finite sets of sizes q,q′≥1, with injective binary encodings e and e′ of widths a=⌈log₂q⌉ and a′=⌈log₂q′⌉ (allow width 0 when the set has size 1). For output coordinate j, let k_j=|{u∈Q: bit j of e′(δ(u)) is 1}|. There is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit that, on every valid encoding e(u), outputs e′(δ(u)), with O(q(a+1)+Σ_{j=1}^{a′}(1+min(k_j,q−k_j))) gates. Proof: For each u∈Q, build an equality indicator I_u for the a-bit encoding e(u), using O(a+1) fan-in-two gates. For coordinate j, if k_j≤q−k_j, output the OR of I_u over states whose image has coordinate j equal to 1. Otherwise output the negation of the OR of I_u over states whose image has coordinate j equal to 0. A binary OR tree uses O(1+r) gates for r indicators. On a valid encoding exactly one I_u is true, so the selected expression equals coordinate j of e′(δ(u)). Summing the indicator and coordinate costs proves the bound. For a=0, Q is a singleton and its sole indicator is the constant 1. This is a transition-table bound; it asserts no structural sparsity for EXT transitions and no connection to arbitrary MCSP decision circuits.
derivation: Construct equality indicators for all valid source encodings. Each output bit is the OR of indicators on its smaller truth side, negated when the zero side is smaller. Exactly one indicator is active on valid inputs, proving correctness; counting gates gives the bound.
scope: All finite maps between nonempty finite sets, for arbitrary fixed injective encodings at the stated minimum widths; correctness is required only on valid source encodings.

label: S1080
statement:
statement: EXPLICIT-CANDIDATE PREFIX UPDATE LEMMA. Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be a fixed explicitly listed family of Boolean functions on {0,1}^n, and let x_1,...,x_{2^n} be a fixed ordering of the inputs. After reading truth-table bits b_1,...,b_t, store A_i=1 iff C_i(x_j)=b_j for every j<=t. Initialize A_i=1 for all i. At position t+1, put c_i=C_i(x_{t+1}), a fixed bit. On input b, update A_i'=A_i AND [b=c_i]. The invariant is preserved, so OR_i A_i is 1 iff some function in F extends the observed prefix. For each fixed position, this transition has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with at most M AND gates and at most one shared NOT gate, hence O(M) gates; the extendibility OR costs O(M). Proof: At t=0 every candidate agrees with the empty prefix. Inductively, C_i agrees with the first t+1 bits exactly when it agrees with the first t bits and C_i(x_{t+1})=b_{t+1}, which is exactly the update. Since c_i is fixed for this position, [b=c_i] is either b or NOT b, and the claimed gate bound follows.
derivation: Use one live-candidate bit per listed function. The prefix-agreement invariant is initialized trivially and preserved because agreement on the extended prefix is old agreement conjoined with matching the next fixed candidate bit. Hardwire each candidate's value at the current position; update each state bit with one AND.
scope: Every finite explicitly listed family F of Boolean functions and every fixed ordering of its truth-table inputs. Gate cost is per position and depends on M; no bound on M and no conversion from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit is asserted.

label: S1081
statement:
statement: RESIDUAL-SEPARATION LEMMA FOR EXACT STREAMING RECOGNIZERS. Let L be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz is in L}. In any deterministic left-to-right streaming recognizer that accepts exactly L, prefixes p and q of the same length that reach the same state have R_p=R_q. Consequently, distinct residuals at level t require distinct states, so the recognizer needs at least as many level-t states as there are distinct residuals. Proof: If p and q reach the same state, then for every suffix z the deterministic computation from that state on z is identical. Exact recognition therefore gives pz in L iff qz in L for every z of length N-t. By the definition of residual, this is R_p=R_q. The state-count conclusion follows by contraposition.
derivation: Compare the recognizer's future behavior from two prefixes that reach the same state. Determinism makes acceptance identical on every common suffix; exactness makes this equality equivalent to equality of their suffix residual sets.
scope: Every finite binary language L of fixed word length N and every deterministic exact left-to-right streaming recognizer. Applied to L=Im(Eval_{n,s}), it lower-bounds states by the number of distinct EXT residuals at each level. It asserts no transition-circuit gate lower bound and no connection from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.

structure.evidence: Direct proof by deterministic continuation: equal states induce identical acceptance on every suffix, hence equal residuals. No finite experiment is needed for this general lemma.

statement:
statement: Let f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}. If every cut matrix M_t^π of f has rank at most 1 over a field K, for a fixed variable order π, then every cut has at most two distinct residual functions, and the ordered decision diagram under π has width at most 2.
proof: At a cut, the rows of M are the residual truth tables. Rank zero means every row is zero, so there is one distinct residual. If rank is one, choose a nonzero row u. Every row is λu for some λ∈K. Since rows and u are Boolean and u has a coordinate equal to 1, inspecting that coordinate shows λ∈{0,1}. Thus there are at most two distinct rows. The number of distinct residual functions is exactly the width of the reduced layered OBDD at that cut. Applying this at every cut proves the width bound.
scope: Finite Boolean functions, one fixed variable order, with all cut-matrix ranks at most one over the same field K.

statement: Counting lemma: for a basis of g binary ops, |Im_{n,s}| <= (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s. Hence for (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s < 2^N a random y in {0,1}^N avoids Im_{n,s} with probability >= 1 - (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s/2^N. Proof: a circuit with k gates is a sequence of k triples (op,i,j) with g*(n+s)^2 choices each; sum over k<=s.

label: S0010
statement:
statement: Randomized restricted range avoidance. Fix n>=1, N=2^n, and the fan-in-two Boolean circuit model on n named inputs with one output and at most s gates over {AND, OR, NOT}, with constants allowed if included in the encoding. Let K be the number of valid encoded circuits. If K <= N^a for a fixed constant a and K/2^N <= 1/2, there is a uniform Las Vegas algorithm that outputs a truth table outside the size-s circuit image, with expected running time O(N(K+1)) circuit-table operations and O(N) bits of candidate storage, plus the space needed to enumerate one circuit. Proof: independently sample a uniformly random y in {0,1}^N; enumerate all valid circuits, evaluate each on the N input assignments, and reject y if any output table equals y. If rejected, resample. Each trial accepts exactly when y is outside the image. At most K tables are in the image, so acceptance probability is at least 1-K/2^N >= 1/2. The expected number of trials is at most 2. Each trial evaluates at most K circuits on N inputs and compares their tables to y, costing O(N(K+1)) Boolean operations. Accepted y is outside the image by the exhaustive membership check. Under the standard gate-description bound K <= 2^{O((s+1)log(n+s+2))}, this gives polynomial-in-N expected time whenever s log(n+s+2)=O(n), subject to the stated encoding bound.
evidence: Complete sampling-and-verification proof supplied here. The result is randomized and only covers circuit counts K polynomial in N; it does not satisfy the deterministic polylogtime-uniform AC0 refuter hypothesis of CJSW Prop. 4.3 and does not close G0001.

label: S0013
statement: Corrected image-counting bound. Fix n>=1, s>=0, g>=1. Consider ordered fan-in-two circuits with n named input wires, constants 0 and 1, at most s gates, each gate chosen from g binary operations and taking its two operands from the input, constant, and earlier-gate wires; the output is any such wire. Put W=n+s+2. There are at most W choices for the output wire. For each k<=s, there are at most (g W^2)^k ordered gate lists. Therefore the total number of descriptions, and thus distinct Boolean functions on the n inputs, is at most W sum_{k=0}^s (g W^2)^k <= (s+1)W(g W^2)^s. Proof: for any fixed k, each of its k gates has at most g choices of operation and W choices for each operand, since n+k+2<=W; after the gate list is fixed there are at most W output choices. Summing over k gives the first bound. Since gW^2>=1, each of the s+1 summands is at most (gW^2)^s, giving the second bound. This repairs the omitted output-wire factor for this explicit encoding; it does not imply polynomial-time range avoidance at the CJSW threshold, so G0001 remains open.

label: S0014
statement: Output-sensitive deterministic range avoidance. Let N>=1 and let L=(z_1,...,z_K) be an explicitly enumerable list of strings in {0,1}^N, with repetitions allowed and K<2^N. There is a deterministic procedure that outputs y outside the set of strings appearing in L using at most NK inspections of list bits, O(N+log(K+1)) working bits beyond the list enumerator, and N sequential scans of L. Proof: start with the empty prefix p, matched by q_0=K list entries. At stage i (1<=i<=N), scan L and count the entries whose first i-1 bits equal p and whose i-th bit is 0 or 1. These counts sum to the number q of entries matching p. Extend p by a bit whose count is at most q/2, breaking ties toward 0. Inductively, after i stages at most K/2^i entries match p. After N stages the matching count is an integer less than 1, hence zero; the resulting y=p is absent from L. Each of N scans reads at most K strings of N bits, so at most NK list-bit inspections suffice. Storing p and counters takes O(N+log(K+1)) bits beyond the enumerator's own state. For a circuit-image list this proves a deterministic construction conditional on a complete enumerator, with total time including N full scans; it gives no polynomial-in-N bound when that list is too large.

statement: PROOF. Put lo = sum_{i in F} min(w_i,0), hi = sum_{i in F} max(w_i,0). Restricted g is constant 1 iff V+lo >= t, constant 0 iff V+hi < t, where V = sum_{i not in F} w_i b_i. So g is non-constant iff V lies in [t-hi, t-lo), a set of hi-lo = W_F consecutive integers. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord: for integers |c_i|>=1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(N,floor(N/2)) of the 2^N sums of subsets of {c_i}. Apply it to 2V - sum w_i = sum w_i eps_i with eps_i = 2b_i - 1 (nonzero coefficients only; zero weights contribute constants) to get max_x Pr[V=x] <= C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N. Union over the W_F integer values gives the first inequality; C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives the second. For N=0 the bound is W_F and is trivially valid. CORROLLARY: E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_i |w_i| <= kKs/n. Since N >= s-k deterministically: if s >= 2k, 1/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt(2/s), so the bound is <= sqrt(2) kK sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n). If s < 2k, use the bound with c <= 1: kKs/n <= 2k^2K/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n) since k^2 <= n/2. Summing over gates gives the stated count.

Union over the W_F integer values gives the first inequality; C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives the second. For N=0 the bound is W_F and is trivially valid. CORROLLARY: E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_i |w_i| <= kKs/n. Since N >= s-k deterministically: if s >= 2k, 1/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt(2/s), so the bound is <= sqrt(2) kK sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n). If s < 2k, use the bound with c <= 1: kKs/n <= 2k^2K/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n) since k^2 <= n/2. Summing over gates gives the stated count.

label: S0017
statement: LEMMA (kind LEMMA, repair attempt for G0013; not claimed to close G0001). Setup: w_1..w_m in Z^n, thresholds t_1..t_m, a set F of k free coordinates, complement R with |R| = n-k, and a fixed assignment b in {0,1}^R. Restricted gate g_j|_b(y) = [sum_{i in F} w_ji y_i >= t_j - S_j(b)], S_j(b) = sum_{q in R} w_jq b_q, for y in {0,1}^F. Claim: the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among {g_j|_b : j <= m} is at most sum_{i=0}^{k+1} C(2^k, i) <= (2^k+1)^{k+1} <= 2^{(k+1)^2}, independent of m and n. PROOF: Each g_j|_b is the trace on the cube {0,1}^F of the halfspace H_j = {y in R^k : a_j . y >= theta_j} with a_j = (w_ji)_{i in F}, theta_j = t_j - S_j(b). Halfspaces in R^k have VC dimension k+1. Sauer-Shelah applied to the family of traces on the 2^k-point cube gives at most sum_{i<=k+1} C(2^k,i) distinct traces. Distinct functions are distinct traces, so the bound follows. QED. Exact finite check cm-36040ff49f6d41f0 (k <= 3) gives threshold counts 4, 14, 104 matching the known counts, with 0 violations. SCOPE: a bound on the number of distinct restricted gate TYPES per fixed restriction. It is a compression of m objects into D_k types only when D_k << m, i.e. k^2 << log2 m. At k of order sqrt(n) (the regime of G0001), D_k is about 2^n, which exceeds m. It does not bound the surviving count itself and does not give a joint description of the m gates across all restrictions b.

structure.lemma: SURVIVOR COMPRESSION (bounded weights, R0837). Let w_1..w_m in Z^n with |w_{j,i}| <= K, thresholds T_j, a k-set F, and a fixing b in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i not in F} w_{j,i} b_i] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct NON-CONSTANT functions among all g_{j,b} is at most D_k = 2Kk(2K+1)^k. PROOF: for fixed u in [-K,K]^F the values u.x (x in {0,1}^F) lie in an integer interval of length 2Kk, so at most 2Kk+1 distinct values; a non-constant table x -> [u.x >= tau] is determined by the cut among the distinct values, so at most 2Kk non-constant tables per u; the restricted weight vectors lie in [-K,K]^F, so at most (2K+1)^k choices of u; union bound. Consequence: the restricted top sum equals const + sum over at most D_k fixed tables of coefficient * table (exact identity).
